docs.title: C.2 Adapter SPI (normative)
docs.text:
# agentcanvas/core/spi/adapter.py
from typing import Protocol, Literal, AsyncIterator, Any
from agentcanvas.core.ir import ExecutionPlan, NodeTypeManifest, Diagnostic
from agentcanvas.core.events import CanonicalEvent
from agentcanvas.core.hitl import ResumeEnvelope, InterruptDecision

SupportLevel = Literal["native", "emulated", "unsupported"]

class AdapterManifest(BaseModel):
    id: str                          # "google_adk"
    version: str                     # adapter semver
    framework: str                   # "google-adk"
    framework_range: str             # ">=2.10,<2.12"  (stack pin)
    languages: list[Literal["python", "typescript", "java", "go", "dotnet"]]
    hosting_modes: list[Literal["agent_server", "native", "a2a_remote", "mcp_remote"]]
    tier: Literal["T1", "T2", "T3", "community"]
    licence: str

class CapabilityMatrix(BaseModel):
    concepts: dict[str, "CapabilityEntry"]   # key = core concept id, e.g. "hitl.tool_approval"

class CapabilityEntry(BaseModel):
    level: SupportLevel
    native_api: str | None = None            # e.g. "google.adk.tools.FunctionTool(require_confirmation=...)"
    emulation: str | None = None             # description of emulation mechanism
    caveats: list[str] = []
    since_framework: str | None = None

class FrameworkAdapter(Protocol):
    manifest: AdapterManifest
    capabilities: CapabilityMatrix

    # authoring
    def node_library(self) -> list[NodeTypeManifest]: ...
    def validate(self, plan: ExecutionPlan) -> list[Diagnostic]: ...
    # compilation
    def lower(self, plan: ExecutionPlan) -> "AdapterPlan": ...
    def generate(self, aplan: "AdapterPlan", target: "Target") -> "BuildArtifact": ...
    # execution
    async def start(self, aplan: "AdapterPlan", run: "RunRequest") -> "RunHandle": ...
    async def resume(self, handle_ref: "RunRef", envelope: ResumeEnvelope,
                     decisions: list[InterruptDecision]) -> "RunHandle": ...
    def events(self, handle: "RunHandle") -> AsyncIterator[CanonicalEvent]: ...
    async def cancel(self, handle: "RunHandle", graceful: bool = True) -> None: ...
    # state
    def serialize_state(self, handle: "RunHandle") -> ResumeEnvelope: ...
    def persistence_mapping(self) -> "PersistenceMapping": ...
    # hosting & packaging
    def host_wrapper(self, aplan: "AdapterPlan", mode: str) -> "HostArtifact": ...
    # optional
    def importer(self) -> "Importer | None": ...
    def conformance_profile(self) -> "ConformanceProfile": ...

Contracts: - lower() must be pure and deterministic; generate() byte-deterministic (TR-COMP-01 applies to every adapter). - events() must emit the mandatory canonical events (C.3) with canvas_node_id on node/tool/interrupt events. - serialize_state() must produce a ResumeEnvelope that can resume the run in a different process (required for Agent Server hosting and horizontal scaling). - Every emulated capability must be covered by a conformance case (C.8).

docs.title: C.3 Canonical Run Event protocol (AG-UI based)
docs.text:
We adopt AG-UI events as the wire base and add a small, namespaced extension set for canvas semantics. Framework translators can therefore reuse AG-UI integrations and only add the extension events.

Canonical event AG-UI base Extension payload (AgentCanvas) Mandatory Run started / finished / error RUN_STARTED, RUN_FINISHED, RUN_ERROR workflow_id, version, adapter, thread_id; RUN_FINISHED outcome success/interrupt ✅ Node started / finished STEP_STARTED, STEP_FINISHED canvas_node_id, ns (nesting path), attempt, duration_ms, status (ok/error/timeout/bypassed/cached) ✅ Token stream TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END canvas_node_id ✅ Reasoning stream REASONING_* canvas_node_id optional Tool call TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/END/RESULT canvas_node_id, tool_source (function/mcp/hosted/agent) ✅ State STATE_SNAPSHOT, STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) channel names mapped to IR state ✅ (snapshot at node end at minimum) Messages MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT — optional Interrupt RUN_FINISHED (interrupt outcome) + CUSTOM name="ac.interrupt" InterruptRequest (C.4) ✅ Handoff / delegation CUSTOM name="ac.handoff" / "ac.delegate" from_agent, to_agent, canvas_node_id ✅ where concept supported Checkpoint CUSTOM name="ac.checkpoint" checkpoint_id, step T1 only Usage/cost CUSTOM name="ac.usage" tokens in/out, model, cost ✅ Framework-native RAW original event (debug view only) optional

Translators live in each adapter (adapter.events()), wrapping the existing AG-UI integration where one exists (ADK adk-middleware, microsoft-agent-framework, crew-ai, pydantic-ai, llama-index, aws-strands, mastra, claude-agent-sdk) and adding node mapping via source-map metadata. OpenAI Agents SDK needs a native translator (RawResponsesStreamEvent, RunItemStreamEvent, AgentUpdatedStreamEvent + RunHooks).

Traces: in parallel, adapters ensure OTel GenAI semantic-convention spans (ADK, MAF, Strands, Pydantic AI emit these natively; OpenAI via a TracingProcessor exporting to OTel; CrewAI via its telemetry/listeners) → OTel collector → LangSmith (or customer backend). Span attribute agentcanvas.node_id is injected by generated code.

docs.title: C.4 Canonical HITL protocol
docs.text:
class InterruptRequest(BaseModel):
    id: str                                   # stable per pending interrupt
    kind: Literal["tool_approval", "input", "elicitation", "file_permission", "remote_input"]
    canvas_node_id: str
    tool: ToolCallInfo | None = None          # name, args, call_id, source
    prompt: str | None = None                 # question / message
    response_schema: dict | None = None       # JSON Schema of expected answer
    allowed_decisions: list[Literal["approve", "edit", "reject", "respond"]] = ["approve", "reject"]
    native_ref: dict                          # adapter-specific handle (never interpreted by core)

class InterruptDecision(BaseModel):
    interrupt_id: str
    type: Literal["approve", "edit", "reject", "respond"]
    edited_args: dict | None = None
    message: str | None = None
    value: Any = None

class ResumeEnvelope(BaseModel):
    adapter: str; adapter_version: str; framework_version: str
    native_state: bytes | dict                # e.g. OpenAI RunState.to_json(), MAF checkpoint id, ADK session/event ids
    pending: list[InterruptRequest]
    state_snapshot: dict                      # canonical IR state view for the canvas

Native mappings (verified):

Adapter Raise Resume LangChain interrupt() / HumanInTheLoopMiddleware Command(resume={"decisions": [...]}) OpenAI Agents needs_approval → result.interruptions (ToolApprovalItem) state = result.to_state() (or RunState.from_json) → state.approve(item) / state.reject(item, rejection_message=…) → Runner.run(agent, state); edit = reject with message + adapter-injected corrected call (documented emulation) Google ADK FunctionTool(require_confirmation=…); workflow node yields RequestInput(message=…) send confirmation / user response event into the same session; Workflow(rerun_on_resume=True) MAF @tool(approval_mode="always_require"); executor ctx.request_info(data, response_type) send responses to pending request_info ids; restore from CheckpointStorage if cross-process CrewAI Flow @human_feedback(...); task human_input=True feedback provider returns outcome → emit route; persisted flow state via @persist Pydantic AI tool raises ApprovalRequired / CallDeferred → DeferredToolRequests agent.run(..., message_history=…, deferred_tool_results=DeferredToolResults(...)) LlamaIndex WF ctx.write_event_to_stream(InputRequiredEvent(...)) ctx.send_event(HumanResponseEvent(...)) Strands hook/tool raises interrupt → agent returns interrupts re-invoke agent with interrupt responses Mastra step suspend(payload) run.resume({ step, resumeData }) Claude Agent SDK can_use_tool callback (async) callback awaits platform decision (in-process wait with timeout) — T3 A2A remote task state input-required / auth-required send follow-up message on same task

docs.title: C.5 State, persistence & memory mapping
docs.text: Concern Rule Thread identity Canvas thread_id ↔ framework conversation handle: LangGraph thread_id; OpenAI Session(session_id); ADK session_id (+user_id, app_name); MAF AgentSession / workflow checkpoint lineage; CrewAI flow id (persisted); Pydantic AI message-history key; Strands session id; Mastra run id. Hosting mode A (Agent Server) The @entrypoint stores the ResumeEnvelope in entrypoint.final(save=…); conversation history is kept either in the framework's session backend (bound per environment to Postgres/Redis/Mongo via doc 08 bindings) or inside the envelope for small runs. Persistence bindings (doc 08) Each adapter maps logical bindings to its native backends: OpenAI SQLAlchemySession/RedisSession/MongoDBSession; ADK DatabaseSessionService (SQLAlchemy URL) / VertexAiSessionService; MAF HistoryProvider (Redis/Cosmos) + CheckpointStorage (custom Postgres implementation shipped by us); CrewAI FlowPersistence (SQLite default; Postgres implementation shipped by us); Mastra stores (@mastra/pg, @mastra/redis, …). Shared IR state Adapters expose IR channels via a state bridge: ADK ctx.state, CrewAI flow state model, MAF shared state, LlamaIndex Context store, Mastra workflow state; reducers not native anywhere except LangGraph are emulated by generated merge functions (E in matrix). Long-term memory Platform Memory Spaces are reachable by every adapter through generated memory tools + agentcanvas_runtime.memory client; native memory services (ADK MemoryService, MAF context providers, CrewAI memory) can be selected as dialect bindings. Data Studio Generated repositories/tools (doc 08 §5) are framework-neutral Python; each adapter wraps them in its tool type.

docs.title: C.6 Tool & model bridges
docs.text:
• Single tool definition (ToolSpec: name, description, JSON Schema args, implementation ref, approval policy, read-only/destructive hints) → per-adapter tool factory: langchain.tools.tool, agents.function_tool, google.adk.tools.FunctionTool, agent_framework.tool, crewai.tools.BaseTool, Pydantic AI Tool, Strands @tool, Mastra createTool (sidecar).
  • MCP: tools from MCP servers are attached natively where supported (all T1/T2 frameworks verified above); the project MCP gateway (doc 11 A7) exposes platform tools uniformly.
  • Models: ModelSpec(provider, model, params, gateway) → per-adapter model object; via the model gateway (LangSmith LLM Gateway or OpenAI-compatible proxy) when the framework cannot reach a provider natively (e.g. Claude models in OpenAI Agents SDK via LiteLLM extension or gateway).
  • Capability-aware validation: e.g. P001 if a Claude Agent SDK node is given a non-Claude model; P002 if structured output is emulated.

docs.title: C.7 Hosting wrappers
docs.text:
Mode A — Agent Server host (Python adapters). Generated host.py:

from langgraph.func import entrypoint, task
from langgraph.types import interrupt
from agentcanvas_runtime.hosting import envelope_codec, emit_canonical

@task
async def run_native(inp: dict, envelope: dict | None, decisions: list | None) -> dict:
    return await ADAPTER.start_or_resume(PLAN, inp, envelope, decisions)   # returns {"output"?, "pending"?, "envelope"}

@entrypoint()
async def agent(inp: dict, *, previous: dict | None = None):
    res = await run_native(inp, (previous or {}).get("envelope"), None)
    while res.get("pending"):
        decisions = interrupt({"interrupts": res["pending"]})             # surfaces in AgentCanvas Inbox / Agent Server
        res = await run_native(inp, res["envelope"], decisions)
    return entrypoint.final(value=res["output"], save={"envelope": res["envelope"]})
(ADK may alternatively use deployments-wrap-sdk's wrap(Runner(...)) + LangsmithSessionService.) Canonical events are forwarded through the custom stream mode.

Mode B — native hosting. Deploy service targets: ADK adk deploy agent_engine|cloud_run|gke|docker; MAF Foundry hosted agents / hosting-* packages; CrewAI AMP; LlamaIndex llama-agents server/control plane. Event translator attaches as a sidecar/plugin (ADK plugin, MAF middleware, CrewAI event listener) posting canonical events to our ingest endpoint; HITL resolved through the framework's native resume API.

Mode C — remote. A2A 1.0 client node (task streaming; input-required → interrupt) and MCP client node.

TypeScript adapters. sidecars/node-adapter-host implements the SPI over JSON-RPC (lower/generate/start/resume/events) so the Python control plane can drive Mastra/OpenAI-JS/ADK-TS; hosted in its own container per deployment with the same canonical event contract.

docs.title: C.8 Conformance suite (normative)
docs.text:
Shared cases in agentcanvas/core/conformance, run with fake models (scripted responses per framework's model interface) and tool cassettes. Each adapter declares which cases apply (by capability level).

Suite Cases (examples) Pass criteria C-AGENT single tool call; parallel tool calls; structured output; MCP tool; model error + retry same tool sequence & final output as reference C-FLOW sequence; router (3 routes); parallel + join; map over 5 items; bounded loop; nested subgraph same node visit multiset & final state (order-insensitive where parallel) C-HITL approve; edit; reject with message; input form; interrupt inside subgraph/sub-agent; resume in a new process from envelope identical post-resume trajectory C-STATE channel writes, emulated reducers (append, merge), state snapshot events canonical state equal C-PERSIST thread continuation across 3 turns; session backend bound to Postgres & Redis history preserved C-EVENTS mandatory canonical events emitted with canvas_node_id; token streaming order schema-valid, complete C-CODEGEN ruff/pyright clean (or eslint/tsc), byte-deterministic, runs with framework CLI (adk run, etc.) pass C-HOST Mode A wrapper passes C-HITL & C-PERSIST on Agent Server (langgraph dev) pass

Portable templates (Router, Support triage, Research-lite, Approval workflow, Map-reduce summariser) must produce equivalent outcomes on every T1 adapter — this is the "same canvas, any framework" guarantee.

docs.title: C.9 Certification tiers (refined)
docs.text: Tier Requirements T1 Direct lowering path; C-AGENT, C-FLOW (all), C-HITL (all incl. cross-process), C-STATE, C-PERSIST, C-EVENTS, C-CODEGEN, C-HOST green; dev-run debugging (live overlay, breakpoints via interrupts or step hooks); importer for its own code or declarative spec (ADK YAML, MAF declarative, CrewAI FlowDefinition, Pydantic AI Agent Spec); nightly upstream CI; documented emulations T2 Direct or bridge path; C-AGENT, C-FLOW (supported subset), C-HITL (approve/reject), C-EVENTS, C-CODEGEN; no breakpoints required T3 Wrapped node; C-AGENT basic, C-EVENTS (run + text + tool), HITL where native callback exists

docs.title: C.10 Stack & version management
docs.text:
• Each adapter pins a framework range per AgentCanvas stack (e.g. stack-2026.10: openai-agents>=0.22,<0.23, google-adk>=2.10,<2.11, agent-framework>=1.19,<1.20, crewai>=1.15,<1.16, pydantic-ai>=2.51,<2.52).
  • Nightly upstream CI runs conformance against the framework's latest release and main; failures open issues and block stack promotion.
  • Pre-1.0 frameworks (OpenAI Agents 0.x, Claude Agent SDK 0.x) get patch-level pins and a dedicated breaking-change watcher.
  • MAF sub-packages in b/a pre-release (e.g. hosting-mcp alpha, purview beta) are not used by T1 features unless flagged experimental.

docs.title: C.11 UI/UX specification for multi-framework
docs.text: Element Behaviour New workflow dialog Choose framework (LangChain default; others shown with tier badge); "Portable" toggle restricts palette to core nodes Palette Core nodes + active framework's dialect nodes; foreign-framework nodes greyed with reason Portability bar "Compiles on: LangChain ✓ · ADK ✓ · OpenAI ⚠ (2 emulated) · CrewAI ✗ (1 blocker)" → click for per-node table Switch framework Re-target wizard: shows blockers/emulations, proposes dialect-node replacements (e.g. langchain.deep_agent → adk.llm_agent + planner) Code view Shows generated code for the selected framework; side-by-side compare across frameworks Compare experiment Run the same dataset on N frameworks/models; results grid (quality, latency, cost, tokens) Node inspector "Implemented as: google.adk.workflow.JoinNode" + capability level + caveats

docs.title: C.12 Security considerations per adapter
docs.text:
• Framework code executes only in data-plane workers/sandboxes (doc 02); adapters run in the compiler workers only for lowering/generation, never executing user code.
  • Framework-specific powerful tools (OpenAI ShellTool/ApplyPatchTool, sandbox agents; ADK code executors; MAF Hyperlight; Claude Agent SDK Bash/Edit tools) are admin-gated dialect nodes, default needs_approval/permission_mode restrictive, and must run with a sandbox binding.
  • Licence gate: adapters record framework licence; Mastra ee/ components excluded from generated code.

docs.title: 13 — Deep Review Report (v0.4 → v0.5)
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-28 · Scope: docs 00–12, adapters/, and all code shown in them · Goal: make the specification buildable by a beginner, without prior context.

docs.title: 1. How the review was done
docs.text:
1. Every API name used in the spec was imported from the real packages (installed: langgraph 1.2.12, langchain 1.4.2, langchain-core 1.6.5, deepagents 0.7.19, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.2, langgraph-checkpoint-redis 0.5.2, fastapi 0.141, cel-python 0.5.0).
  2. The worked example's behaviour was executed: graph with retry/timeout policies, router, agent with tool approval, pause → resume, state history, time-travel fork, state edit, Postgres checkpointer & store, Deep Agent with a composite backend, streaming (v2 and v3), custom stream events.
  3. A walking-skeleton implementation was built and tested (build-guide/reference/): IR models, validator, safe expressions, runtime node library, interpreter, code generator, FastAPI runner with SSE, React Flow UI. Verified with 20 backend tests (incl. security tests), 2 frontend tests, ruff + pyright (0 errors), a clean-room install from lockfiles, and a headless-browser end-to-end test (run → nodes light up → approve → complete, twice).
  4. Each document was read for contradictions, undecided choices, scope that a small team cannot deliver, and missing information a newcomer would need.

Generated code exposes build_graph(resources, checkpointer, store); hosts decide how to call it. The LangSmith-deploy target wraps it in a module-level graph (build guide §09).

docs.title: 3.2 Runtime pitfalls (now documented in build-guide/11-troubleshooting-faq.md)
docs.text: ID Pitfall (verified) Handling P-01 LangChain fake chat models do not implement bind_tools() → agents fail with NotImplementedError. agentcanvas.testing.ToolFakeModel. P-02 With stream_mode="messages", a fake model reply that contains only tool calls yields no chunks → ValueError: No generations found in stream. Fakes use disable_streaming=True. P-03 Scripted fakes are stateful; a resume that builds a fresh fake restarts the script and re-issues the tool call (endless approvals). Resources are resolved per thread (resources_factory(thread_id)). P-04 langgraph-checkpoint-redis needs Redis with RediSearch + RedisJSON (Redis 8, or Redis Stack). Plain Redis 7 fails with unknown command 'FT.INFO'. Docker Compose uses redis:8; binding validation checks modules (MODULE LIST) before use. P-05 stream_events(version="v3") exists but warns "experimental" at runtime. MVP uses astream(..., version="v2") (stable, typed parts). v3 adoption tracked for later. P-06 When resuming after interrupt(), LangGraph re-runs the interrupted node from its start. Code before interrupt() runs twice. Validator rule E070 + guidance: side effects go after the approval, in a separate node.

docs.title: 3.2b Security gap found in the reference during review
docs.text: ID Problem Resolution SEC-01 Script nodes and Python tools imported any module:function from import_path (e.g. os:system). safe_import() allow-lists workspace packages (scripts., tools., examples.); validator rule E080; tests in tests/test_security.py (also proving the template/CEL sandboxes block __class__/__globals__ escapes).

docs.title: 3.3 Contradictions
docs.text: ID Contradiction Resolution C-01 02 §6 says graph node names are slug__nodeid; 03 §5 says identifier = slug(name). Node name = IR name (unique snake_case). The runtime keeps a name → canvas_node_id index; metadata={"canvas_node_id": …} is also set for traces. C-02 02 §6 defines its own UI event schema; 12 §C.3 defines AG-UI-based canonical events. 12 §C.3 is authoritative. 02 §6 now points to it. The reference translator emits RUN_STARTED/FINISHED/ERROR, STEP_STARTED/FINISHED, TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT, STATE_DELTA, CUSTOM ac.interrupt. C-03 03 §7: generated code "inlined idiomatic code by default" vs. "calls the runtime library" — two strategies, equivalence unclear. MVP: generated code calls the same node library the interpreter uses (agentcanvas.runtime.nodes) and assembles the graph with plain LangGraph calls. Equivalence is tested (test_generated_code_matches_interpreter). A fully-inlined "clean eject" is a P2 option. C-04 Control-DB tables defined in 02 §7 and 08 §7 (duplicates). Single authoritative DDL: build-guide/05-backend-guide.md §3. C-05 D6 "LangGraph Agent Server is the runtime" vs. licensing open question in 06 §4.1. See D-01: the MVP ships its own open-source runner; Agent Server/LangSmith Deployment is a publish target. C-06 02 lists "Temporal (or Hatchet)" as "Arq/Celery-free" (confusing). MVP: no workflow engine; background work uses asyncio tasks + a Postgres job table. Temporal introduced at GA for long jobs (evals, deploys). C-07 Doc 06 roadmap has MVP including Yjs multiplayer (P1) in some tables and not others. Multiplayer (Yjs) is post-MVP. MVP uses REST autosave with optimistic locking (version column, HTTP 409 on conflict).

docs.title: 3.4 Undecided choices → decisions (recorded as ADRs in build-guide/02 §6)
docs.text: ID Question Decision D-01 Runtime for MVP AgentCanvas Runner: FastAPI + LangGraph library + Postgres checkpointer/store + SSE, implementing a subset of the Agent Server API shape (threads, runs/stream, state, history). Fully open source. LangSmith Deployment = optional publish target. D-02 Expression language CEL (cel-python) for conditions; sandboxed Jinja2 (jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, StrictUndefined) for templates. Never eval. D-03 Canvas library React Flow (@xyflow/react 12). D-04 Frontend stack React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, TanStack Query, @rjsf/core for config forms, Monaco for code. D-05 Streaming transport SSE over POST (fetch + stream reader) for runs; WebSocket only later for collaboration. D-06 Database migrations Alembic (SQLAlchemy 2.0 models). D-07 Auth in MVP OIDC login via any provider (Keycloak in docker-compose for local), JWT verified by the API; single organisation; roles admin, builder, viewer. D-08 IDs Prefixed ULIDs: wf_, n_, r_, e_, th_, run_, ver_. D-09 API error format RFC 9457 application/problem+json. D-10 Script execution in MVP Scripts run in-process only in the local/dev edition; the hosted edition runs them in a Docker sandbox runner (gVisor where available). D-11 Python/Node versions Python 3.12, Node 22 LTS, pnpm 10, uv for Python packaging.

docs.title: 3.5 Scope and sequencing
docs.text: ID Problem Resolution S-01 "MVP" in 06 contained ~40 features — too large for a first release by a small or junior team. New milestone plan M0–M8 (build-guide/04) with a walking skeleton first and each milestone shippable. S-02 Framework-agnostic groundwork (doc 11 §4) not mapped to tickets. Mapped into M1/M3/M5 tickets (IR core/dialect split, canonical events, adapter boundary). S-03 No requirement → ticket traceability. build-guide/12-traceability.md maps every P0 requirement to tickets. S-04 Persistence (doc 08) and learning (doc 09) scope mixed with MVP. MVP persistence = Postgres checkpointer + store + thread browser; Redis/Mongo bindings, RoutedStore, Data Studio → post-MVP milestones.

docs.title: 3.6 Beginner gaps (all addressed by the new build guide)
docs.text: Missing before this revision: concept primer; environment setup with exact versions; local infrastructure (Docker Compose); repository layout for the real product; coding conventions; git/PR workflow; step-by-step tutorial; ticket-level plan with acceptance criteria; full DDL; API contract examples; frontend architecture; "how to add a node type" recipe; testing strategy with fakes; deployment runbook; security checklist; troubleshooting FAQ.

docs.title: 4. Remaining known limitations (explicitly accepted)
docs.text:
• The reference implementation covers 6 node types; the full catalog (doc 04) is built incrementally per the milestone plan.
  • Non-LangChain adapters (doc 12) are not in the reference implementation; they start after GA as planned.
  • Model identifiers in examples (e.g. openai:gpt-5-mini, anthropic:claude-sonnet-5) are illustrative; the model catalog is data-driven and validated against the provider at connection time.

docs.title: 14 — Deep Review Report (v0.5 → v0.6)
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-29 · Scope: docs 00–13, adapters/, build-guide/ and the reference implementation · Goal: re-verify every claim against the current LangChain ecosystem, close the gaps a real build exposes, and deepen the product concept (doc 15) before sprint execution starts (build-guide/13).

  1. Official documentation re-read at source: langchain-ai/docs at commit 1a30368 (2026-09-28): LangGraph (event streaming, fault tolerance, persistence, Pregel/DeltaChannel, functional API), LangChain (agents, middleware, MCP, frontend patterns), Deep Agents (backends, subagents, dynamic subagents, interpreters, rubric, profiles, ACP/A2A/AG-UI, multimodal), LangSmith (Agent Server, graph rebuild/ServerRuntime, event streaming API, sandboxes + auth proxy, Engine, decision models, LLM Gateway, Fleet, Managed Deep Agents).

  3. The reference implementation's 20 tests were re-run in a clean uv sync: all pass. Its design was then read against the new findings.

docs.title: 2. Summary
docs.text: Category Found Resolution Factual / version errors 4 fixed in docs (V-01, V-02, V-09, §4 C-08) New runtime pitfalls (verified by execution) 4 documented + handled in the product code (V-03, V-04, V-06, V-10) Newly-verified capabilities that change a decision 2 ADRs 0013/0014 (V-05, V-08) Upstream features the spec did not use 27 mapped to requirements in doc 15 (V-07) Security gaps 3 new validator rules E041, E042, W074 (V-11) Contradictions / process issues 5 §4

docs.title: 3.1 Verified errors and pitfalls
docs.text: ID Finding (verified) Impact Resolution V-01 from langchain.mcp import MCPAdapter fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fastmcp unless LangChain is installed with the mcp extra (langchain[mcp], pulls fastmcp>=4,<5). The namespace is beta and emits LangChainBetaWarning. MCPAdapter(target) accepts an http(s) URL string, a Path (spawns a local stdio subprocess), an MCPConfig dict ({"mcpServers": …}), a FastMCP server/client or a transport. MCP node unusable in a default install; stdio targets are a code-execution vector. Stack pins langchain[mcp]; the runtime filters the beta warning once and records it in diagnostics (I010 beta API in use). Stdio/Path targets are admin-gated (new rule E042) and only run inside a sandbox in the hosted edition. V-02 CodeInterpreterMiddleware is exported by langchain_quickjs and requires langchain-quickjs>=0.3.7 via deepagents[quickjs]; doc 03 §6.4 said >=0.2. It is still experimental. Wrong pin → resolver conflict. Doc 03 corrected; interpreter capability marked experimental in the node manifest. V-03 Per-node timeouts only work on async nodes. add_node(sync_fn, timeout=…) raises ValueError: Node timeouts are only supported for async nodes…. The reference node library returns sync callables for approval, set, router and script nodes. Setting a timeout policy on those nodes crashes graph build. All node-library builders return async callables. Sync user functions (scripts) are wrapped with await asyncio.to_thread(fn, state) — verified: interrupt(), get_config() and get_store() keep working because to_thread copies the context. V-04 v3 event streaming (astream_events(version="v3")) still warns "The v3 streaming protocol on Pregel is experimental" in 1.2.12; in async code stream.output is a method (await run.output()), not the awaitable property shown in the docs. Agent Server event streaming is Beta and needs langgraph-api>=0.10, langgraph-sdk>=0.4. Adopting v3 now couples the UI protocol to a moving API. Keep astream(..., version="v2") (review P-05 stands). Canonical events (doc 12 §C.3) stay the contract, so switching the producer to v3 later is an adapter-internal change. Re-evaluate when the warning is removed (tracked as spike SP-3 in the sprint plan). V-06 DeltaChannel has a different reducer contract: reducer(state, [write1, write2, …]) receives batches and must be deterministic and batching-invariant. Switching a persisted channel between delta and non-delta is unsupported (existing threads become unreadable). Deep Agents ≥ 0.6 already stores messages and files as delta channels, so downgrading deepagents across 0.6 is unsafe once threads exist. FR-STATE-01 listed DeltaChannel as just another reducer; a user toggling it on a published workflow would corrupt live threads. DeltaChannel becomes a channel storage mode (storage: "delta" | "full") orthogonal to the reducer, allowed only with batch-safe built-in reducers (append, add_messages) until custom batch reducers are supported. New publish-time rule E074: changing a channel's storage mode (or removing a delta channel) while the previous version has live threads is blocking. The stack-upgrade assistant refuses deepagents downgrades across a delta boundary. V-10 Reference runner streams the graph inside the HTTP response generator; a browser disconnect cancels the run mid-step. It also keeps thread → workflow in memory, and allows the examples. import prefix everywhere. Lost runs on flaky networks; restart breaks resume; demo code importable in prod. Product runner uses the queue + background task design of build-guide/05 §5 (run survives disconnect), stores threads in the DB, and allows examples. only when AGENTCANVAS_ENV=dev.

docs.title: 3.2 Newly verified capabilities that change a decision
docs.text: ID Finding Decision V-05 Graph factories on Agent Server are now officially documented ("Rebuild graph at runtime"): a factory may be an async def make_graph(config, runtime: ServerRuntime) or an async context manager; runtime.execution_runtime distinguishes real execution from introspection (schemas, drawing); runtime.ensure_user() exposes the authenticated user. ServerRuntime is beta (langgraph-api>=0.7.31, langgraph-sdk>=0.3.5). This resolves review F-03 ("factory not verified"). ADR 0013: the LangSmith Deployment publish target may host interpreted mode — the factory loads the pinned IR from the assistant's config and calls the same build_graph the runner uses. Benefits: publish without regenerating code, per-user tool loading (MCP per-user OAuth), and identical semantics to canvas runs. Compiled export remains the portable default. V-08 langmem has had no release since 2025-10-27 while docs 09/10 build the learning ladder on "LangMem-style memory managers and prompt optimisers". ADR 0014: AgentCanvas does not take a hard dependency on langmem. Memory extraction, consolidation and prompt optimisation are implemented as AgentCanvas learning-loop workflows built from supported primitives (create_agent + structured output + BaseStore + LangSmith datasets/prompts). A langmem adapter may be offered as optional.

docs.title: 3.4 Security
docs.text: ID Gap New control V-11a LocalShellBackend executes shell commands on the host. E041 error: LocalShellBackend/FilesystemBackend in a workflow bound to a hosted environment. V-11b MCPAdapter with a Path or stdio transport spawns a subprocess on the runner host. E042 error unless the project setting allow_local_mcp is on (admin) and execution is sandboxed. docs.title: 15 — Concept Evolution: WYSIWYG for Agents, Revisited (v0.6)
docs.text:
The original brief: "A ComfyUI-like product where users create agentic workflows by dragging and dropping components. Users only use widgets, connections and scripts, but the backend creates a full-fledged agentic workflow on LangChain (Python or a better-suited language). Workspaces let users write code for custom events."

Docs 00–13 turned that into a buildable system. This document steps back and asks: what does "what you see is what you get" really have to mean for agents, where does the concept break, and what would make the product decisively better? It ends with 24 new requirements (FR-X-01…24) that are sequenced into the sprint plan.

docs.title: 1. The core idea, stated as three contracts
docs.text:
A visual builder is only trustworthy if it keeps promises that users can check. AgentCanvas makes three:

Contract Promise How it is enforced Fidelity The picture is the program. Every box is a named construct in real LangGraph/LangChain/Deep Agents code, and what runs on the canvas is what ships. IR as single source of truth (D1); shared node library for interpreter and generated code (ADR 0004); differential tests (TR-COMP-40); source maps; canvas_node_id on every node and span. Ownership You can always leave with your code. Export is clean, idiomatic, runs with open-source dependencies, and your scripts are copied verbatim. Export target is a standard LangGraph project (langgraph dev runnable); runtime helper is Apache-2.0; code islands never templated; drift detection. Evolution Changing an agent is as safe as changing code. Every change is versioned, diffable, testable, gated and reversible — including changes that agents make to themselves. Versions & visual diff; saved test cases → eval gates; resume-compatibility checks; governed learning ladder (doc 09); rollback.

Everything in this document either strengthens one of these contracts or removes friction from keeping them.

docs.title: 2. Deepening WYSIWYG: from five axes to a ladder
docs.text:
The README defines five fidelity axes (structural, behavioral, runtime, temporal, escape-hatch). Two more are needed for agents, which — unlike images — act on the world and cost money:

  1. Consequence fidelity — see what it could do before it does it. The canvas shows each workflow's blast radius: which nodes and tools can write to external systems, send messages, spend money, execute code or read sensitive data, and which of those are behind approvals. A "dry run" stubs every side-effecting tool while keeping the rest real (FR-X-02).
  2. Contract fidelity — see the outside of the workflow. A workflow is also an API (REST, MCP, A2A, AG-UI, chat widget). The canvas shows that outer contract — input/output schemas, auth, exposure surfaces — and flags breaking changes between versions (FR-X-14).

These seven axes form a WYSIWYG ladder that also serves as the product's maturity model and onboarding path:

Level The user can see… Enabled by Persona who needs it first L1 Structure the graph and its wiring canvas, typed ports, validator P1 citizen builder L2 Code the exact code each widget becomes Live Code Mirror (FR-X-01), source maps P2/P3 L3 Execution what is running now, token by token live overlay, v2 stream → canonical events all L4 History every past step, editable and forkable checkpoints, timeline, time travel P2 L5 Consequences what it can change in the world, what it costs blast-radius map, budgets, cost estimator (FR-X-02, FR-X-15) P4/P5 L6 Contract how the outside world calls it and what breaks contract view & API diff (FR-X-14) P3/P6 L7 Production how it behaves at scale and why it fails traces overlay, Engine bridge, online evals (FR-X-06) P3/P5

Design rule: a feature ships only if it makes one rung visible on the canvas, not only in a separate console.

docs.title: 3. Where the concept breaks — and the answers
docs.text: Tension Why it bites Answer in AgentCanvas Graphs vs. agents. ComfyUI graphs are DAGs; agents loop, branch on model output and spawn subagents at run time. A static picture cannot show a dynamic trajectory. Users misread a Deep Agent box as "one step". Three tiers (D3). Runtime-expanding nested canvases for subagents (ns events), trajectory overlay per run, and "Explode to graph" (FR-AGENT-09) to make an agent's loop explicit. Non-determinism. The same picture produces different runs. "It worked yesterday." Pins, mocks and cassettes (FR-RUN-07/08), saved test cases with repetitions, record/replay from production traces (FR-X-13), eval gates. Spaghetti at scale. Visual programs become unreadable around 50–100 nodes. Pros abandon the canvas. Subgraphs/components, wireless links, outline view, script nodes, Copilot refactors, and a policy that any node can be "code-backed" without leaving the canvas. Two-way sync with code. Users want to edit generated code. Round-trip editors rot. Code islands are the only editable regions; everything else is regenerated. Eject is explicit; import is best-effort with a fidelity score. We do not promise arbitrary round-tripping. Hidden prompts are hidden logic. Prompts steer behaviour more than wiring does. The picture can look correct while behaviour is wrong. Prompts are first-class resources with versions, diffs and tests; prompt changes appear in visual diffs and trigger the same gates as wiring changes. Self-modifying agents. Learning loops change prompts, memories and skills. The canvas stops being the truth. Learned artifacts are versioned IR-adjacent resources (doc 09) with provenance; the canvas shows "learned" badges and a diff of what was learned since the last human-approved version.

docs.title: 4. Language decision, revisited
docs.text:
The brief allowed "Python or any other language that might be better suited". The v0.6 evidence strengthens the original decision:

Criterion (verified 2026-09) Python TypeScript Others (Go/Java/Rust/C#) LangGraph node timeouts & error handlers ✅ (Python-only per LangGraph 1.2 changelog) ❌ ❌ no LangGraph runtime Deep Agents interpreters/PTC, rubric, permissions interrupt mode, profiles ✅ partial ❌ langchain.mcp (FastMCP-based) ✅ separate JS package community only Data work in scripts (pandas, numpy, sklearn) ✅ weak varies Browser/edge deployment, React UI, useStream, headless tools ❌ ✅ ❌

Decision (unchanged, sharpened): - Generated agent code: Python (canonical target). The IR stays language-neutral; a TypeScript target (P2) is enabled per node through the capability matrix. - Product frontend and embeddable widgets: TypeScript/React — this is where LangChain's frontend patterns (useStream, headless tools, generative UI) live. - Other languages are served through the published contract, not codegen: every workflow is REST/MCP/A2A, so Java/Go/C# systems call agents rather than host them. - Polyglot scripts run in sandboxes: JavaScript via QuickJS (pure transforms) or Node sandbox, SQL against connections — without changing the Python graph.

docs.title: 5. Positioning (as understood in September 2026 — verify before external use)
docs.text:
Product family What it does well Where AgentCanvas differs ComfyUI Node graphs for generative media, huge custom-node ecosystem Same UX DNA; AgentCanvas adds state machines, HITL, durable execution, evals, governance, and compiles to code instead of interpreting a JSON graph forever. n8n / Zapier-style automation Integrations, triggers, no-code automation AgentCanvas is agent-native (Deep Agents, subagents, memory, middleware) and emits real LangGraph code you can own. Langflow / Flowise / Dify Visual LLM app builders AgentCanvas's differentiators are the compiler contract (idiomatic, exportable, tested-equivalent code), graph-tier control over LangGraph primitives, workspaces with events-as-code, and eval-gated releases. LangSmith Fleet (formerly Agent Builder) No-code agents from templates, connections, approvals Complementary: Fleet targets individual productivity; AgentCanvas targets teams building systems with explicit graphs, code islands and CI/CD. AgentCanvas can publish to LangSmith Deployment and Managed Deep Agents. LangSmith Studio Visualize/debug LangGraph apps that already exist as code AgentCanvas is an authoring environment whose debugger works the same way; exported projects remain Studio-compatible.

Strategy: integrate with the LangChain platform rather than compete — LangSmith for traces/evals/Engine/sandboxes/gateway, Agent Server and Managed Deep Agents as publish targets — and win on authoring, composition, governance and ownership.

docs.title: 6. Workspaces and custom events, deepened: "Events as Code"
docs.text: The brief singles out "workspaces where we can do code for any custom events". Doc 05 specifies inbound events, runtime events and UI events. v0.6 unifies them into one model that is code-first but canvas-visible.

docs.title: 6.1 One event model, four handler kinds
docs.text: Handler kind Written as (workspace) Runs Typical use LangChain primitive underneath Trigger handler @on("crm.lead.created", filter=…, dedup_key=…) in events/*.py Trigger service → sandbox start a workflow, resume a thread waiting on an external event, fan out to topics runs API; Command(resume=…) for waits Lifecycle hook @on("node.failed", workflow="support_triage") Event service on canonical run events alerting, compensation, audit, chaining canonical events from the stream; Agent Server webhooks for deployed runs In-graph emitter runtime.emit("invoice.flagged", {...}) / get_stream_writer() in scripts, tools, middleware inside the run progress, custom UI, domain events for other workflows custom stream mode Stream projection (P2) class in events/transformers/*.py inside the run (v3) typed custom channels (stream.extensions.*) for UIs and SDK clients compile(transformers=[…])

docs.title: 6.2 Event catalog & schema registry
docs.text:
• Every event type (crm.lead.created, custom.invoice.flagged, node.failed, …) is declared once with a JSON Schema and version in events/schemas/; emitters and handlers are type-checked against it (validator rule E081: handler filter references a field not in the schema).
  • The Event Map view (new canvas mode) shows the whole project as a system: event sources → handlers → workflows → emitted events → downstream workflows. It is generated from code (AST scan) and IR — nothing is drawn by hand.

docs.title: 6.3 Developer loop
docs.text:
1. Write a handler in the Workspace editor (typed Event payload autocompletes from the schema).
  2. Replay a captured event (from the event log) or a sample against the handler in the sandbox; see the actions it would take (dry-run) before enabling it.
  3. Enable; delivery is at-least-once with dedup keys, retries, DLQ with replay (FR-EVT-01…08).
  4. Handler runs appear in the same run timeline as workflows, so an incident can be followed from webhook → handler → run → approval → side effect.

docs.title: 6.4 Custom widgets from code
docs.text: Custom events are one half; the other half is custom nodes (@canvas_node), custom tools, middleware, reducers, evaluators and stream transformers — all discovered from the Workspace by AST scan and appearing in the palette with a workspace provenance badge (doc 05 §3). v0.6 adds: custom nodes can declare side_effects=["external_write"] so they participate in the blast-radius map (FR-X-02) and E070 checks.

docs.title: 7.1 New diagnostics introduced by FR-X and the v0.6 review
docs.text: Code Severity Rule E041 error Host-executing backend (LocalShellBackend, FilesystemBackend) bound to a hosted environment E042 error Local/stdio MCP target without allow_local_mcp and sandboxed execution E074 error Channel storage mode changed (delta ↔ full) or delta channel removed while the previous version has live threads E081 error Event handler filter/mapping references a field missing from the event schema E090 error Budget below the static minimum for one successful path E095 error An element breaks an organisation policy (FR-X-19) E096 error An organisation policy cannot be evaluated on an element (fails closed) W074 warning Sandbox without an egress allow-list W080 warning Side-effecting node (external_write/message_send/spend) reachable without an approval or dry-run stub W081 warning Breaking change to the external contract without a major version bump W095 warning An element breaks a warning-level policy, or a policy enforced only when publishing to another environment I010 info Workflow uses an upstream beta/experimental API (listed)

docs.title: 8. What we deliberately do not do
docs.text:
• No proprietary runtime. LangGraph executes; we assemble, observe and govern (D6).
  • No arbitrary code↔canvas round-trip. Code islands plus explicit eject/import only.
  • No silent self-modification. Every learned change is a versioned, gated artifact.
  • No lowest-common-denominator multi-framework UI. Core IR + native dialects (doc 11/12); LangChain is and stays the flagship adapter.
  • No beta upstream API on the critical path without a stable fallback (see doc 14 §7).

docs.title: 16 — Competitive Roadmap (S15–S36)
docs.text:
Re-planned 2026-10-09 at the owner's request after the framework coverage review (doc 17): framework design and mixed-framework flows move ahead of Ship to users and RAG, and the owner's builder fixes become S17. §7 is the current order; §6 keeps the original scoring for reference.

Approved by the owner on 2026-10-07. This order replaces the S15–S19 plan from the Copilot plan v2 and the "S20+ GA backlog" row of the sprint plan. Live, editable copy: AgentCanvas competitive roadmap (Claude Doc).

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
After S14 (AI Copilot I, merged in #15), the next three sprints are cheap, high-value wins: make every workflow callable over MCP and A2A, add integrations through an MCP connector gallery, and let any framework's agent run as a node on the canvas. That last one gives AgentCanvas working support for every popular open-source agent framework by S16, before full per-framework authoring lands.

  • Ranking rule: each candidate gets a value score (1–5, from the market gaps in §3) and an effort in sprints; the plan runs the highest value per sprint first, with a +1 bump for multi-framework work because it is the product's core promise.
  • Multi-framework in three tiers: every framework gets Interop in S16; from S20–S22 (re-plan of 2026-10-09) the canvas designs single agents in every framework and mixes them in one flow, then the most-used frameworks get whole-flow authoring and code export one by one, in order of adoption (§4).
  • Unique feature it unlocks: compile one workflow to two or more frameworks and compare quality, cost and latency side by side in Evaluation Studio (S25). No competitor found offers this.
  • Every sprint keeps the standing rule: review the whole codebase for errors first, merge when done, version tags are left to the owner.

docs.text:
Buyers in 2026 rank governance, quality and observability first, where AgentCanvas is already strong; it is behind on reach (integrations, interop, end-user surfaces) and on RAG.

docs.title: 4. Multi-framework strategy
docs.text:
Builds on doc 11, doc 12, the adapter SPI in apps/api/agentcanvas/adapters/spi.py and the adapter specs; it does not redesign them.

Tiers (doc 11 §7): Interop — the framework's agent runs as a node (Wrapped Agent, remote A2A agent or MCP agent node), cheap and covers every framework at once · Authoring — idiomatic codegen, deploy, tracing, limited step debugging · Full — authoring plus live debugging, approvals, persistence, evals and import.

Framework Interop Authoring or Full Sprint Why this order LangChain / LangGraph / Deep Agents Done Full, done — Most real-world usage OpenAI Agents SDK S16 Agent design S21; flows and Full (agent tier) S25 S21, S25 Large user base; smallest adapter; unlocks convert-and-compare Pydantic AI and Agno S16 Agent design S21; flows Authoring S32 S21, S32 Fast-growing, cheap at Authoring tier; Agno is new to the adapter list CrewAI S16 Agent design S21; Full for Flows, Authoring for Crews S27 S21, S27 Biggest multi-agent community; moved ahead of Microsoft and ADK Google ADK S16 Agent design S21; flows Full S29–S30 S21, S29–S30 Enterprise reach through Google Cloud Strands and LlamaIndex Workflows S16 Agent design S21; flows Authoring S35 S21, S35 Smaller share; LlamaIndex pairs with Knowledge Studio Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen's successor) S16 Agent design S21; flows Authoring, Full later S21, S33–S34 Covers AutoGen users and .NET-leaning enterprises Mastra (TypeScript) S16 via MCP or A2A Authoring S36 Needs a Node.js sidecar host Claude Agent SDK S16 Agent design S21 S21 AG2, smolagents, Semantic Kernel, Haystack, DSPy, Vercel AI SDK, .NET and Java frameworks S16 Interop only (wrapped, A2A or MCP) until users ask — Wrapped or remote is enough until demand shows
  • Portable core plus native extras: core blocks compile to any framework; framework-only blocks are marked, and a portability check says which frameworks a workflow can target.
  • Mixed flows (S21, S28): each agent on the canvas picks its framework; the flow runs in the LangGraph host with the other frameworks' agents in process (A2A for other languages), and S28 exports and deploys such a flow as one project with typed boundaries between the parts.
  • Full depth only for the top three (OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK); the rest stop at Authoring until users ask, because each adapter spec sizes Full at 12–24 team-weeks.
  • Convert and compare: from S25, one click recompiles a workflow for another framework and Evaluation Studio runs both on the same dataset.
  • Same platform services for all: runs, inbox, triggers, versions, evals, policies and deployments stay framework-neutral, so each adapter inherits them.

docs.title: 5. Changes to the owner's ideas
docs.text:
1. "Support all frameworks" becomes "every framework runs from S16, the top ones go deep": equal depth for ten frameworks would take years and produce a lowest-common-denominator canvas.
  2. Multi-framework is a feature, not a checkbox: convert-and-compare uses the Evaluation Studio already built.
  3. Integrations come through a curated MCP connector gallery instead of hand-built connectors.
  4. Every workflow becomes a tool others can call (MCP and A2A endpoints, old S17, moved to S15).
  5. The Copilot is framework-aware (started in S14, #15).
  6. The two beginner sprints merge into one (S23), paired with importers from Langflow, Flowise and n8n.

docs.title: 8. Risks and open questions
docs.text:
• Framework churn: pinned versions per adapter, nightly upstream checks, adapter versions separate from the core.
  • Estimates: the adapter specs size each adapter for a team over 12–24 weeks; one or two sprints here assume the pace of S9–S14 and may stretch.
  • Re-plan cost (2026-10-09): Ship to users and Knowledge Studio move back six and four sprints to make room for S17 and S20–S22.
  • Interop is not authoring: wrapped agents are black boxes on the canvas (no per-step debugging inside them); docs and badges must say so.
  • Open question: a hosted cloud trial is the biggest adoption lever but means running paid infrastructure. Owner's call; not scheduled.

docs.title: 9. Sources
docs.text: Opened: this repository's README, docs 11, 12 and 15, the adapter specs index, adapters/spi.py. Search-result summaries only (pages not opened): the CrewAI, Dynatrace, Dify and keenable links above; n8n MCP server, top agent repositories by stars, open-source builders compared, enterprise platforms 2026. That AutoGen was folded into Microsoft Agent Framework (AG2 being its community fork) is from prior knowledge.

docs.title: 17 — Framework coverage review (2026-10-09)
docs.text:
Adopted by the owner on 2026-10-09 ("update the sprint plan as per the framework coverage review"). The plan changes in §5 are now the sprint order in doc 16 §7: F1 became S20 Framework foundation, F2 S21 Design any agent, F3 S22 Whole flows, preview; mixed-flow export is S28. Sprint numbers below in §5 are the ones this review proposed before renumbering.

2026-10-09 · reviewed main at v0.10.0 (merge 25be73e, after S16) and the approved plan in docs/agent-canvas-spec/16-competitive-roadmap.md, build-guide/13-sprint-plan.md, HANDOVER.md, docs 11 and 12 and the adapter specs. Review only; no code changed.

docs.title: 1. Short answer
docs.text:
• It is not tied to LangSmith. LangSmith is optional (tracing and dataset sync). The canvas designs, runs and exports flows on LangGraph / LangChain as its one engine.
  • Today the canvas can only design LangGraph flows. Agents from nine other frameworks (OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, Agno, Strands, LlamaIndex, Microsoft Agent Framework, Claude Agent SDK) can be used as steps, but someone has to write those agents in code first; the canvas runs them as black boxes.
  • "Mixed frameworks in one flow" works only in that limited sense: a LangGraph flow that calls finished agents from other frameworks. You cannot draw an agent on the canvas and say "build this one in CrewAI".
  • Against your expectation the plan scores about 55–60%. Real per-framework authoring is planned, but late (first one in S21, last in S32), the mixed part is missing from the sprint list entirely, and two foundation pieces it depends on are not scheduled.
  • It is feasible, if "every framework" means design and export single agents and simple flows in every framework, full depth in the top three. Full parity for ten frameworks is not realistic.
  • Recommendation: move framework work forward with three new sprints right after S16, before S17 Ship to users (§5), so that by roughly S19 you can design an agent on the canvas, pick its framework per node, run a mixed flow and export it.

docs.title: 2. What exists today (checked in code)
docs.text:
Capability Status Evidence Design a flow visually ✅ LangGraph only Only adapter installed: adapters/__init__.py raises no adapter installed for framework '…' for anything but langchain Pick a framework for a workflow ❌ IR has workflow.framework = "langchain" (ir/models.py:234) but no UI picker and no second value accepted Pick a framework per node (mixed design) ❌ No engine field in the IR; doc 12 WS7 describes it but nothing is built Export code ✅ LangGraph project only (with S19 deploy kit) get_adapter(wf.framework).package(...) in api/v1/versions.py:177 Run on the platform (runs, debugger, inbox, approvals, memory, time travel) ✅ LangGraph only api/main.py binds the langchain adapter for the whole process; the SPI (adapters/spi.py) assumes LangGraph checkpoints, update_state, thread copy and a LangGraph store Use an agent built in another framework ✅ black box, 9 frameworks agent.framework node: import_path to code in the Workspace (adapters/langchain/interop.py:223); runs inside the LangGraph host; one approval before it runs, no step-by-step view inside Use a remote agent ✅ A2A node (0.3 methods, no streaming) and MCP agent node Open Agent Spec import/export ✅ JSON agentspec.py: exports a workflow as an Agent Spec Flow; imports any Agent Spec flow/agent. Other Agent Spec runtimes can load the export, but nothing here runs or tests it on CrewAI/OpenAI/AutoGen Portable vs framework-only nodes ⚠️ half Node registry already splits core.* (16 portable nodes) from LangChain-only nodes (agent.deep, 10 mw.*, backend.*), but there is no portability check (P001–P004 from doc 12 are not implemented) Copilot builds for another framework ❌ It is "framework-aware" in prompts, but it can only build what the canvas can compile, so LangGraph

So the honest one-liner for users today: "Build in LangGraph; bring agents from anywhere."

docs.title: 3. How the plan matches the expectation
docs.text:
Your expectation has four parts. Scored against the approved roadmap S17–S32:

Expectation Planned? When Score A. Use agents made elsewhere Done in S16 (black box, A2A, MCP) done 90% B. Design flows in another framework and export its code Yes: OpenAI (S21), Pydantic AI+Agno (S24), CrewAI (S25–26), ADK (S27–28), Strands+LlamaIndex (S29), Microsoft (S30–31), Mastra (S32) 5 to 16 sprints away 60% (right content, too late, single-framework per workflow) C. Mix frameworks in one designed flow Not in the sprint list. Doc 12 has it (WS7, per-node engine, boundary contracts), the roadmap dropped it never scheduled 15% (only the black-box form from S16) D. Widely used frameworks covered 10 Python + Mastra — 75% (missing: AG2/AutoGen classic, Semantic Kernel, smolagents, Haystack, DSPy, Vercel AI SDK; .NET and Java not at all)

Weighted roughly equally: about 55–60%.

docs.title: 4. Feasibility and gaps
docs.text:
Feasible: - Single agents in any framework are cheap. Every framework has the same agent shape: instructions, model, tools, structured output. The canvas Agent node already holds exactly that. Generating Agent(...) for each framework is a template per framework, not a new engine. This is the fastest way to "design in any framework". - Mixed flows are architecturally ready. S16 already runs foreign agents inside the LangGraph host and keeps approvals, traces and the inbox working. A canvas-designed agent compiled to CrewAI can use the same mechanism instead of hand-written code. - The Agent Spec bridge (doc 12 M1.4: load portable flows with pyagentspec into LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, AutoGen, WayFlow) can give a "preview" export of whole flows for several frameworks at once. It is in doc 12 but missing from the roadmap.

Gaps that will block the planned adapter sprints: 1. SPI is LangGraph-shaped. It requires checkpoint history, update_state, thread copy and a key-value store from every adapter, and it also carries the Copilot's and the LLM judge's model calls. A second adapter can't implement that honestly. Needs an SPI v2: required core (generate, package, execute, events) plus optional capabilities (state, time travel, memory), with model calls moved out of the framework adapter. 2. One adapter per process. api/main.py binds langchain at startup; runs, state and memory never look at workflow.framework. The runtime must choose the adapter per workflow. 3. No framework picker, no portability check, no per-node engine in the IR or UI. 4. Effort estimates are optimistic. The adapter specs size each adapter at 12–24 weeks for a three-person team; the roadmap gives each one or two sprints. Sprint pace so far has been fast, but "Full" tier (live debugging, approvals, persistence, import) for five frameworks will stretch. Plan "Authoring" first for all, "Full" only for the top three. 5. Export is one framework per project. Mixed export (a LangGraph host plus CrewAI and OpenAI agent modules in one deployable project) needs the deploy kit to install several framework packages and vendor several runtimes. The S16 export already does this for black-box agents, so the gap is small. 6. Framework-only nodes are LangChain-only today. Each adapter needs its own dialect nodes (CrewAI crew, ADK loop agent, OpenAI handoff and guardrail) or users of those frameworks will find the canvas shallow. 7. Wrapped agents need hand-written code. That is fine for "bring your own agent", but it is the opposite of "design on the canvas", which is the core of your ask.

docs.title: 5. Recommended plan changes
docs.text:
Keep the existing sprint content; insert three framework sprints now and add mixed-flow work to the list.

New order Sprint Scope Done when next F1 Framework foundation (new) SPI v2 (required core + optional capabilities; model calls out of the adapter); runtime picks the adapter per workflow; IR v1.2 with engine per node; framework picker in the editor; portability check and badges (which nodes can compile to which framework) A toy second adapter passes the conformance kit; the editor shows what blocks a workflow from targeting each framework then F2 Design any agent (new) The canvas Agent node compiles to a native agent in each of the 9 frameworks (instructions, model, tools including MCP/HTTP/Python, structured output); chosen per node; runs as a step in the LangGraph flow with approvals and traces; export of a single agent as a native project per framework A flow with one OpenAI, one CrewAI and one ADK agent, all drawn on the canvas, runs and exports; each framework's agent also exports alone and runs with that framework's own runner then F3 Whole flows, preview (new) Agent Spec bridge: export portable flows to CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, AutoGen and LangGraph via pyagentspec, tested in CI; marked "preview" 5 templates export and run on 3 frameworks S17 Ship to users unchanged S20 Knowledge Studio unchanged S21 OpenAI Agents SDK flow tier + convert-and-compare, now on the F1 foundation S22 Model gateway unchanged S23 CrewAI (moved up from S25–26) Flows authoring + dialect nodes; Full only for Flows Bigger community than Pydantic AI and Agno S24 Mixed-flow export and boundaries (new, from doc 12 WS7) Typed contracts between framework parts, one deployable project with several frameworks, A2A for cross-language parts A mixed template deploys with the deploy kit S25–26 Google ADK, S27 Onboarding and importers, S28 Pydantic AI + Agno, S29–30 Microsoft Agent Framework, S31 Strands + LlamaIndex, S32 Mastra Authoring tier first; Full only for OpenAI, CrewAI and ADK later Long tail via Interop only AG2, smolagents, Semantic Kernel, Haystack, DSPy, Vercel AI SDK, .NET and Java frameworks Black box / A2A until users ask

Why this order: it delivers the core promise (design in any framework, mix them) about eight sprints earlier than today's plan, it builds on S16 code that already exists, and it makes every later adapter sprint cheaper because F1 removes the LangGraph assumptions once. The cost is that S17 Ship to users and S20 Knowledge Studio move back by three sprints.

Other plan fixes: - Rename the tiers in the docs and UI so users understand them: "Bring your agent" (Interop), "Design in X" (Authoring), "Debug in X" (Full). - Update the README and user guide to say plainly what works today: "Build in LangGraph, bring agents from anywhere" until F2 lands. - Add one conformance suite shared by all adapters (doc 12 M0.5) as part of F1, so each later adapter sprint has a clear "done".

docs.title: 6. Decision for the owner
docs.text:
1. Adopt the F1–F3 insert before S17 (recommended): framework design and mixed flows arrive next, S17 and S20 wait three sprints.
  2. Keep the approved order, add F1 and mixed flows only: cheaper change, but designing in other frameworks still starts at S21.
  3. Keep the plan as is: LangGraph-only design until S21, no mixed design at all.

docs.title: 2. Positioning
docs.text: Two layers: Crews (role-based autonomous collaboration) and Flows (event-driven, precise control, state, persistence, human feedback). Flows map to the Graph tier; Crews and Agents to the Agent tier. The declarative FlowDefinition is the adapter's primary codegen target and import source. Target T1 for Flows, T2 for hierarchical Crews (manager-driven delegation is non-deterministic to visualise step-by-step).

docs.title: 5. Code generation
docs.text:
from crewai.flow import Flow, HumanFeedbackResult, human_feedback, listen, persist, router, start   # verified exports

class TriageState(BaseModel):                     # from IR state schema
    ticket: Ticket | None = None
    category: str = ""
    draft: str = ""

@persist(postgres_persistence)                    # binding from doc 08 (adapter-provided FlowPersistence)
class SupportTriageFlow(Flow[TriageState]):
    @start()                                      # @canvas-node n_ingest
    def ingest(self):
        return self.state.ticket

    @router(ingest)                               # @canvas-node n_route
    def route(self):
        self.state.category = classify_crew.kickoff(inputs={"ticket": self.state.ticket.text}).pydantic.category
        return self.state.category                # "billing" | "tech"

    @listen("billing")                            # @canvas-node n_billing (crew action)
    @human_feedback(message="Approve this reply?", emit=["approved", "rejected"], llm="gpt-5-mini",
                    default_outcome="rejected")   # @canvas-node n_review
    def billing(self):
        self.state.draft = billing_crew.kickoff(inputs={"ticket": self.state.ticket.text}).raw
        return self.state.draft

    @listen("approved")                           # @canvas-node n_send
    def send(self, result: HumanFeedbackResult):
        send_reply(self.state.ticket, result.output)
The compiler also emits the equivalent FlowDefinition (JSON) — used for validation, import and visual diffing.

docs.title: 6. HITL
docs.text:
• @human_feedback with an async provider implemented by the adapter: raising HumanFeedbackPending(context=PendingFeedbackContext(...)) ends the run with a canonical input/approval interrupt; ResumeEnvelope.native_state = {flow_class, flow_id, pending_context}.
  • Resume: restore persisted flow (@persist) and call flow.resume(feedback) / await flow.resume_async(feedback); emit outcomes map to canvas route ports; llm maps free-text feedback to outcomes.
  • learn=True (feedback learning) surfaced as a Learning Loop hook (doc 09).

docs.title: 7. State & persistence
docs.text: Thread ↔ flow id (persisted state). Bindings: Postgres/Redis FlowPersistence (ours), SQLite (dev). CheckpointConfig(location, on_events, provider) enabled for T1 durability; crews within flows are re-run on resume unless outputs cached in state (validator warns on side effects, W070).

docs.title: 8. Events & tracing
docs.text: Reuse AG-UI crew-ai integration; add a BaseEventListener subclass that maps flow method start/finish, crew/task/agent/tool events to canonical events with canvas_node_id (from method name ↔ source map). OTel via CrewAI telemetry integration + our listener spans.

docs.title: 5. Code generation (router + loop + approval — mirrors verified samples)
docs.text:
from google.adk import Agent, Event, Workflow
from google.adk.events import RequestInput
from google.adk.tools import FunctionTool

# ── @canvas-node n_classify ──
classify = Agent(name="classify", model="gemini-3.6-flash",
                 instruction="Classify the ticket: {ticket_text}",
                 output_schema=Classification, output_key="classification")

# ── @canvas-node n_route ──
def route_ticket(classification: Classification):
    yield Event(route=classification.category)

# ── @canvas-node n_refund (tool with approval from interrupt_on) ──
refund_tool = FunctionTool(issue_refund, require_confirmation=True)
billing = Agent(name="billing", model="gemini-3.6-pro", instruction=BILLING_PROMPT, tools=[refund_tool])

# ── @canvas-node n_review (Human input) ──
def request_review(draft: str):
    yield RequestInput(message=f"Approve this reply?\n---\n{draft}")

root_agent = Workflow(
    name="support_triage",
    edges=[
        ("START", ingest, classify, route_ticket),
        (route_ticket, {"billing": billing, "tech": tech_agent}),
        (billing, draft_reply, request_review, handle_review),
        (handle_review, {"revise": draft_reply, "approved": send_reply}),
    ],
)

docs.title: 6. HITL
docs.text:
• Tool approval: require_confirmation → canonical tool_approval; resume by delivering the function response containing a ToolConfirmation (confirmed/payload) into the same session.
  • Input node: RequestInput → canonical input with response_schema from the node's declared input; resume by sending the human response; rerun_on_resume controls node re-execution (default True) — the adapter sets it per node to preserve side-effect correctness (doc 08 §5.5).
  • Cross-process: session events are the durable log; ResumeEnvelope.native_state = {app_name, user_id, session_id, pending_ids}.

docs.title: 7. State & persistence
docs.text:
• Thread ↔ session_id (+ user_id from authenticated identity, app_name = workflow slug).
  • Bindings: Postgres/MySQL → DatabaseSessionService(db_url); dev → SqliteSessionService; GCP → VertexAiSessionService. Memory Spaces via platform tools, or MemoryService dialect binding.
  • IR state channels ↔ session state keys (namespaced ac:<channel> to avoid collisions with user keys; ADK state prefixes such as user:/app: exposed as scope options).

docs.title: 8. Events & tracing
docs.text:
• Reuse AG-UI adk-middleware integration for text/tool/state events; add node mapping from workflow node names (slug__canvasid) and ac.* extension events (interrupts, checkpoints = session event ids, usage).
  • OTel: ADK emits GenAI semconv spans; generated code adds agentcanvas.node_id via a small BasePlugin (AgentCanvasPlugin) that also emits canonical events in Mode B.

docs.title: 9. Hosting
docs.text:
• Mode A: deployments-wrap-sdk wrap(Runner(...)) + LangsmithSessionService, or our generic @entrypoint wrapper.
  • Mode B: adk deploy agent_engine | cloud_run | gke | docker driven by the Deploy service; AgentCanvasPlugin posts canonical events; HITL through ADK APIs.
  • Mode C: ADK A2A server exposure; RemoteA2aAgent for consuming.

docs.title: 10. Import / round-trip
docs.text:
• ADK YAML AgentConfig (JSON Schema in agents/config_schemas/AgentConfig.json) ↔ Core IR for the agent layer (lossless for supported fields).
  • Workflow(edges=…) Python import via AST (edge tuples and route dicts are statically analysable); function bodies become Script nodes.

docs.title: 11. Gaps & emulations
docs.text: Reducers (E, generated merges); IR Send with arbitrary payloads (mapped to parallel_worker over a generated list; per-item payload must be the item); breakpoints implemented as injected RequestInput-style debug pauses in dev mode only.

docs.title: 12. Work plan (squad B, ~24 weeks)
docs.text: Weeks Deliverable 1–2 Verification refresh (incl. TS/Java parity notes), capability sign-off 3–5 Dialect nodes; ToolSpec/ModelSpec factories; YAML AgentConfig import/export 5–11 Workflow lowering (sequence, routes, JoinNode, parallel_worker, loops, nested), state bridge, emulated reducers, source maps 10–13 HITL (require_confirmation, RequestInput), envelope, Inbox 12–14 Session/memory bindings (DatabaseSessionService on Postgres) 13–16 Events: adk-middleware reuse + AgentCanvasPlugin; OTel mapping 16–19 Hosting A & B (Agent Engine, Cloud Run) 18–22 Conformance (full T1), templates (Triage, Research fan-out, Approval loop) 22–24 Beta & certification

docs.text: workflow package is new in 2.x and evolving (pin minor; nightly CI); feature parity differs across ADK languages (Python first); Vertex-specific services require GCP credentials (bindings optional).

docs.title: 1. Verified baseline
docs.text:
• llama-index-workflows 2.11.1 (MIT) plus llama-agents-server, -client, -control-plane, -dbos, -agentcore, llamactl.
  • Verified: workflows/decorators.py (@step(num_workers=4, retry_policy=…)), events.py (StartEvent, StopEvent, InputRequiredEvent, HumanResponseEvent, StepFailedEvent, timeout/cancel events), context/context.py (Context.send_event, write_event_to_stream, state store, serializers), representation/ (build & validate workflow graph), retry_policy.py.

docs.text: Event-driven workflows: steps consume and emit typed events; edges are event types. Target T2.

docs.title: 3. Core IR mapping (lowering rule: one Event subclass per IR edge)
docs.text: Core concept Level Construct Workflow N class <Name>(Workflow) Node N @step async def node(self, ctx: Context, ev: <InEdgeEvent>) -> <OutEdgeEvent> Sequence N step A returns AtoB event consumed by step B Router N step returns one of several event types (union return annotation) Parallel + join N ctx.send_event(...) multiple events; join step uses ctx.collect_events(ev, [TypeA, TypeB]) Map N num_workers + one event per item; collect at join Loop N event back to an earlier step type + counter in state Subgraph N nested workflow invoked in a step Agent node E LlamaIndex agent (e.g. function agent) run inside a step Shared state N Context state store (typed) Input / approval N ctx.write_event_to_stream(InputRequiredEvent(...)) + wait for HumanResponseEvent; external ctx.send_event(HumanResponseEvent(...)) Persistence N Context serialisation; DBOS durability package Retry / timeout N retry_policy, workflow timeout Events N stream_events(); AG-UI llama-index integration

docs.title: 4–11 (summary)
docs.text: Dialect: llamaindex.agent, llamaindex.query_engine, llamaindex.retriever (RAG strengths). Envelope: serialised Context + pending event ids. Hosting: Mode A; Mode B llama-agents server/control plane or AgentCore; Mode C A2A. Import: representation package can build a graph from a Workflow class → IR. Gaps: reducers (E); tool-level approval inside agents (E).

docs.text: Verification (1–2) · event-per-edge lowering & representation import (3–7) · HITL events & context serialisation (6–8) · events (8–9) · conformance & beta (9–12). Risk: event-type explosion for large graphs (namespaced generated event module).

1. Verified baseline

• @mastra/core 1.72 (Apache-2.0 except ee/ directories, which use a separate enterprise licence and are excluded from generated code).

docs.text:
from agent_framework import Case, Default, Executor, WorkflowBuilder, WorkflowContext, handler, response_handler

class Classify(Executor):                                   # @canvas-node n_cls
    @handler
    async def run(self, ticket: Ticket, ctx: WorkflowContext[Classified]) -> None:
        result = await classifier_agent.run(ticket.text)     # Agent(client=…, instructions=…)
        await ctx.send_message(Classified(ticket=ticket, category=parse(result)))

class Review(Executor):                                     # @canvas-node n_review (Approval)
    @handler
    async def run(self, draft: Draft, ctx: WorkflowContext[Draft]) -> None:
        await ctx.request_info(request_data=ApprovalRequest(text=draft.text), response_type=ApprovalResponse)

    @response_handler
    async def on_response(self, original: ApprovalRequest, response: ApprovalResponse, ctx: WorkflowContext[Draft]) -> None:
        await ctx.send_message(Draft(text=response.edited_text or original.text, approved=response.approved))

workflow = (
    WorkflowBuilder(start_executor=classify, name="support_triage", checkpoint_storage=checkpoints)
    .add_switch_case_edge_group(classify, [
        Case(condition=lambda m: m.category == "billing", target=billing),
        Default(target=tech),
    ])
    .add_edge(billing, review)
    .add_edge(review, send)
    .build()
)
(Verified against samples/02-agents/devui/workflow_spam/workflow.py: ctx.request_info(request_data=…, response_type=…) and @response_handler async def …(self, original_request, response, ctx).)

docs.text:
# ── @canvas-node n_cls "Classify" (core.agent → openai) ──
classifier = Agent(name="classify", instructions=CLASSIFY_PROMPT, model="gpt-5-mini", output_type=Classification)

# ── @canvas-node n_bill "Billing agent" ──
billing = Agent(name="billing", instructions=BILLING_PROMPT, tools=[refund], model="gpt-5.5")

@function_tool(needs_approval=True)          # @canvas-node n_refund (approval from interrupt_on)
async def refund(order_id: str, amount: float) -> str: ...

async def orchestrate(inp: Input, ctx: RunCtx, emit: Emitter, resume: ResumeState | None):
    # generated state machine: each canvas node is a resumable step (step index saved in the envelope)
    if resume is None or resume.step <= 0:
        with emit.node("n_cls"):
            r = await Runner.run(classifier, inp.text, context=ctx, session=ctx.session)
            ctx.state.category = r.final_output.category
    if ctx.state.category == "billing":                                  # @canvas-node n_route
        with emit.node("n_bill"):
            r = await Runner.run(billing, resume.state if resume else inp.text, context=ctx, session=ctx.session)
            if r.interruptions:                                          # HITL pause
                return Paused(step=1, native=r.to_state().to_json(), pending=to_canonical(r.interruptions))

docs.title: 6. HITL
docs.text:
• Raise: tools with needs_approval (bool or async callable (ctx, params, call_id) -> bool); Agent.as_tool(needs_approval=…); hosted MCP require_approval.
  • Pause: result.interruptions → canonical InterruptRequest(kind="tool_approval") per ToolApprovalItem.
  • Envelope: result.to_state().to_json() stored in ResumeEnvelope.native_state (cross-process safe).
  • Resume: RunState.from_json(...) (or from_string) → state.approve(item) / state.reject(item, rejection_message=…) → Runner.run(top_agent, state).
  • Edit decision: emulated = reject with a message containing the corrected arguments and a system note instructing the model to re-issue the call (conformance case C-HITL-edit validates behaviour); marked P002.
  • Sticky decisions: always_approve / always_reject exposed as Inbox "approve for this thread".

  • RunHooks (on_agent_start/end, on_tool_start/end, on_handoff, on_llm_start/end) used for usage/cost events.
  • Tracing: custom TracingProcessor exporting spans to OTel with agentcanvas.node_id; option to keep OpenAI tracing on/off per workspace policy (set_tracing_disabled).
