docs.title: 5. The runner (runtime/runner.py)
docs.text:
Responsibilities: build the graph for a thread, stream canonical events, record run status, register interrupts, support cancel.

This is the target design for tickets M1-T6, M4-T4, M4-T8, M4-T10 (repository and adapter calls are placeholders). The tested, runnable starting point is reference/backend/agentcanvas/api/app.py (_stream).

class RunRegistry:
    """In-process registry of active runs (per API instance)."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}

async def stream_run(ctx: RunContext) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    run = await runs_repo.create(ctx.thread_id, ctx.ir_hash, mode=ctx.mode)
    graph = await adapter.build(ctx.workflow, ctx.resources, checkpointer=ctx.checkpointer, store=ctx.store)
    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": ctx.thread_id}, "recursion_limit": settings.recursion_limit,
              "metadata": {"workflow_id": ctx.workflow.id, "run_id": run.id}}
    queue: asyncio.Queue[dict | None] = asyncio.Queue()

    async def pump():
        try:
            async for part in graph.astream(ctx.graph_input, config,
                                            stream_mode=["tasks", "updates", "messages", "custom"],
                                            subgraphs=True, version="v2",
                                            interrupt_before=ctx.breakpoints_before or None,
                                            interrupt_after=ctx.breakpoints_after or None):
                for ev in adapter.translate(part, ctx.names):
                    await queue.put(ev)
            snap = await graph.aget_state(config)
            await record_interrupts(run, snap)                 # -> interrupt_task rows (Inbox)
            status = "interrupted" if snap.interrupts or snap.next else "success"
            await runs_repo.finish(run.id, status)
            await queue.put({"type": "RUN_FINISHED", "runId": run.id, "outcome": status})
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await runs_repo.finish(run.id, "cancelled")
            await queue.put({"type": "RUN_ERROR", "message": "cancelled"})
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            await runs_repo.finish(run.id, "error", error=str(exc))
            await queue.put({"type": "RUN_ERROR", "message": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"})
        finally:
            await queue.put(None)

    registry.tasks[run.id] = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    yield sse({"type": "RUN_STARTED", "runId": run.id, "threadId": ctx.thread_id})
    while (ev := await queue.get()) is not None:
        yield sse(ev)
    registry.tasks.pop(run.id, None)
Why a queue + background task: the run keeps going (and can be cancelled or observed) even if the browser disconnects. Add GET /runs/{id}/events later to re-attach (post-MVP: buffer events in Redis Streams).

Note: with breakpoints the graph stops with snap.next non-empty but no interrupts — treat that as interrupted too (verified).

docs.title: 6. Resources, secrets and models
docs.text:
• Resources(thread_id) resolves model.chat resources via init_chat_model(model, **params); api_key params come from secret refs: config {"api_key": {"$secret": "OPENAI_API_KEY"}} → decrypt from secret table → pass as api_key= (never set process-wide env vars per user).
  • Cache resolved Resources per (thread_id, ir_hash) for the life of a run; real models are stateless, fakes are not (FAQ P-03).
  • Secrets encryption (M5): cryptography.fernet.Fernet(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sha256(settings.secret_key).digest())); M8 replaces this with cloud KMS envelope encryption.

docs.title: 7. Persistence wiring (MVP)
docs.text:
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    async with AsyncPostgresSaver.from_conn_string(settings.database_url) as saver, \
               AsyncPostgresStore.from_conn_string(settings.database_url) as store:
        await saver.setup(); await store.setup()
        app.state.checkpointer, app.state.store = saver, store
        yield
- Durability: default async; for workflows marked "side effects" use durability="sync" in astream(...) (verified parameter). - Deleting a thread: await saver.adelete_thread(thread_id) (verified) + delete thread row. - Redis/Mongo checkpointers and the RoutedStore are post-MVP (doc08); Redis requires Redis 8/Stack (FAQ P-04).

docs.title: 8. Script execution protocol (sandbox)
docs.text: Request (stdin, JSON): {"import_path": "scripts.score:run", "state": {...}} · Response (stdout, JSON): {"update": {...}} or {"error": {"type": "...", "message": "..."}}. Exit code 0 always; the runner converts error into an exception so LangGraph retry policies apply. Timeout enforced by the runner (asyncio.wait_for), container killed on timeout.

docs.title: 9. Triggers & scheduling
docs.text:
• Webhooks: verify hmac.compare_digest(expected, received) where expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret, raw_body, sha256).hexdigest(); reject if older than 5 minutes when a timestamp header is present.
  • Cron: apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio.AsyncIOScheduler with CronTrigger.from_crontab(expr, timezone=tz); on multiple API replicas, only the instance holding Postgres advisory lock pg_try_advisory_lock(42) runs the scheduler.

docs.title: 10. Errors and logging
docs.text:
• Domain exceptions → problem+json in api/errors.py (02 §5).
  • structlog processors: timestamp, level, request_id, bound context (workflow_id, thread_id, run_id); JSON renderer in non-dev.
  • Never log: secret values, full prompts/outputs in prod (log lengths and hashes instead).

docs.title: 06 — Frontend Guide
docs.text: Stack (ADR 0006): React 19 · TypeScript (strict) · Vite · @xyflow/react 12 (canvas) · Zustand (client state) · TanStack Query (server data) · @rjsf/core 6 (config forms) · elkjs (auto-layout) · @monaco-editor/react (code) · Vitest + Playwright. Every snippet below type-checks with these versions (see reference/web/snippets/verifyLibs.tsx and verifyGuide06.tsx).

apps/web/src/
├── app/            App.tsx, routes.tsx, Layout.tsx, providers.tsx (QueryClientProvider, theme)
├── api/            client.ts (apiFetch + ApiError), schema.d.ts (generated), queries.ts (useWorkflow, useNodeTypes…)

docs.title: 2. Data flow
docs.text:
TanStack Query ──GET workflow──► useWorkflow() ──► irToFlow() ──► <ReactFlow nodes edges>
      ▲                                                               │ user edits
      │ invalidate on success                                          ▼
  POST /commands (If-Match) ◄── commandQueue (debounce 300 ms) ◄── commands.ts (AddNode, Connect…)
                                                                          │ optimistic apply
                                                                          ▼
                                                                  local IR copy (Zustand)
Run: postStream() ──SSE──► runStore.apply(event) ──► node status colours, outputs, interrupt card
Rules: - The IR is the model; React Flow nodes/edges are derived (irToFlow). Never store business data only in React Flow state. - Edits are commands, applied optimistically to the local IR and sent to the server; on 409 refetch and re-apply nothing (show toast). - Node positions live in the separate layout document (M1-T5).

docs.title: 3. The API client
docs.text:
export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(public status: number, public problem: { title?: string; detail?: string; errors?: unknown[] }) {
    super(problem.title ?? `HTTP ${status}`);
  }
}
export async function apiFetch<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit & { version?: number }): Promise<T> {
  const headers = new Headers(init?.headers);
  headers.set("content-type", "application/json");
  if (init?.version !== undefined) headers.set("If-Match", String(init.version));
  const res = await fetch(`/api/v1${path}`, { ...init, headers });
  if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(res.status, await res.json().catch(() => ({})));
  return res.status === 204 ? (undefined as T) : ((await res.json()) as T);
}

docs.title: 4. Custom node renderer (M2-T5)
docs.text:
One generic component draws every widget from its manifest: 

import { Handle, Position, type NodeProps } from "@xyflow/react";

export function WidgetNode({ data }: NodeProps<Node<WidgetData>>) {
  const { manifest, label, status, routes } = data;
  return (
    <div className={`widget status-${status}`}>
      {manifest.ports.inputs.map((p, i) => (
        <Handle key={p.name} id={p.name} type="target" position={Position.Left}
                style={{ top: 24 + i * 16, background: PORT_COLORS[p.type] }} title={`${p.name}: ${p.type}`} />
      ))}
      <header>{manifest.icon} {label}</header>
      {(routes ?? ["next"]).map((r, i) => (
        <Handle key={r} id={routes ? `route:${r}` : "next"} type="source" position={Position.Right} style={{ top: 24 + i * 16 }} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
// register once: <ReactFlow nodeTypes={{ widget: WidgetNode }} … />  (define nodeTypes outside components to avoid re-renders)

docs.title: 5. Type-checked connections (M2-T6)
docs.text:
import type { IsValidConnection } from "@xyflow/react";

export const makeIsValid = (portType: (nodeId: string, handle: string | null, dir: "in" | "out") => string | undefined)
  : IsValidConnection => (c) => {
    const out = portType(c.source, c.sourceHandle ?? null, "out");
    const inp = portType(c.target, c.targetHandle ?? null, "in");
    return !!out && !!inp && (out === inp || inp === "Any" || (inp === "Tool[]" && out === "Tool"));
  };
Show why a connection is refused: keep the last rejected pair in state and render a tooltip near the cursor.

docs.title: 6. Inspector forms with RJSF (M2-T7)

import Form from "@rjsf/core";
import validator from "@rjsf/validator-ajv8";

<Form schema={manifest.config_schema} formData={node.config} validator={validator}
      widgets={{ prompt: PromptWidget, channel: ChannelSelect, cel: CelEditor }}
      uiSchema={uiSchemaFromFormats(manifest.config_schema)}   // maps "format": "prompt" -> "ui:widget": "prompt"
      onChange={(e) => queueCommand({ op: "UpdateNodeConfig", node_id: node.id, patch: e.formData })}
      liveValidate showErrorList={false} />
- PromptWidget: textarea + autocomplete of {{ state.<channel> }} + token estimate (chars / 4). - ChannelSelect: <select> of state channel names. - CelEditor: input that calls POST /v1/expressions/check (debounced) and shows the error. - Hide the default submit button: pass <Form …><></></Form> children.

docs.title: 7. Auto-layout with ELK (M2-T11)
docs.text:
import ELK from "elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js";
export async function layout(nodes: Node[], edges: Edge[]): Promise<Node[]> {
  const res = await new ELK().layout({
    id: "root", layoutOptions: { "elk.algorithm": "layered", "elk.direction": "RIGHT", "elk.spacing.nodeNode": "40" },
    children: nodes.map((n) => ({ id: n.id, width: n.measured?.width ?? 180, height: n.measured?.height ?? 60 })),
    edges: edges.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, sources: [e.source], targets: [e.target] })),
  });
  return nodes.map((n) => { const p = res.children?.find((c) => c.id === n.id); return { ...n, position: { x: p?.x ?? 0, y: p?.y ?? 0 } }; });
}

docs.title: 8. Run store & SSE (from the reference)
docs.text:
reference/web/src/sse.ts and runStore.ts are production-ready starting points: - postStream(url, body, onEvent) — POST + incremental SSE parsing (handles messages split across network chunks). - reduce(state, event) — pure function; unit-test every event type. - Batch high-frequency TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT updates with requestAnimationFrame (M4-T3) to avoid 1,000 re-renders per second.

Status colours (keep consistent everywhere): idle #e5e7eb · running #3b82f6 · ok #22c55e · error #ef4444 · interrupted #f59e0b · cached #9ca3af.

Interrupt payload UI Resume value sent {"action_requests": [...], "review_configs": [...]} (agent tool approval) tool name, JSON args (editable if edit allowed), Approve / Edit / Reject (+ message) {"decisions": [{"type": "approve"}]} · {"decisions": [{"type": "edit", "edited_action": {"name": "...", "args": {...}}}]} · {"decisions": [{"type": "reject", "message": "..."}]} {"kind": "approval", "value": ...} value preview (editable), Approve / Reject {"approved": true, "value": <edited or omitted>} {"kind": "input", "response_schema": {...}} RJSF form the form data

docs.title: 11. Accessibility & UX checklist
docs.text:
• Every button has a text label or aria-label; focus rings visible.
  • Keyboard: Tab moves through nodes (nodesFocusable), Delete removes, ⌘Z undo, ⌘K palette.
  • Colour is never the only signal: status also shown as an icon/text badge.
  • Loading skeletons for data fetches; empty states with a call to action ("Drag a node from the palette").

docs.title: 12. Testing
docs.text:
• Vitest: irToFlow, reduce, command inverse functions, makeIsValid, form→command mapping.
  • Playwright: skeleton flow (run → approve), build-a-workflow flow (drag, connect, configure, run), undo/redo, conflict toast. Use the fake-model backend (agentcanvas.dev.fake_server) in CI.

docs.title: 07 — Compiler & Node Types: the "add a node type" recipe
docs.text: Every widget in the catalog (spec doc04) is added with the same 9 steps. The tutorial exercise (03 Part 10) walks through them once for core.counter; this page is the checklist to reuse for every M3 ticket.

docs.title: The 9-step recipe
docs.text: # Step File(s) Done when 1 Design the node: inputs/outputs (ports), config fields, what it reads/writes in state, how it maps to LangChain/LangGraph (doc04 "Compiles to" column) ticket description reviewed by a teammate 2 IR: add the type string to Node.type (or Resource.type) ir/models.py model validates an example 3 Manifest: ports, config_schema (JSON Schema with titles, descriptions, defaults, format hints) registry/nodes/<type>.json GET /v1/node-types lists it 4 Builder in the node library: pure function returning a LangGraph node (or agent/subgraph) adapters/langchain/nodes.py unit test calls it directly 5 Interpreter branch adapters/langchain/interpreter.py graph builds 6 Template branch (same builder call; optional keys via .get(); literals via py filter) templates/graph.py.j2 generated code passes ruff + pyright 7 Validator rules specific to the node (required wiring, channel types, safety) ir/rules/*.py failing/passing IR tests 8 Tests: builder unit test, interpreted run, generated-equals-interpreted test, validator tests tests/… all green 9 UI: icon/category, custom inspector widget if needed, docs link web/src/… node appears in palette and is configurable

docs.title: Rules that keep generated code honest
docs.text:
1. One builder, two callers. Interpreter and template must call the same builder with the same arguments. Never duplicate logic in the template.
  2. Determinism. Iterate IR lists in stored order; no timestamps/UUIDs in output; run ruff format. test_generation_is_deterministic must stay green.
  3. Source map comment before every block: # ── @canvas-node <id> "<label>" (<type>) ──.
  4. No secrets in generated code — only {"$secret": "NAME"} references resolved by Resources at runtime.
  5. Readable names. Generated identifiers come from IR name (snake_case, validated); router functions are <name>_route.
  6. Side effects after approvals. If a node both calls external systems and needs approval, split it into two nodes (validator E070; FAQ P-06).

docs.title: Mapping cheat-sheet (verified APIs)
docs.text: Widget Builder uses LLM call model.ainvoke([HumanMessage(render_template(prompt, state))]) Agent create_agent(model, tools=…, system_prompt=…, middleware=[HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={...}), …], response_format=…, name=…) Deep Agent create_deep_agent(model=…, tools=…, system_prompt=…, subagents=[{"name","description","system_prompt","tools"}], backend=CompositeBackend(default=StateBackend(), routes={"/memories/": StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (...))}), interrupt_on={...}, name=…) Router builder.add_conditional_edges(name, router_fn(cases, default), {route: target}) Map conditional edge returning [Send(target, {"item": x}) for x in state[items]]; results via an append channel Join builder.add_edge(["a", "b"], "join") Approval / input interrupt({...}) → resume Command(resume=value) Retry / timeout / cache add_node(..., retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=n), timeout=TimeoutPolicy(run_timeout=s), cache_policy=CachePolicy(ttl=s)) + compile(cache=InMemoryCache()) MCP tools async with MCPAdapter({"mcpServers": {name: {"url": url, "auth": token}}}) as a: tools = await a.list_tools() Guardrails PIIMiddleware, ModelCallLimitMiddleware, ToolCallLimitMiddleware, ModelRetryMiddleware, ModelFallbackMiddleware, SummarizationMiddleware (signatures in 04 M3-T12) Error route add_node(..., error_handler=<fn(state, error: langgraph.errors.NodeError) -> Command>)

docs.title: Equivalence test template (copy for every node type)
docs.text:
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES)            # inputs covering each branch of the node
async def test_generated_equals_interpreted(tmp_path, case):
    wf = load_ir("examples/<node>.ir.json")
    mod = load_generated(generate(wf), tmp_path)    # helper from tests/test_run.py
    a = await run_case(build_graph(wf, fakes(case), checkpointer=InMemorySaver()), case)
    b = await run_case(mod.build_graph(fakes(case), checkpointer=InMemorySaver()), case)
    assert a == b

docs.title: 2. Fake models — read this before writing agent tests
docs.text:
Verified pitfalls (FAQ P-01…P-03): 1. LangChain's fake chat models lack bind_tools() → use agentcanvas.testing.ToolFakeModel. 2. Token streaming (stream_mode="messages") + a tool-call-only fake reply → No generations found in stream → scripted() sets disable_streaming=True. 3. Scripted fakes remember their position → give each thread its own Resources (see resources_factory in tests/test_api.py).

from agentcanvas.testing import scripted, tool_call
smart = scripted(tool_call("send_reply", {"text": "Hi"}), "Reply sent.")   # 1st call: tool call, 2nd: final text
res = Resources(overrides={"smart_model": smart, "fast_model": scripted("low")})
To assert what the model received (e.g. PII redaction), subclass ToolFakeModel and record messages in _generate.

docs.title: 3. Async tests
docs.text:
• pytest-asyncio with asyncio_mode = "auto" (in pyproject.toml): write async def test_… directly.
  • Async fixtures that need cleanup use yield (see the client fixture).
  • For the app lifespan in tests: async with api.lifespan(api.app): … then httpx.ASGITransport(app=api.app).

docs.title: 4. Database tests
docs.text:
• Use a dedicated database (TEST_DATABASE_URL) created per CI job; run alembic upgrade head in a session-scoped fixture.
  • Isolate tests with transactions rolled back at the end, or unique thread/workflow ids per test.
  • LangGraph checkpoint tables are created by saver.setup(); call it in the fixture.

docs.title: 5. Property-based tests (M1-T4)
docs.text:
from hypothesis import given, strategies as st
@given(st.lists(command_strategy(), max_size=20))
def test_commands_are_invertible(cmds):
    wf0 = example_workflow(); wf = wf0
    inverses = []
    for c in cmds:
        inverses.append(c.invert(wf)); wf = c.apply(wf)
    for inv in reversed(inverses):
        wf = inv.apply(wf)
    assert wf == wf0

docs.text: Gate Command Python lint & format uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . Python types uv run pyright (standard mode, 0 errors) Import boundaries (M3+) uv run lint-imports TS types pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json Tests uv run pytest -q, pnpm test, pnpm exec playwright test Generated code tests run ruff via generate() and pyright on a generated sample Dependencies pip-audit / pnpm audit --prod (M8)

docs.title: 8. Performance tests
docs.text:
• Validator: 200-node IR validates < 150 ms (pytest-benchmark).
  • Canvas: 500 nodes pan/zoom at 60 fps (Playwright + performance.now() sampling) — M2 stretch goal.
  • Runner: k6 script with 200 concurrent SSE runs using the fake backend (M8-T5): infra/load/runs.js against compose prod with the infra/load/compose.load.yml overlay (demo models, dev sign-in):
docker compose -f infra/compose.prod.yml -f infra/load/compose.load.yml --env-file infra/.env.prod up -d
k6 run infra/load/runs.js            # VUS=200 HOLD=2m by default; fails on p95 first event ≥ 250 ms

Result (2026-10-05, 4 vCPU, 2 API replicas, Postgres 16, support_triage template): 5,875 runs, 0 failed; time to first event p50 42 ms, p95 89 ms, p99 321 ms; whole run p50 5.2 s, p95 6.5 s at 200 runs in flight (≈37 runs/s, CPU-bound: one run takes about 0.1 s alone). The first attempt failed (46 % of requests): each stream held a control-database connection until it ended and exhausted the pool (5 + 10). Since then a request gives its connections back once the response starts, the pool is configurable (AGENTCANVAS_DB_POOL_SIZE, AGENTCANVAS_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW), and checkpoints use a connection pool (AGENTCANVAS_PERSISTENCE_POOL_SIZE) instead of one shared connection.

docs.title: 9. Code review checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Does the change keep interpreter and generated code equivalent?
  • [ ] New config keys: optional ones read with .get() in templates?
  • [ ] Any eval, string-built SQL, secrets in logs? (must be no)
  • [ ] Side effects placed after approvals?
  • [ ] Errors surface to the UI as diagnostics or RUN_ERROR, not silent?
  • [ ] Tests at the right level; names describe behaviour.

docs.title: 09 — Deployment & Operations
docs.text:
Files referenced here are in the repository's infra/ folder: Dockerfile.api, Dockerfile.web, nginx.conf, compose.prod.yml, .env.prod.example, the Helm chart helm/agentcanvas/, and docker-compose.yml (development services only).

Verification status (S11): both images build, and compose.prod.yml comes up healthy with two API replicas behind nginx on Postgres; a run streams through nginx and both replicas serve. CI repeats this on every push (job images) and lints and renders the Helm chart.

docs.title: 1. Environments
docs.text: Env Purpose Data Models dev laptops docker-compose Postgres/Redis fake server or personal keys ci tests ephemeral Postgres service fake models only staging pre-release checks, demos managed Postgres (separate DB) real keys with low spend limits prod customers managed Postgres with PITR real keys, per-project secrets

docs.title: 2. Build images
docs.text:
# from the repository root
docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.api -t agentcanvas-api:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) apps/api
docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.web -t agentcanvas-web:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) .
  • API image: multi-stage (uv builds the virtualenv; the runtime stage has no build tools), runs as uid 10001, includes git for project workspaces, logs JSON, and exposes /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (the database and the run store answer; 503 otherwise). ruff is a runtime dependency: the code generator formats output with it. On SIGTERM uvicorn lets open streams finish for up to 30 s.
  • Web image: nginx (unprivileged, port 8080) serves the built app and proxies /api/ to $API_UPSTREAM (default http://api:8000) without buffering, so Server-Sent Events stream in real time. Hashed assets are cached for a year; the app shell is always revalidated.
  • Base images are pinned by digest in the Dockerfiles; Dependabot proposes new digests weekly. To build from a mirror, replace the exact reference with BuildKit: docker build --build-context 'python:3.12-slim@sha256:<digest>=docker-image://mirror.gcr.io/library/python@sha256:<digest>' … (same digest: the mirror serves the same image).

docs.title: 3. Single host: compose.prod.yml (small teams, staging)
docs.text:
cp infra/.env.prod.example infra/.env.prod      # fill in: database password, secret key, OIDC, provider keys
docker compose -f infra/compose.prod.yml --env-file infra/.env.prod up -d --wait

It runs Postgres (with pgvector), a one-shot migrate service (alembic upgrade head) that must succeed before any API replica starts, API_REPLICAS API containers (2 by default) sharing one workspaces volume, and the web container on WEB_PORT (8080). Put a TLS-terminating proxy (Caddy, Traefik or a cloud load balancer) in front of web and keep response buffering off for /api/*.

docs.title: 4. Kubernetes: the Helm chart
docs.text:
kubectl create secret generic agentcanvas-secrets \
  --from-literal=DATABASE_URL=postgresql://… --from-literal=AGENTCANVAS_SECRET_KEY=… \
  --from-literal=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=…
helm install agentcanvas infra/helm/agentcanvas \
  --set secrets.existingSecret=agentcanvas-secrets \
  --set config.oidc.issuer=https://login.example.com/realms/acme --set config.oidc.audience=agentcanvas-api \
  --set config.oidc.clientId=agentcanvas-web --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=agentcanvas.example.com
Object Notes Deployment …-api 2 replicas by default; startup and liveness probes on /healthz, readiness on /readyz; rolling updates never drop below the replica count; terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60 and a 5 s preStop so open streams can finish; non-root, all capabilities dropped Deployment …-web nginx; 2 replicas; proxies /api/ to the API service Job …-migrate-<revision> alembic upgrade head as a pre-install,pre-upgrade hook, so new API pods never start against an old schema PersistentVolumeClaim …-workspaces project workspaces (git) shared by every API replica: needs a ReadWriteMany storage class (EFS, Filestore, Azure Files, NFS); kept on uninstall Ingress routes everything to the web service; annotations turn proxy buffering off and allow hour-long streams NetworkPolicy …-api only the web pods reach the API port Secrets never in values: name an existing Secret (secrets.existingSecret), for example one synced by External Secrets

Several replicas are safe: runs persist in Postgres, a reconnecting client reads state via GET /v1/threads/{id}, so sticky sessions are not required. Each cron minute starts one run however many replicas tick: a scheduler claims the minute by moving the trigger's last_fired forward in a conditional update, and only the replica whose update matched starts the run.

Safe redeploy (FR-X-10). A rolling update never loses a run. On SIGTERM an API pod leaves the Service (preStop), uvicorn gives open streams 30 s, then the pod drains: /readyz answers 503 {"status":"draining"}, new runs get 503 with Retry-After: 5, and running runs get AGENTCANVAS_DRAIN_GRACE_S (20 s) to finish. Runs still going are stopped at their last checkpoint: they end interrupted with error code redeploy and run.handover set. Every replica looks for handed-over runs at startup and every AGENTCANVAS_HANDOVER_INTERVAL_S (10 s), claims each with a conditional update (one replica wins), and continues the conversation from its checkpoint on the version it was running. Keep 5 + 30 + drain grace below terminationGracePeriodSeconds (60) and compose's stop_grace_period (60 s). A step that was cut off runs again on the new pod, so steps with side effects should be idempotent (the same rule as retries). A pod killed without draining (OOM, a lost node) cannot hand its runs over, so each replica refreshes the heartbeat of its running runs on every hand-over tick; a run still running without a heartbeat for AGENTCANVAS_ORPHAN_AFTER_S (60 s) is marked interrupted and handed over the same way.

Publishing over running conversations. A deployment's conversations continue on its newest version only when that version can resume them: every state field keeps its type and reducer and every pause point (approval, human input, tool approval) keeps its step name and kind. Otherwise a conversation finishes on the version it started on (run.workflow_version_id shows which), and new conversations get the new version.

Client addresses. The audit log records the caller's IP from X-Forwarded-For only when the direct peer is a trusted proxy: set FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (uvicorn) to the proxies' addresses. The chart and compose.prod.yml use * because only the web pods can reach the API: the chart adds a NetworkPolicy that admits only them (networkPolicy.enabled), and compose publishes no API port. If you turn the policy off or expose the API another way, list the proxies instead.

docs.title: 5. Configuration & secrets in production
docs.text:
• Required env: AGENTCANVAS_ENV=prod, DATABASE_URL, AGENTCANVAS_SECRET_KEY (64+ random chars), LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY (encrypts checkpoints; with it set, use EncryptedSerializer.from_pycryptodome_aes() as the checkpointer serde), AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE=oidc with AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_ISSUER, AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_AUDIENCE and AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, AGENTCANVAS_CORS_ORIGINS. The API refuses to start in staging, prod or the hosted edition with AUTH_MODE=dev.
  • Sign-in (M7-T1). Register a public SPA client at your identity provider with redirect URI https://<app>/auth/callback and post-logout URI https://<app>/; the web app uses authorization code + PKCE. The API checks the access token's signature (JWKS from the issuer's discovery document, or AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_JWKS_URL), iss, aud and exp. The default scopes (AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_SCOPES) include offline_access, so the client gets a refresh token and renews the access token silently; allow refresh tokens for the client at the provider (or drop the scope to fall back to a hidden-iframe renewal, which browsers that block third-party cookies break). Optional: AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_EMAIL_CLAIM, AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_TRUST_EMAIL=true for providers that send no email_verified but own the email domain.
  • Database connections per API process: the control database pool keeps AGENTCANVAS_DB_POOL_SIZE (10) open and opens up to AGENTCANVAS_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW (20) more; checkpoints and memory use their own pool of AGENTCANVAS_PERSISTENCE_POOL_SIZE (20). Size Postgres max_connections (or PgBouncer) for replicas × (pool + overflow + persistence pool) plus migrations. Requests give their connection back when the response starts, so open streams hold none (M8-T5: 200 concurrent streams on two replicas, p95 time to first event 89 ms).
  • First admin. List one or more emails in AGENTCANVAS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAILS (JSON list); on their first verified sign-in they become admins of the default organisation (once: an admin removed later is not re-added). With sign-in on, the seeded development user loses its memberships at startup. Admins then invite everyone else from the Members page (PUT /v1/org/members).
  • Roles (M7-T3): viewer reads; reviewer also answers the Inbox; builder also builds, runs and publishes; admin also manages members and reads the audit log (GET /v1/org/audit, M7-T4).
  • Policies (FR-X-19). Admins add organisation rules on the Policies page (/v1/org/policies). A rule picks steps, resources or the whole workflow (scope, narrowed by a CEL match) and states what must hold (require, CEL). CEL sees node (type, config, effects with effect/gated, ungated, models, tools), resource (type, config, used_by), workflow (nodes, resources, node_types, models) and env. Examples: node.effects.all(e, e.effect != "external_write" || e.gated); for scope=resource, match: resource.type == "model.chat", require: resource.config.model in ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5"] with environments: ["prod"]. Rules without environments apply in the editor and at every publish; rules with environments block publishing there and show as warnings in the editor. A rule that cannot be evaluated counts as broken. Steps and resources inside subgraphs are checked as well.
  • Long-term memory per organisation. Runs keep memories under the workflow's organisation (namespaces start with org:<id>), and the Memory inspector works inside the caller's organisation. On upgrade from v0.1.0, existing memories move to the default organisation once, at the first start; the API records that and never moves memories again. Deployment API end users are kept as api:<deployment>:<user_id>, apart from organisation members.
  • Model provider keys are per project secrets (M5-T6), not process env vars.
  • Secrets at rest (envelope encryption). Project secrets and webhook signing secrets are encrypted with a random data key per organisation; the data key is stored wrapped by the master key in AGENTCANVAS_KMS_KEY: file:/run/secrets/master.key (32+ random characters), aws:<key ARN> (install boto3), gcp:<key resource name> (install google-cloud-kms), or empty to derive it from AGENTCANVAS_SECRET_KEY (development). Rotate the master key without downtime: deploy with the new key in AGENTCANVAS_KMS_KEY and the old one in AGENTCANVAS_KMS_PREVIOUS_KEYS (JSON list), run python -m agentcanvas.security.kms rewrap once (it also moves secrets written before v0.3.0 onto the data keys), then remove the old key.
  • Checkpoints at rest. Set LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY (exactly 32 characters) to encrypt conversation checkpoints with AES; checkpoints written before stay readable. The API logs checkpoints.unencrypted at startup in staging and prod without it.
  • Browser policy. The web image sends a Content-Security-Policy; sign-in calls the identity provider, so its origin (taken from OIDC_ISSUER, which compose and the chart pass from the API settings) is allowed in connect-src. If the token or keys endpoints live on another host, list those origins in CSP_CONNECT_SRC (chart: web.cspConnectSrc).
  • Rate limits. nginx limits the public deployment and webhook endpoints to 20 requests/s per client address (bursts of 40, then 429). The API also limits each caller per minute, counted in the database so the limits hold across replicas: AGENTCANVAS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_DEPLOYMENT (120, per API key), AGENTCANVAS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_WEBHOOK (120, per trigger) and AGENTCANVAS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_PROJECT (600, all of a project's deployments and webhooks together); AGENTCANVAS_RATE_LIMIT_BY_ENVIRONMENT overrides the per-key limit for a deployment environment (JSON, e.g. {"dev": 30}); 0 turns a limit off. Over a limit the API answers 429 with Retry-After.

docs.title: 6. Observability
docs.text:
• Logs: JSON (structlog) to stdout in the images; ship with your platform's collector. Fields: request_id, workflow_id, thread_id, run_id, level, event, and trace_id / span_id inside a traced request.
  • Metrics: Prometheus at GET /metrics on each API pod (AGENTCANVAS_METRICS_ENABLED, on by default). The web image's nginx answers 404 for /api/metrics, so scrape the pods directly; the Helm chart adds prometheus.io/* pod annotations and lets the monitoring namespace through its NetworkPolicy (observability.metrics.*).
Metric Labels Meaning agentcanvas_runs_started_total origin (user, trigger, event, test, api…) runs started agentcanvas_runs_finished_total origin, status (success, interrupted, error, cancelled) runs finished or paused agentcanvas_run_duration_seconds status histogram of run duration agentcanvas_runs_active runs in progress in this pod agentcanvas_tokens_total / agentcanvas_cost_usd_total direction model usage and cost agentcanvas_sse_clients open run event streams agentcanvas_http_requests_total / agentcanvas_http_request_duration_seconds method, route (template, never ids), status HTTP traffic agentcanvas_online_score_mean deployment, evaluator mean online score over the evaluator's alert window (S13) agentcanvas_eval_alert_open deployment, evaluator, kind (below, drop) 1 while a drift alert is open; every pod refreshes it from the database once a minute agentcanvas_eval_alerts_total kind drift alerts opened
  • Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for FastAPI, the control database (SQLAlchemy) and outgoing httpx calls when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set (OTLP/HTTP; the standard OTEL_* variables configure it; Helm: observability.otlpEndpoint). Request spans carry request.id. LLM traces go to LangSmith when LANGSMITH_TRACING=true (runs tagged with workflow_id).
  • Dashboard and alerts: infra/observability/grafana-dashboard.json (import it and pick the Prometheus data source) and infra/observability/alerts.yaml: server errors above 5 % for 10 min, more than 20 % of runs failing, API p95 above 2 s (streams excluded), no API pod scraped, and an online evaluator in drift for 5 min (AgentCanvasEvaluationDrift, severity ticket).
  • Online evaluation (S13). Scoring of sampled deployment runs happens in each API pod after the response is sent (at 30 requests/s with every run scored, p95 rose from 42 to 52 ms on compose prod; lower the sampling rate for heavy traffic or LLM judges); an LLM judge's calls use the project's model keys and their cost is reported apart from run cost (the Production tab). LangSmith dataset sync uses the project secret LANGSMITH_API_KEY, else the server's environment variable of that name, and LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT for a self-hosted LangSmith.

docs.title: 7. Backups, retention, disaster recovery
docs.text:
• Retention (M8-T4). A job in every API pod deletes conversations (threads with their checkpoints, runs and decisions) that have been inactive longer than the organisation keeps them: PUT /v1/org/settings {"retention_days": 30} (admin; null = the server default AGENTCANVAS_RETENTION_DAYS, 90; 0 = keep forever). Conversations that are running or waiting for a person are never deleted. It checks every AGENTCANVAS_RETENTION_INTERVAL_S (1 h) and counts deletions in agentcanvas_threads_expired_total. The same job deletes audit-log rows older than AGENTCANVAS_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (400; 0 keeps them forever) and, only when AGENTCANVAS_MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS is set (off by default), long-term memories (and Deep Agent store files) not updated for that many days, in every organisation. Otherwise erase memories from the Memory inspector.
  • Managed Postgres: turn on point-in-time recovery (7 days or more). Restoring to a point in time is the provider's operation; then point DATABASE_URL at the restored instance and roll the API pods (the migration hook runs first).
  • Portable copy: infra/scripts/backup.sh writes a pg_dump (custom format) of the whole database: control tables, checkpoints and long-term memory. Run it nightly and keep the files off the database host. Workspaces live on their own volume (/data/workspaces, git repositories): back that volume up with your platform's snapshots.
  • Restore runbook (rehearsed on compose prod, 2026-10-05: a conversation deleted after the backup came back with its state; about 11 s for a small database):
  • ENV_FILE=infra/.env.prod infra/scripts/restore.sh <file.dump>. This stops web and api, recreates the database from the dump, runs migrations (a backup from an older release is brought up to date), and starts the API and web again.
  • Check GET /readyz, sign in, and open a recent conversation.
  • Runs that were in progress when the backup was taken show as running; cancel or resume them from the Run panel.
  • Drill quarterly: restore into a scratch environment, run the smoke checks above and record how long it took.

docs.title: 8. Release process
docs.text:
1. Merge to main → CI builds images tagged with the commit SHA.
  2. Deploy to staging automatically; run Playwright smoke tests against staging.
  3. Tag vX.Y.Z → promote the same images to prod (no rebuild); migrations run first.
  4. Rollback = redeploy the previous image tag; migrations must be backward compatible for one release (expand → migrate → contract).

docs.title: 9. Runbooks (write these in M8)
docs.text: Situation First steps Runs stuck "running" graceful restarts hand runs over (FR-X-10, §4); runs of a pod that was killed (OOM, node loss) are taken over by another pod after AGENTCANVAS_ORPHAN_AFTER_S (60 s) without a heartbeat (S12). If they stay running, check that at least one API pod is up, then cancel them from the Run panel SSE shows nothing until the end a proxy is buffering: check ingress/nginx proxy_buffering off, header X-Accel-Buffering: no DB connection exhaustion lower pool size per replica; check long transactions; add PgBouncer. LangGraph's AsyncPostgresSaver.from_conn_string already connects with autocommit=True, prepare_threshold=0 (no prepared statements, verified in source), so transaction pooling works for checkpoints; if you build your own psycopg pool for the saver, use the same three settings (autocommit=True, prepare_threshold=0, row_factory=dict_row). For SQLAlchemy + asyncpg behind transaction pooling set connect_args={"statement_cache_size": 0}. Model provider outage enable fallback models (ModelFallbackMiddleware) in affected workflows; show provider status banner Evaluation drift alert open the workflow's Evaluation page → Production: compare the hourly mean with the 7-day trend, open the lowest-scoring runs (their timelines are one click away), and send them to an annotation queue; a recent publish or a model provider change is the usual cause. The alert resolves by itself once the window's mean recovers Leaked secret revoke at provider, rotate secret in project, audit audit_log for secret.read events

docs.title: 10 — Security Checklist
docs.text: Use as a gate: M6 (MVP) must pass all P0 items; M8 all items. Each item says how to verify.

docs.title: 1. Code execution
docs.text: # Item Verify Pri S1 No eval/exec on user input; conditions via CEL, templates via SandboxedEnvironment grep -rn "eval(\|exec(" apps/api returns nothing in request paths; tests try {{ ''.__class__ }} and expect an error P0 S2 Hosted mode runs scripts in the Docker sandbox: --network none, read-only FS, CPU/memory/time limits, non-root test script opening a socket fails; infinite loop killed at timeout P0 (hosted) S3 Workspace file API blocks path traversal (resolve() stays under root) tests with ../, absolute paths, symlinks P0 S4 Custom tools/nodes imported only from the project workspace; no arbitrary import_path outside allowed packages (scripts., tools., examples.) validator rule rejects os:system P0 S5 Generated code never contains secrets test: generate with secret refs, grep output P0

docs.title: 2. Agent & tool safety
docs.text: # Item Verify Pri S6 Tools that change external state default to approval (approve_tools, MCP destructive_hint) validator W002 on missing approval P0 S7 HTTP tool domain allow-list; no access to metadata IPs (169.254.169.254) or private ranges unless allowed tests with blocked hosts P0 S8 Call limits in templates (ModelCallLimitMiddleware, ToolCallLimitMiddleware) and recursion limit loop test hits limit P1 S9 PII middleware available and documented; traces can mask inputs/outputs test redaction P1 S10 Memory writes from untrusted content are tagged and reviewable (doc08/09) post-MVP P2

docs.title: 4. Authentication & authorisation

docs.title: 6. Supply chain & operations
docs.text: # Item Verify Pri S25 Lockfiles committed (uv.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml); CI installs with --frozen CI config P0 S26 Dependency audit in CI (pip-audit, pnpm audit --prod), Dependabot/Renovate CI P1 S27 Containers run as non-root, minimal base images, image scanning (Trivy) CI P1 S28 Audit log for edits, publishes, approvals, secret access tests P1 (M7) S29 Data retention & deletion (threads, checkpoints, traces) documented and automated job exists P1 S30 Rate limits on run creation and webhooks per project/key load test P1

docs.title: 7. Review at the end of S11 (M8-T6, 2026-10-06)
docs.text:
Every item was checked against the code; tests named here run in CI (apps/api/tests/). No open P0 item. Items marked Partial keep a follow-up in the S12 backlog (13-sprint-plan.md).

docs.title: 11 — Troubleshooting & FAQ
docs.text: Every entry marked ✅ was reproduced during the review with the pinned versions (01 §1).

docs.title: A. LangChain / LangGraph
docs.text:
P-01 ✅ NotImplementedError from bind_tools in tests. LangChain's GenericFakeChatModel does not implement tool binding, and agents call bind_tools(). Use agentcanvas.testing.ToolFakeModel (overrides bind_tools to return itself).

P-02 ✅ ValueError: No generations found in stream. Happens when the run streams tokens (stream_mode contains "messages") and a fake model returns a message that has only tool calls (no text). Create fakes with disable_streaming=True (done by agentcanvas.testing.scripted).

P-03 ✅ Approvals repeat forever / the agent re-asks after I approved (tests & fake server). Scripted fakes are stateful. If the resume builds new fake models, the script restarts and the model re-issues the tool call. Give each thread its own Resources (resources_factory(thread_id)). Real models are stateless and not affected.

P-04 ✅ RedisSearchError … unknown command 'FT.INFO'. langgraph-checkpoint-redis needs RediSearch + RedisJSON. Use Redis 8 (modules built in) or Redis Stack, not Redis 7. Check with redis-cli MODULE LIST.

P-05 ✅ LangChainBetaWarning: The v3 streaming protocol on Pregel is experimental. Use graph.astream(..., version="v2") (stable typed parts {"type","ns","data"}) as the reference does. Revisit v3 when it is stable.

P-06 ✅ Code before interrupt() runs twice. On resume LangGraph re-runs the interrupted node from the start; interrupt() then returns the resume value. Move side effects (emails, DB writes, payments) into a node after the approval node. Validator rule E070 flags risky patterns.

P-07 ✅ GraphRecursionError: Recursion limit of N reached without hitting a stop condition. A loop has no exit or the router never takes it. Add a counter + router exit (tutorial Part 10) or raise recursion_limit in the run config for legitimately long workflows.

P-09 ✅ ValueError: Node timeouts are only supported for async nodes … (v0.6). LangGraph cancels timed-out attempts with asyncio, so timeout= only works on async def nodes. Every AgentCanvas node builder returns an async callable; wrap sync user code with await asyncio.to_thread(fn, state) — interrupt(), get_config() and get_store() still work inside it (context is copied).

P-10 ✅ ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastmcp' when importing langchain.mcp (v0.6). Install LangChain with the MCP extra: uv add "langchain[mcp]". The namespace is beta and emits LangChainBetaWarning on import.

P-11 ✅ TypeError: object method can't be used in 'await' expression with v3 event streaming (v0.6). In async code the v3 run stream's output is a method: await run.output(). (The docs' sync examples use a property.) The product keeps v2 until v3 is stable (P-05).

P-12 ✅ Old threads become unreadable after changing a channel to/from DeltaChannel (v0.6). Delta and non-delta representations are not interchangeable for persisted threads, and deepagents ≥ 0.6 already stores messages/files as delta channels. Never flip a channel's storage mode on a published workflow with live threads (validator E074), and never downgrade deepagents across 0.6.

P-13 ✅ KeyError: 'checkpoint_ns' from AsyncSqliteSaver.aput_writes when editing a past checkpoint (Sprint 2). graph.aupdate_state(config, …) with a checkpoint_id but no checkpoint_ns in configurable fails on the SQLite saver (Postgres/memory tolerate it). Always send {"thread_id": …, "checkpoint_id": …, "checkpoint_ns": ""} for past checkpoints — the LangChain adapter does this in _config().

P-14 ✅ NotImplementedError from checkpointer.acopy_thread(...) (Sprint 2). The method exists on BaseCheckpointSaver but InMemorySaver, AsyncSqliteSaver and AsyncPostgresSaver do not implement it (langgraph-checkpoint, 2026-09). AgentCanvas copies threads through the public saver contract (alist → aput + aput_writes, ids and namespaces preserved) in adapters/langchain/persistence.py:copy_thread; a canary test tells us when upstream implements it.

P-15 ✅ A node's error_handler does not run; the run fails with the original exception (Sprint 2). In langgraph 1.2.12, node-level error handlers are bypassed when streaming with stream_mode containing "messages" or "custom", or with subgraphs=True (they work with invoke, "updates", "tasks", "values"). Verified for raised exceptions and NodeTimeoutError. Workaround in the runner: workflows that declare an error route stream with ["tasks", "updates"] only (no token streaming) and emit CUSTOM ac.warning tokens_disabled. The strict-xfail canary tests/test_upstream_canaries.py turns red when upstream fixes it.

P-16 ✅ Please remove duplicate middleware instances. when building an agent (Sprint 5). create_agent rejects two middleware with the same .name. Names include a key for some types (PIIMiddleware[email], ToolCallLimitMiddleware[send_email]) but not for others (two ModelCallLimitMiddleware clash). Deep Agents (deepagents 0.7) already contain SummarizationMiddleware in their base stack, so wiring a Summarization widget into a Deep Agent fails the same way. Planning (TodoListMiddleware) is no longer in the Deep Agent base stack — the widget's "Planning" toggle adds it, so a separate To-dos widget would clash. Validator E035 reports all three cases before a run.

P-17 ✅ Structured output: the tool name changes between runs, or a scripted test cannot answer it (Sprint 5). With a JSON-Schema response_format that has no title, LangChain names the structured-output tool response_format_<random>. AgentCanvas always sets a title (the schema's, or <node>_output) so generated code, traces and tests are deterministic. The agent writes the result to structured_response; declare that channel (validator E021 says so).

P-18 ✅ A per-user memory folder fails after an approval with "needs the run's user" (Sprint 5). LangGraph does not checkpoint Runtime.context: every invocation (start, resume, continue, fork) must pass it again. The runner stores each run's context on the run row and reuses the thread's last context for resume/continue/decisions and the source thread's for forks — so a reviewer approving someone else's run never becomes the run's user (the /memories/ namespace stays the requester's).

P-19 ✅ TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "str") to list in a map worker (Sprint 5). operator.add as the append reducer rejects single values, and most widgets (LLM call, Set values) write one value. AgentCanvas's append reducer wraps non-list writes into a one-item list; a map worker can write its result straight into an append channel (E022 requires one: parallel workers writing a replace channel would raise P-10).

P-20 ✅ MCP: "A string target must be an http(s) URL" / tools stop working after the adapter closes? (Sprint 6). langchain.mcp.MCPAdapter (beta) refuses string targets that are not http(s) URLs — fastmcp.Client would otherwise treat a string naming an existing file as a local script and launch it. AgentCanvas always passes an explicit transport (StreamableHttpTransport(url, headers=…), or StdioTransport only when an admin allows local MCP, E042). Tools listed inside async with MCPAdapter(...) keep working after the context closes (each call reconnects), so tools are discovered once per graph build. Tool annotations (destructive_hint, read_only_hint) are in tool.metadata["mcp"]["tool"]["annotations"]; MCP tool results are content blocks with random ids — compare their text in tests.

P-21 ✅ store.asearch(ns, query="tea") returns everything (Sprint 6). Without a semantic index (index= on the store) the query is ignored. Memory Recall and search_memory fall back to keyword ranking over key + value; configure an embedding index for semantic recall.

P-22 ✅ Token usage attributed to the wrong node, or not priced (Sprint 6). Callback metadata carries the checkpoint namespace: a call inside an agent subgraph has checkpoint_ns = "agent:<id>|model:<id>" — the first segment is the canvas node. The model's own .metadata is merged into its callback metadata, so AgentCanvas tags each model with its catalog id (ac_model) to price usage; models whose catalog entry has no prices make the run cost "incomplete" (W015 for USD budgets).

P-08 ✅ Breakpoint run ends with no interrupts but the run is not finished. With interrupt_before/after, get_state().interrupts is empty and next holds the pending node. Treat next non-empty as "paused"; continue with ainvoke(None, config).

P-09 ✅ Router took the wrong branch after I edited old state. aupdate_state(checkpoint.config, values) records the edit as the node that produced that checkpoint, so routers after it are re-evaluated with the new values — that is expected (M4-T7). To avoid re-routing, edit a checkpoint after the router.

P-10 ✅ InvalidUpdateError: At key '…': Can receive only one value per step. Two parallel nodes wrote the same channel whose reducer is replace. Change the reducer to append/merge or write to different channels (validator E020).

P-11 KeyError in a node reading state. State is total=False: keys exist only after something wrote them. Use state.get("key") or give the channel a default via an initial Set node.

P-12 Agent node output is missing in the parent state. The agent subgraph shares only matching keys. The workflow state must have a messages channel with reducer add_messages (and structured_response if you use structured output).

P-23 ✅ LangSmith Sandboxes: every host reachable, or a memory change ignored (Sprint 7, SP-2). Without access_control a sandbox reaches every host on every port; AgentCanvas always sends an allow_list (empty = offline, plus port 443 for hosts that header rules target). update_sandbox(name, proxy_config=…) patches egress and injected headers in place, but the size (mem_bytes, vcpus) is fixed at creation — a new memory_mb replaces the sandbox. TTLs must be multiples of 60. Secrets go into opaque header values (write-only), never into the sandbox environment.

P-24 ✅ astream_events(version="v3"): "'async for' requires … got coroutine" (Sprint 8, SP-3). In LangGraph 1.2.x the v3 call is a coroutine: run = await graph.astream_events(x, cfg, version="v3"), then async for ev in run and await run.output() (a method). It is still marked experimental and its default stream has values events only; AgentCanvas keeps astream v2.

P-25 ✅ Agent Server: a graph factory is called with the wrong arguments (Sprint 8, SP-4). The server injects by type hint: annotate runtime: ServerRuntime (from langgraph_sdk.runtime) and/or config: RunnableConfig. String annotations (from __future__ import annotations) work if the name is importable in the module. Return the same topology for runs and introspection.

P-26 ✅ A LangChain callback collector only sees the root run (Sprint 8). collect_runs() / run_collector_var is a non-inheritable configure hook: child runs (graph nodes) never reach it. Assert node names through the canonical STEP events instead, or pass a handler in config["callbacks"].

docs.title: B. Templates & code generation
docs.text:
T-01 ✅ jinja2.exceptions.UndefinedError: 'dict object' has no attribute '<key>' during code generation. The template reads an optional config key with n.config.key. Use n.config.get("key", default) (StrictUndefined is intentional).

T-02 ✅ Generated strings contain '. You used | tojson for a Python literal. Use the py filter (repr).

T-03 ✅ pyright: function not assignable to StateNode parameter. Annotate node callables' state parameter as Any (the state type is built at runtime), not dict.

T-04 CompileError: generated code is not valid Python. The template produced a syntax error; the message contains ruff's error with a line number. Render without formatting (generate(wf, format_code=False)) to inspect the raw output.

docs.title: C. API & streaming
docs.text:
A-01 SSE events arrive all at once at the end. A proxy buffers the response. nginx: proxy_buffering off; (see reference/infra/nginx.conf); send header X-Accel-Buffering: no; Vite dev proxy streams correctly.

A-02 EventSource cannot POST. Correct — use fetch + ReadableStream (reference/web/src/sse.ts).

A-03 ✅ 404 thread not found after restarting the API (M0 reference). Workflows and the thread→workflow map are in memory in M0; ticket M1-T6 stores them in Postgres.

A-04 CORS errors in the browser. In development use the Vite proxy (/api → :8000) so the browser sees one origin. In production serve web and API behind the same host, or configure CORSMiddleware with explicit origins.

A-05 409 Conflict when saving. Someone (or another tab) saved first. Reload the workflow and re-apply; the canvas does this automatically (M2-T3).

docs.title: D. Environment
docs.text:
E-01 ✅ Postgres initdb: could not access directory … Permission denied. Run Postgres as a non-root user with a data directory that user owns — or use Docker (reference/infra/docker-compose.yml).

E-02 uv sync uses the wrong Python. uv python install 3.12; the project's requires-python = ">=3.12" makes uv pick it.

E-03 pnpm lockfile errors in CI. Commit pnpm-lock.yaml; install with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; use the same pnpm major version (10) locally and in CI.

E-04 Playwright cannot find a browser. Run npx playwright install chromium (or point executablePath at a system Chromium).

docs.title: F. Frontend (Sprint 3)
docs.text:
F-01 ✅ openapi-typescript crashes with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'createKeywordTypeNode'). It uses the TypeScript compiler's JavaScript API, which TypeScript 7 (native compiler) no longer ships. AgentCanvas generates API types from the OpenAPI component schemas with json-schema-to-typescript instead (apps/web/scripts/gen-api-types.mjs, pnpm gen).

F-02 ✅ Maximum update depth exceeded in React Flow's StoreUpdater. A prop derived on every render (e.g. new Map(...) of manifests, or a Zustand v5 selector returning a fresh array) re-triggers React Flow's store sync forever. Memoize derived collections (useMemo) and use useShallow (or a constant fallback like NONE) for selectors that build arrays.

F-03 ✅ [React Flow]: Couldn't create edge for source handle id: "model" (error 008) after a reload; edges missing. Handles that appear after a node's first render (ports known only once node-type manifests load, or a router gaining a route) are not measured. Render the canvas only after manifests are loaded, and call useUpdateNodeInternals()(id) when a node's handle set changes — but not on mount: re-measuring every node on mount is O(n²) (500 nodes: 5.9 s → 0.8 s load after the fix).

F-04 ✅ Initial view is zoomed in on part of the graph. <ReactFlow fitView> can fit before every node is measured. Fit once when useNodesInitialized() becomes true, with maxZoom: 1.

F-06 ✅ Ctrl/⌘-click or box selection keeps only one node selected (Sprint 6). Rebuilding React Flow nodes from the IR on every store change reset selected to the editor's single selected element. Merge React Flow's own selected flag into rebuilt nodes (the editor's selection is only ever added), and clear it explicitly when focusing a node from elsewhere.

F-07 ✅ An e2e drag sometimes creates no edge (Sprint 6). A content-sized node whose validation badge appears/clears after the server answers moves its handles between "measure" and "press". Keep node widths fixed (resource pills are 200 px) and wait for "Saved" before measuring handles in tests.

F-08 ✅ Playwright: "strict mode violation … resolved to 2 elements" for a button (Sprint 7). getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }) matches by substring, so a new "Save secret" button on the same page broke the workspace journey. Use { name: "Save", exact: true } for short labels. Run the whole e2e suite (not only the new spec) before pushing UI additions.

F-05 ✅ A renamed field (or values key) comes back after the edit is saved (Sprint 5). A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) merges nested objects, so sending a nested object wholesale keeps its old keys. diffToMergePatch must diff recursively and send null for removed nested keys. Coalescing queued edits needs the same care: mergePatch(p1, p2) drops the nulls of p2, and "delete, then set an object" has no single-patch equivalent — composePatches keeps nulls and refuses that case (the editor then queues both commands).

docs.title: E. Product questions
docs.text:
Why not use LangSmith Agent Server as the runtime? Self-hosting it in production needs a licence; the MVP needs a free local runtime and full control of events (review D-01). Publishing to LangSmith Deployment remains a target.

Why does generated code import agentcanvas.runtime.nodes? So canvas runs and exported code behave identically (ADR 0004). A fully inlined "eject" mode is planned (P2).

Can I add my own node types? Yes: follow 07-compiler-and-node-types.md; workspace-level custom nodes arrive in M5 (spec doc05).

docs.title: 13 — Sprint Plan (S0–S36) and Execution Log
docs.text: The milestone plan (04-implementation-plan.md) says what to build and in which order; this document time-boxes it into two-week sprints, slots in the v0.6 requirements (doc 15, FR-X) and the review fixes (doc 14), and records execution status.

docs.title: 1. Planning assumptions
docs.text:
Item Value Team 4 developers (backend, compiler/runtime, frontend, full-stack/DevOps) + part-time design & PM Sprint length 2 weeks (S0 is 1 week) Capacity 4 devs × 10 days × 0.7 focus ≈ 28 ideal days per sprint; plan to ≤ 24 (buffer for bugs/reviews) Estimates ticket estimates from build-guide/04 (ideal days for one developer) Repository this repository (ADR 0012): apps/api, apps/web, packages/ir-schema, infra/, docs/ Branching trunk-based, short-lived branches, Conventional Commits, CI green before merge (02 §7) Definition of Done build-guide/README §4 + "docs updated in the same PR" + "execution log below updated at sprint end" + "HANDOVER.md updated at sprint end"

Ceremonies: planning (day 1, 2 h), daily 15-min sync, backlog refinement (mid-sprint, 1 h), demo + retro (last day). Demo = the sprint's demo script below, run live against main.

Release trains: v0.1.0 (MVP) at end of S9; v0.2.0 (accounts) S10; v0.3.0 (production-ready) S11; GA features from S12.
