docs.title: S11 — Production readiness → v0.3.0
docs.text:
M8-T1 containers (2) · M8-T2 Helm/compose prod (3) · M8-T3 observability (3) · M8-T4 backups & retention (2) · M8-T5 load test (2) · M8-T6 security review (3) · FR-X-10 safe redeploy (3).

Goal: one team can run AgentCanvas for real users on their own infrastructure: several API replicas behind nginx, a managed Postgres, metrics and traces, tested backups, and redeploys that do not break running work.

Backlog (planned at the end of S10, 2026-10-05). Branch claude/sprint-11-production-readiness, in #4.

# Item Acceptance Est. 1 M8-T1 Containers docker build of infra/Dockerfile.api and Dockerfile.web succeeds in CI; images run as a non-root user; nginx streams SSE unbuffered (/api/v1/**/stream, /runs/*/events) and serves the SPA with long-lived caching for hashed assets only. 2 2 M8-T2 Compose prod & Helm infra/compose.prod.yml (api ×2, web, Postgres, Redis, migrations as a one-shot job) comes up healthy; Helm chart in infra/helm/agentcanvas (api Deployment with N replicas, web, migration Job, Ingress, Secret refs, probes) passes helm lint and helm template in CI. /readyz pings the database and the persistence store; /healthz stays a cheap liveness check. 3 3 Leader lock for schedulers (carried over) With two API replicas each cron schedule fires once: the scheduler loop takes a Postgres advisory lock (no-op on SQLite) and hands over within one tick when the leader stops. 1 4 M8-T3 Observability OpenTelemetry traces for FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and httpx when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set; /metrics (Prometheus) with runs started/finished by status, run duration, node errors, tokens and cost, SSE subscribers; a Grafana dashboard JSON in infra/observability/. Request ids appear in logs and spans. 3 5 M8-T4 Backups & retention Retention setting per organisation (default 90 days) and a daily job deleting older threads with adelete_thread plus their rows; restore runbook (Postgres PITR) in the docs, rehearsed once against compose prod. 2 6 FR-X-10 Safe redeploy On SIGTERM the API stops taking runs, lets running ones reach a superstep boundary, marks them interrupted and exits; another replica resumes them. A publish that changes a deployment's version resumes pinned threads on the new version only when the resume-compatibility check passes (same pause points and state channels); otherwise they finish on the version they started on. 3 7 M8-T5 Load test k6 script in infra/load/: 200 concurrent streaming runs on fake models against compose prod; p95 event latency < 250 ms; the result recorded in this log. 2 8 M8-T6 Security review 10-security-checklist.md completed with evidence links; dependency and container scanning (pip-audit, pnpm audit, Trivy) in CI; findings fixed or ticketed. 3 9 KMS envelope encryption for secrets (carried over) Secrets encrypted with a per-organisation data key wrapped by a KMS key (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / local key file for dev); a re-wrap command rotates the master key without downtime. 2 10 S10 review carry-overs Invitations need the invitee's acceptance when they already belong to another organisation, and member lists show no profile details before that; the default organisation is the one used last (not the first by id); the web app refreshes tokens silently (offline_access) and reads its project per request instead of at module load; FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS documented for the proxy in front of the API. 2

Load: 23 days (≤ 24). If the sprint runs long, KMS (item 9) moves to S12 first, then the Grafana dashboard.

Order: containers and compose prod first (everything else is tested against them), then the leader lock, observability and safe redeploy, then retention, load test and the security review at the end.

Demo script: docker compose -f infra/compose.prod.yml up; sign in; start a long run; restart one API replica mid-run and watch it finish on the other; open the Grafana dashboard; show the k6 report and the completed security checklist.

Exit: compose prod and the Helm chart deploy cleanly; the load test meets its target; no open high-severity security finding; tag v0.3.0 (maintainer's call).

Review (2026-10-06). All ten items met their acceptance; the evidence is in the execution log below and in 10-security-checklist.md §7. Item 3 needed no advisory lock: claiming each minute with a conditional update of trigger.last_fired works on SQLite and Postgres alike. The load test found that every open stream held a database connection; requests now release their sessions once the response starts. Deviations and gaps, all carried into S12 unless noted: - script-src keeps 'unsafe-eval' (Ajv compiles schemas at runtime). - Rate limits are per client address in nginx only, not per API key or project in the API (S30 partial). - Trace payloads to LangSmith/OTel are not masked (S9 partial); audit-log and memory retention are missing (S29 partial). - An instance killed without a graceful shutdown leaves its runs running; nothing sweeps them. - Base images are not pinned by digest; the workspace path test has no symlink case. - Webhook signatures changed format (timestamped), a breaking change called out in the changelog. - Not carried: AWS/GCP KMS adapters are tested with fakes only (needs cloud accounts); the store is not encrypted (upstream); memory provenance tags (S10, P2) stay in the GA backlog.

docs.title: S12 — Evaluation Studio → v0.4.0
docs.text:
FR-EVAL-02 datasets (3) · FR-EVAL-03 evaluators (4) · FR-EVAL-04 experiments (4) · results UI (3) · FR-EVAL-05 release gate (2) · S11 follow-ups (7).

Goal: a builder can show, with numbers, that a new version of a workflow is better than the last one before it reaches prod: build a dataset from test cases and real runs, score versions with evaluators, compare them side by side, and have publishing to prod refuse a version that regresses.

Backlog (planned at the end of S11, 2026-10-06). Branch claude/sprint-12-evaluation-studio, in #5.

# Item Acceptance Est. 1 FR-EVAL-02 Datasets A dataset belongs to a workflow and holds examples (input, optional context, reference output, optional reference tool trajectory, split, metadata). Create from saved test cases, from selected past runs ("Add run to dataset"), or by importing CSV/JSONL (column mapping, validated against the workflow's input schema). Every change creates a new dataset version; experiments pin a version. Export as JSONL. Org-scoped, audited, role-checked like other resources. 3 2 FR-EVAL-03 Evaluators Evaluators per workflow: exact match, regex and JSON Schema on a channel; LLM-as-judge with a rubric, a model from the catalog and a 0–1 score with reasoning; trajectory match (tool sequence strict / unordered / subset); code evaluators from workspace evals/*.py run in the project's sandbox; each returns score, pass/fail at a threshold, and a comment. Uses openevals/agentevals where they fit. Unit-tested with fake models. 4 3 FR-EVAL-04 Experiments Run one or more workflow versions (or the draft) × a dataset version × optional variants (model or prompt override per resource) in the background with bounded concurrency, through the normal runner (mocks honoured, no triggers or event handlers). Each example result keeps the thread id, output, scores, tokens, cost and latency; aggregates per variant (mean score, pass rate, p50/p95 latency, cost). Cancellable; survives a redeploy through the existing handover. 4 4 Results UI Evaluation page per workflow: datasets (import, edit, versions), evaluators (configure, try on one example), experiments (start, progress, cancel). Results grid of examples × variants with scores, a diff of outputs, and a link to each run's timeline. Comparing two experiments shows per-evaluator deltas and which examples improved or regressed. 3 5 FR-EVAL-05 Release gate An environment can require a gating dataset and thresholds (minimum mean score per evaluator, maximum regression vs. the live version). Publishing there adds an "evaluation" checklist item that runs or reuses an experiment on the exact version and refuses when a threshold fails; admins can override with a reason, recorded in the audit log. 2 6 API rate limits per key and project (S11, S30) Deployment run creation and webhooks are limited per API key / trigger and per project, counted per minute in the control database so the limits hold across replicas (done instead of a Redis token bucket: compose prod and the chart have no Redis); 429 with Retry-After; limits configurable per environment. 2 7 Orphaned-run sweeper (S11) Runs still running whose instance stopped heartbeating are marked interrupted and resumed by the handover job; a heartbeat per instance; test kills an instance without draining. 1 8 Trace masking (S11, S9) Secret values and fields named in the workflow's trace policy are masked in LangSmith and OTel payloads; test with a known secret. 1 9 Audit-log and memory retention (S11, S29) Retention settings for the audit log (default 400 days) and long-term memory (off by default); the daily job deletes older rows; documented. 1 10 Drop 'unsafe-eval' (S11, S22) Form validation works under script-src 'self' (an interpreting validator or precompiled schemas); CSP updated; the e2e suite passes under the stricter policy. 1 11 Image digests and symlink test (S11, S27/S3) Base images in both Dockerfiles pinned by digest (Dependabot updates them); a workspace test proves a symlink cannot escape the root. 1

Load: 23 days (≤ 24). If the sprint runs long, the comparison view in item 4 and variant overrides in item 3 move to S13 first.

Order: S11 follow-ups that touch running systems first (sweeper, rate limits), then datasets → evaluators → experiments → results UI → release gate, then the CSP and image follow-ups.

Demo script: import a CSV of 20 questions into a dataset; add an LLM-as-judge and a trajectory evaluator; run an experiment comparing v1 and the draft with two models; open the grid and a regressed example's timeline; turn on the prod gate and watch publishing refuse the weaker version.

Exit: the demo works end to end on compose prod; the security checklist has no partial P1 left from S11 except the cloud-KMS live test; tag v0.4.0 (maintainer's call).

Review (2026-10-06). All eleven items met their acceptance; CI ran green on every push, including the digest-pinned images and the e2e suite on the production build under script-src 'self'. An end-of-sprint review (backend, gates and masking, web) found and fixed, before merge: - A builder could weaken an admin-only gate through what it measures with (delete the gating dataset, which cascaded to the gate, or lower an evaluator's threshold). Changing a gating dataset or an evaluator of a gated workflow now needs an admin. - Publishing pinned the draft as it was after the evaluation; it now refuses (409) when the draft or the workspace moved meanwhile. Evaluation reuse also requires the same workspace commit (new experiment.workspace_commit). - Examples whose run never started were left out of averages, so a gate could pass on the few that ran; they now score 0, and a gate fails when not every example finished. NaN scores counted as 1.0; they now count as unscored. - A pathological regex ((a+)+$) froze the API worker, its heartbeats and so its runs' leases: regexes run in a worker process with a 2 s limit; code evaluators time out after 60 s; a failing experiment cancels its examples. - Trying an evaluator used the default project's keys and code; masking missed run errors, span statuses and secrets that JSON escapes; the publish request held a database connection during the evaluation. - Web: switching experiments with an output diff open crashed the page; the new validator rejected Python-style regexes in custom-format fields and mis-placed errors for keys containing dots.

Deviations and gaps, carried into S13 unless noted: - settings.trace_redact covers each step's trace but not the graph's root run or model runs. - Run and experiment leases have no owner: an instance stalled for over 60 s can be taken over while it keeps going. - A gate measures with the dataset's latest version and the evaluators' current settings (protected by the admin rule above) rather than a snapshot. - Datasets are not synced to LangSmith; pairwise, composite and human-annotation evaluators (FR-EVAL-03) are not built. - Not carried: the experiment comparison uses each experiment's first target only (by design for now).

docs.title: S13 — Evaluation in production → v0.5.0
docs.text:
FR-EVAL-06 online evaluators (4) · annotation queues (3) · pairwise & composite evaluators (2) · FR-EVAL-08 rubric (3) · FR-EVAL-07 simulated users (3) · LangSmith dataset sync (2) · S12 follow-ups (3) · record/replay tool I/O (2).

Goal: quality is measured after release too. Production runs are sampled and scored, drops raise an alert, people review what the evaluators flag and turn it into dataset examples, and agents can grade and correct their own work before answering.

Backlog (planned at the end of S12, 2026-10-06). Built on branch claude/sprint-13-evaluation-in-production (#8) from main after #5.

# Item Acceptance Est. 1 FR-EVAL-06 Online evaluators Per deployment, attach evaluators with a sampling rate (0–100 %) and an optional filter (status, metadata); sampled finished runs are scored in the background after the response, never delaying it; scores stored per run and shown in the run list and timeline; daily and hourly aggregates per evaluator. A drift rule (mean below X, or Y points below the trailing 7-day mean) raises an alert in the app and on /metrics (Prometheus alert rule shipped). Judge cost counted separately from the run's cost. 4 2 Annotation queues A queue per workflow fed by rules (online score below a threshold, a failed run, a thumbs-down from the deployment API) or by hand from any run; reviewers (role reviewer+) see input, output and the timeline, give a score per rubric criterion and a comment, and can add the run to a dataset with a corrected reference in one step; queue progress and inter-reviewer agreement shown. Org-scoped, audited. 3 3 Pairwise & composite evaluators (FR-EVAL-03) A pairwise LLM judge compares two experiment targets per example (position-swapped to cancel order bias) and reports a win rate with a confidence interval in the comparison view; a composite evaluator combines others with weights or all/any rules. Both usable in experiments and release gates. 2 4 FR-EVAL-08 Rubric self-grading A Rubric widget on Deep Agent and agent nodes (deepagents RubricMiddleware: rubric text, grader model, max iterations, tools) authored in the inspector; grading iterations stream as ac.rubric events and appear live in the run panel and timeline; codegen and export carry it. 3 5 FR-EVAL-07 Simulated users For chat workflows, an experiment can drive a multi-turn conversation with a simulated user (persona, goal, max turns, stop condition) played by a catalog model; each conversation is one result with its full transcript, scored by evaluators that see every turn. 3 6 LangSmith dataset sync (FR-EVAL-02) Push a dataset version to LangSmith and pull one back (examples, splits, metadata) when a LangSmith key is configured; the link is shown on the dataset; sync is explicit, never automatic. 2 7 S12 follow-ups trace_redact also applied to the graph's root run and model runs (LangSmith and OTel); run and experiment leases get an owner, and a heartbeat that finds itself replaced stops its work; a release gate snapshots its dataset version and evaluator specs when an admin saves it. 3 8 Record/replay tool I/O (carried since S8) Recorded runs capture tool inputs and outputs, and replays return them instead of calling the tools again; covered for HTTP, MCP and workspace tools. 2

Load: 22 days (≤ 24). If the sprint runs long, simulated users (item 5) move to S14 first, then LangSmith sync.

Order: S12 follow-ups first (they touch the gate and leases), then online evaluators → annotation queues (fed by them) → pairwise/composite → rubric → simulated users, with LangSmith sync and record/replay alongside.

Demo script: publish a support agent with an online LLM judge at 50 % sampling; send 40 requests through the deployment API, a quarter of them off-topic; watch the hourly mean drop and the drift alert fire; open the annotation queue, correct two answers and add them to the gating dataset; turn on a rubric on the agent and watch it revise an answer live; run a pairwise comparison of the old and new prompt.

Exit: the demo works end to end on compose prod; online scoring adds no latency to deployment responses (p95 unchanged within noise on the load test); tag v0.5.0 (maintainer's call).

Review (2026-10-06). All eight items met their acceptance in the test suite (343 API tests, 59 web unit tests). An end-of-sprint review found and fixed, before merge: - Drift alerts stayed open forever once their online evaluator was deleted, or a rule was turned off; they are now resolved then, and every pod resolves alerts no online evaluator watches any more. - Scoring tasks or pods that saw a rule break at the same moment could each open an alert; a partial unique index (eval_alert_one_open) allows one open alert per deployment, evaluator and rule. - Runs stopped for a hand-over on a redeploy were scored (as interrupted) and then scored again when continued; resumed and continued runs were scored without their input and labels. Hand-over stops are no longer scored, and continuations are scored with the thread's last fresh input and labels. - A failed run sent to a queue by the "failed" rule showed reviewers no input; fresh failed runs now keep their input (not a full cassette: they still cannot become test cases or dataset examples directly). - "Add to dataset" committed the example before the review was saved, so a refused review could leave one behind; the review is saved first. Two reviews of one item at once could leave it pending; items are locked while counted. - Mirrored pairwise verdicts counted in each target's overall pass rate, which bent the gate's regression check; a pairwise verdict no longer decides whether an answer passed.

Demo on compose prod (2026-10-06), two API replicas with demo models (infra/load/compose.load.yml; no provider keys here, so a regex "stays on topic" evaluator stood in for the LLM judge). 40 requests through the deployment API at 50 % sampling, the off-topic quarter in the second half: no alert after the first 20, then 20 scored runs, hourly mean 0.65 and a below alert (agentcanvas_eval_alert_open = 1 on /metrics). Off-topic runs were queued (by hand for those scored before the queue existed, by the rule for later ones); two corrected answers became a new version of the gating dataset. The rubric ran a grading round live; the pairwise judge, the rubric grader and the simulated user need a real model, so with the demo model they ended unscored or as grader_error. The demo found one defect, fixed: a grader model that never returned a verdict looped for LangGraph's default ~10,000 steps and held the run; the grader now gets 25 steps and ends the round as grader_error.

Latency (exit criterion), infra/load/deployment.js against the API on the compose network, 30 requests/s for 60 s, every run scored (sampling 100 %), two rounds each: without online scoring p50 31/33 ms, p95 42/44 ms; with it p50 33/33 ms, p95 52/51 ms. The first measurement was p95 +15-25 ms; per-run drift checks (now at most every 10 s per evaluator and instance) and re-parsing the published workflow (now cached) were trimmed. Saturated (100 users back to back, CPU-bound) throughput drops from 69 to 54 runs/s at 100 % sampling, since scoring shares the API pods' CPU.

Deviations and gaps, carried into S14 unless noted: - Online scoring runs in the API pods (bounded to 4 tasks per pod), not in a separate worker: at 100 % sampling p95 rises about 8 ms below saturation and throughput drops at saturation. A separate scoring worker is the S14 option. - Simulated users run turn by turn on one thread; they do not branch or retry a turn. - Replayed MCP tools take any arguments (their schemas are not recorded), and a replayed run's thread state cannot be viewed while the MCP server is unreachable. - test_validation_of_200_nodes_is_fast (150 ms) failed once on a slow CI runner (473 ms) and passed on the next runs; watch it.

docs.title: S14 — AI Copilot I → v0.6.0
docs.text:
Before the sprint the whole codebase was reviewed (all gates green: API 364 passed; web 67 unit tests) and the review's findings were fixed first (see the S14 review below).

# Item Days Acceptance 1 Spike + eval harness 3 agentcanvas.copilot.evals: 10 plain-language build requests, each checked for a proposal that applies, validates without errors and uses the expected blocks; runs with any provider:model; CI runs it with a scripted model 2 Tool layer 4 copilot/tools.py: get_workflow, find_blocks, get_block, get_template, set_brief, propose_changes over the IR command API; proposals apply to a working copy only, failures come back to the model, secrets refused 3 Knowledge pack 2 copilot/pack.py generated from the registry (workspace blocks included) and templates plus a short guide; sent as a cacheable prefix 4 Copilot service 5 brief → plan → build loop with self-repair (copilot/service.py), SSE POST /v1/workflows/{id}/copilot/messages, conversations stored per person and workflow, prompt caching on Anthropic 5 Model setting 2 same model as the workflow or separate; tool-calling check; org model policies apply; token cap per conversation 6 Chat panel and brief card 3 Copilot tab, Build/Ask modes, live tool activity, brief card 7 Ghost proposals 4 proposal previewed read-only on the canvas (new green, changed amber); Accept = one undoable edit; Reject 8 Guardrails 1 Ask mode has read-only tools (viewers allowed); max 16 model calls per turn, 80 commands per proposal; workflow text marked as data; literal secrets refused; one turn at a time per conversation

Pre-sprint review (2026-10-07). A review of the whole codebase found 11 defects, all fixed before S14 work: two runs could start on one thread (double-clicked approvals; the thread slot is now taken before any await, and an inbox item is decided once, 409 after); event-handler resume used the wrong project's resources and could not resume deployment threads; an expired LangSmith sandbox was never replaced; secret masking missed values JSON escapes and the live ac.interrupt event; the editor's flush() returned while a save was in flight (a run could use a stale draft); the Memory page was 403 for non-admins; state edits and branch forks could change a thread with an active run; deleting a thread did not wait for its cancelled run; GET /runs/{id}/events sent 200 before a 404; a label with a newline could inject code into generated Python; signed webhooks could be replayed within the tolerance window (now 409, recorded in the shared dedup table).

Review (2026-10-07). Every item met its acceptance in the tests (test_copilot.py, e2e/copilot.spec.ts). Deviations and gaps: - The eval harness has not been run against a hosted model here (no provider keys in this environment); CI runs it with a scripted model. Run python -m agentcanvas.copilot.evals --model … before relying on a model. - Answers arrive per model turn, not token by token. - "One turn at a time per conversation" is enforced per API instance; two replicas could each take one message. - Removed elements are listed on the proposal card, not drawn as ghosts on the canvas.

docs.title: S16 — Any framework as a node → v0.10.0
docs.text:
# Item Days Acceptance 1 Wrapped agent step (agent.framework) 5 an agent from the Workspace built with OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, Agno, Strands, LlamaIndex Workflows, Microsoft Agent Framework or Claude Agent SDK (or a Python function) runs as one step in the interpreter and in generated code; prompt and output fields; factory per run; approval before it runs; ac.agent trace events; hosted edition refuses it (E041); exports install the pinned framework package 2 Remote agent (A2A) step 3 message/send to an Agent Card or endpoint; input-required pauses the run for a person and resumes the same task without sending twice; private addresses refused unless allowed; secret headers 3 MCP agent step 1 calls one tool of a wired mcp.server with templated arguments 4 Framework badge 1 each such block names its framework (or A2A, MCP) on the canvas 5 Open Agent Spec export and import 4 flows with LLM, agent, A2A, question and branching nodes, other steps as tools; an exact round trip of AgentCanvas files (layout included); import of any Agent Spec flow or agent with a report; Versions download and home-page import 6 Real-framework CI 2 a real agent of each framework at its pinned version runs as a step against a fake model server; exports load in pyagentspec 7 Docs 1 user guide section, changelog, handover

Review (2026-10-08). Before the sprint the deploy kit (S19) was reviewed: Azure deployed "unset" for empty settings, Cloud Run's service account could not read its secrets, and placeholder API keys counted as set; all fixed. Deviations from the plan: - The roadmap's "generated wrappers" are one generic step that calls each framework's own entry point (named in interop.FRAMEWORKS), not generated code per framework; the agent stays the user's own code in the Workspace. - Agent Spec files are JSON (YAML is not read); routers export as branches only for rules like state.x == "v" on one field, and agents' tools and middleware are not exported (both listed in the report). - The real-framework job uses a fake model server, so it proves the wiring, not model quality; the Claude Agent SDK runs its bundled CLI against the fake Anthropic API.

docs.title: S17 — Workspace and editor fixes → v0.11.0 (✅ done)
docs.text:
Reported by the owner on 2026-10-09. Causes marked (checked) were confirmed in the code; the others are the likely cause and are confirmed at the pre-sprint review.

# Item Role Days Acceptance 1 Way back from the Workspace F 1 Opening the Workspace from a block or the editor shows "Back to workflow name" and returns to the same workflow, selection and canvas position; the browser Back button does the same; the Workspace page shows which workflow it belongs to. (checked: /workspace is one route with no workflow in it, apps/web/src/app/App.tsx) 2 A workspace per workflow B, F 4 Each workflow has its own code folder (workflows/<workflow>/ with scripts/, tools/, nodes/, events/); a shared lib/ holds code several workflows use; existing projects migrate (current files move to lib/ so nothing breaks); import paths, the code editor's file tree, secrets and Copilot tools follow the workflow; versions pin the workflow's own code. (checked: one workspace per project today, workspace_commit is the project's head) 3 Exports bundle the right code B 2 An export contains the workflow's own folder, every lib/ module it imports (found by following imports, not by copying everything), data files under those folders and a requirements list the workflow's code declares; other workflows' code is left out; an export test fails if any import_path in the workflow cannot be imported inside the exported project. (checked: packager.py copies only scripts/ tools/ nodes/ events/ of the whole project, WORKSPACE_DIRS) 4 Copilot in the code editor B, F 4 In the Workspace editor: "Write with Copilot" turns a plain description into a function with the right signature for the block that uses it (script step, tool, custom block, event handler); "Explain" and "Fix" on the open file or a selected range, using the ruff markers; changes arrive as a diff to accept or reject, never written silently; starter snippets per file type for beginners; works with the workflow's Copilot model and its privacy mode 5 Every button labelled F 2 Icon-only buttons get visible text or a tooltip plus an accessible name; the list fields in block settings ("Tools that need approval" in the AI agent block and every other list) show "Add", "Remove", "Move up" and "Move down"; a new list item starts empty instead of null, so it no longer shows "Instance type null is invalid"; a Playwright check with axe's button-name rule runs on the editor, inspector, Workspace, Versions, Copilot and settings pages and fails on any unlabelled button. (likely cause: the settings form library's default list buttons use an icon font the app does not load) 6 Docs all 1 User guide Workspace page (per-workflow code, shared library, Copilot in the editor), changelog, handover

Demo: open the AI agent block, add a tool that needs approval with labelled buttons, open its code in the Workspace, write the tool with the Copilot, go back to the same spot on the canvas, export and run the export's tests.

Review (2026-10-09). The pre-sprint review confirmed every cause in the table, including the unlabelled list buttons (the settings form library's default buttons draw glyphicons, a font the app does not load, and a new list item started as null). It also found that workspace files could not import each other in the server process (from scripts.x import y failed outside the sandbox); fixed, so code imports the same way in a run and in an export. Deviations from the plan: - Shared code stays where it was (scripts/, tools/, nodes/, events/ at the workspace root) instead of moving to lib/: existing import paths keep working, so no migration is needed. A workflow's own code is in flows/<workflow id>/{scripts,tools,nodes}/, imported as flows.<id>.scripts.<file>:<function>. - Event handlers and secrets stay per project (an event can start any workflow); custom block types written in a workflow's folder are still registered for the whole project. - Editing a helper module does not reload the files that import it until they change too (the hot reload follows the file a step names). - The unlabelled-button check is a Playwright check written for the app (any visible button whose name has no letter or digit fails), not axe, to avoid a new dependency; it runs on every editor tab, dock panel and page. - Copilot code help uses the Copilot model and privacy settings of the workflow's project, like the chat.

docs.title: Spike SP-2 — LangSmith Sandboxes as the script runner
docs.text: Sprint S7 (time-boxed, 1 point) Question Can workspace code (script nodes, custom nodes, event handlers) run in a LangSmith Sandbox, with secrets injected by the auth proxy so they never enter the sandbox? Outcome Yes, behind a setting. AGENTCANVAS_SCRIPT_EXECUTION=langsmith is implemented and tested against a fake client. It has not yet run against the live service, because this environment has no LangSmith credentials. Latency and the open questions below need one session with a real key. Code apps/api/agentcanvas/sandbox/langsmith.py, sandbox/policy.py, sandbox/runners.py (SandboxRunner), tests/test_sandbox.py

docs.title: 1. The SDK surface (langsmith 0.14.1, verified by inspection)
docs.text:
• AsyncSandboxClient(api_endpoint=None, api_key=None, …). The key defaults to LANGSMITH_API_KEY and the endpoint to LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT.
  • create_sandbox(snapshot=…, name=…, idle_ttl_seconds=…, delete_after_stop_seconds=…, mem_bytes=…, proxy_config=…) returns an AsyncSandbox. It waits until the sandbox is ready. Both TTLs must be multiples of 60.
  • update_sandbox(name, proxy_config=…) patches the proxy in place. Access-control changes apply immediately. Size (vcpus, mem_bytes, fs_capacity_bytes) cannot be updated.
  • The AsyncSandbox methods are:
  • write(path, bytes|str)
  • read(path)
  • run(command, timeout=int, cwd=…, env=…), which returns ExecutionResult(stdout, stderr, exit_code) or raises CommandTimeoutError
  • delete_sandbox(name) and aclose().
  • proxy_config has three parts:
  • rules: header rules shaped {name, match_hosts, match_paths, headers: [{name, type, value}]}. The header type is workspace_secret ({NAME}), plaintext or opaque. opaque is write-only and encrypted at rest. Rules can also be of type aws or gcp.
  • access_control: {allow_list: [...]} (default-deny) or {deny_list: [...]}.
  • callbacks.
  • Default egress is allow-all when there is no access_control. This confirms review item V-11c. Organisations on restricted egress have their allow-list replaced by the org policy.

docs.title: 2. Design
docs.text:
SandboxRunner (one per project, from the ProjectRegistry)
  ├─ subprocess / docker → a child process per call (unchanged)
  └─ langsmith → LangSmithBox (one sandbox per project, created lazily)
        create_sandbox(snapshot, mem_bytes, idle TTL, proxy_config = policy + secrets)
        write /sandbox/child.py                     (the same stdlib child as the local modes)
        write /sandbox/ws.tgz + tar -x into /ws     (only when a workspace file changed)
        per call: write /sandbox/in-<id>.json; run `python3 -I /sandbox/child.py IMPORT < in.json` in /ws
  • One warm sandbox per project, not one per call.
  • Creating a sandbox boots a VM and waits until it is ready. That cost is acceptable once, but not on every node execution.
  • Calls reuse the sandbox and differ only by their input file.
  • The workspace is uploaded as a single archive, which takes one write and one run. It is re-uploaded only when the files' mtimes change.
  • Same child protocol in every mode. child.py is stdlib-only. It prints the result as the last line on stdout and sends user prints to stderr, so result parsing (_parse) is shared by every mode.
  • Secrets never enter the sandbox.
  • Header values in the policy reference project secrets as {{ secret.NAME }}.
  • Those values are sent to LangSmith as opaque headers. The proxy injects them into matching HTTPS requests from outside the sandbox.
  • The sandbox receives no environment variables from us. The test asserts that neither the uploaded files nor the environment contain the value.
  • Policy or secret change → update_sandbox; size change → a new sandbox. The proxy config is fingerprinted, including secret values, without logging them.
  • Offline by default. An empty egress sends access_control.allow_list = []. Hosts named in inject rules are added on port 443, because an allow-list must include the hosts that rules target.
  • No leaks after a crash. Sandboxes stop after AGENTCANVAS_LANGSMITH_IDLE_S (600 s) of inactivity and are deleted 600 s later. ProjectRegistry.aclose() deletes them at API shutdown.

docs.title: 3. Sandbox policy (FR-X-08, basic)
docs.text:
The policy is the file sandbox.json at the workspace root. It is versioned like the rest of the code:

{
  "egress": ["pypi.org:443"],
  "inject": [{"name": "crm", "hosts": ["api.crm.example.com"],
              "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer {{ secret.CRM_TOKEN }}"}}],
  "timeout_s": 30,
  "memory_mb": 512
}
  • Limits apply in every sandboxed mode. timeout_s and memory_mb are enforced as follows:
  • subprocess: rlimits, plus the host-side timeout
  • docker: --memory
  • langsmith: mem_bytes and the run timeout
  • Egress and injection need the langsmith mode. The local sandboxes have no network at all.
  • Checks: the file editor and /workspace/catalog report these problems:
Code Problem E082 The policy file is invalid. E083 A header uses a secret the project does not have. W082 Egress or inject rules are set, but the execution mode cannot apply them. W074 Egress allows every host. - Workspace UI: the Workspace page has a Sandbox policy button that scaffolds the file.

docs.title: 4. Open questions (need a LangSmith key; about 1 hour)
docs.text:
1. Is allow_list: [] accepted as "no egress"? If it is refused, send a single unroutable entry instead, such as offline.invalid:1.
  2. Latency: measure a cold create_sandbox from a snapshot, a warm run round trip, and the upload of a 1 MB workspace. The target for a warm script node is under 300 ms of overhead.
  3. Can one sandbox run several commands at once (parallel core.map branches)? If not, keep a small pool per project.
  4. Is python3 present in the default snapshot? Recommendation: build a project snapshot from python:3.12-slim plus the workspace's locked dependencies, keyed by the uv.lock hash (spec 05 §4), and set AGENTCANVAS_LANGSMITH_SNAPSHOT.
  5. With restricted egress, does the org allow-list replace or intersect a sandbox's access_control? The docs say it replaces it. Our "offline by default" then does not hold, so the UI should show a warning.

docs.title: 5. Recommendation
docs.text:
• Keep docker as the self-hosted default and make langsmith the hosted-edition default for scripts and event handlers once questions 1–3 are answered.
  • Follow-ups for the GA backlog:
  • snapshot per uv.lock hash
  • a pool when concurrent calls need it
  • workspace_secret references for secrets that live only in LangSmith
  • reuse the same policy for Deep Agent sandbox backends (backend.sandbox, where W074 applies)

docs.title: Spike SP-3 — Is LangGraph v3 event streaming ready to replace astream(version="v2")?
docs.text: Sprint S8 (time-boxed, 0.5 d) Question Can the runner produce the canonical events (doc 12 §C.3) from astream_events(version="v3") instead of astream(..., stream_mode=[...], subgraphs=True)? Outcome Not yet — keep v2 (review item V-04 stands). Re-check on each LangGraph minor release.

docs.title: Findings (langgraph 1.2.12, probed on 2026-09-29)
docs.text:
1. It is still experimental. Every call emits LangChainBetaWarning: The v3 streaming protocol on Pregel is experimental.
  2. The call shape differs from the docs.
  3. astream_events(..., version="v3") is a coroutine: run = await graph.astream_events(...) returns an AsyncGraphRunStream.
  4. run.output is a method, so you write await run.output().
  5. Projections are values, messages, lifecycle, subgraphs, interrupts and extensions.
  6. The default stream carries values events only. Each event is {"type": "event", "method": "values", "params": {"namespace", "timestamp", "data", "interrupts"}, "seq"}.
  7. It has no step start/finish events.
  8. For a flat graph, the lifecycle projection yielded nothing.
  9. STEP_STARTED/STEP_FINISHED (canvas node status, durations, lineage) would have to be rebuilt from state diffs, which loses which node wrote what.
  10. Interrupts and resume work. Command(resume=...) resumes into a new stream as expected, and interrupts arrive on values events.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The canonical event contract stays as it is. The adapter keeps astream v2 with updates, messages, custom, tasks and subgraphs.
  • Switching later only touches adapters/langchain/events.py and adapter.execute; the UI and the public API do not change.
  • Revisit when both of these hold:
  • the beta warning is gone
  • node lifecycle events are available for root graphs

docs.title: Spike SP-4 — Hosting on LangGraph Server with a ServerRuntime graph factory
docs.text: Sprint S8 (time-boxed, 0.5 d) Question Can an exported project (and later AgentCanvas's interpreted mode, ADR 0013) be served by Agent Server through a graph factory instead of a module-level graph? Outcome Yes. The export's langgraph.json now points at server.py:make_graph, an async context manager annotated with langgraph_sdk.runtime.ServerRuntime. It was verified end to end under langgraph dev.

docs.title: What was verified
docs.text:
1. The docs. ServerRuntime needs langgraph-api >= 0.7.31 and langgraph-sdk >= 0.3.5.
  2. The server reads the factory's type hints to decide what to inject: a ServerRuntime and/or a RunnableConfig.
  3. It calls the factory for runs (threads.create_run, where runtime.execution_runtime is set) and also for updates, state reads and introspection. The topology must be the same in every case.
  4. ServerRuntime is beta.
  5. A live run. A Greeter workflow was exported, then uv sync, uv add --dev "langgraph-cli[inmem]" and langgraph dev, with langgraph-api 0.15.1 and langgraph-sdk 0.4.5.
  6. POST /assistants/search listed the graph.
  7. POST /runs/wait {"assistant_id": "greeter", "input": {"who": "Ada"}} returned {"who": "Ada", "out": "Hello Ada"}.
  8. String annotations still inject. from __future__ import annotations is fine: the server resolves the annotation string against the module's globals. The import is guarded, so the project also runs without the runtime module.

docs.title: Design notes for ADR 0013 (interpreted hosting)
docs.text:
• Loading the IR. make_graph(runtime) can load the pinned IR from the assistant's config and call the same build_graph the runner uses.
  • Expensive work. MCP connections and per-user credentials go under runtime.execution_runtime. Introspection calls must still get the same nodes, so MCP-backed graphs build their tools in both paths today, which costs one discovery per call.
  • Identity. Per-user resources come from runtime.ensure_user() (custom auth). They map onto context fields with source: "user".
  • Beta caveat. The upstream API is beta (D16), so this stays behind a capability flag. The compiled export remains the portable default.

docs.title: AgentCanvas user guide
docs.text: AgentCanvas is a visual builder for AI agents and agentic workflows. You draw a workflow on a canvas (models, agents, tools, routers, human approvals, memory) and AgentCanvas turns it into a real LangGraph / LangChain / Deep Agents Python program that you can run, debug, test, evaluate, export and publish behind an API.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: Use any model Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, Grok, any OpenAI-compatible API, or models on your own computer (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp). Choose one on the first-run screen, with its API key. Build Drag widgets onto a canvas, wire them up, and configure them in the Inspector. Start from one of seven templates, a guided six-step tutorial, or the Beginner's guide. Hover or click any dot on a block to see what it does and what can connect to it. Add your own Python scripts, tools and custom widgets in the project workspace. Run and debug Run a workflow and watch each step light up. Pause for human approvals, set breakpoints, step back through the timeline, edit state and fork, and read a plain-language explanation of what happened. See tokens, cost and latency per step. Test and evaluate Save runs as test cases, build datasets, score runs with evaluators (exact match, regex, schema, LLM judge, tool trajectory, your own code), compare versions in experiments, and block releases that score worse. Ship Freeze versions, export a standalone Python project, or publish to an environment behind an API key. Start runs from webhooks, schedules or events, and keep scoring live traffic in production. Govern Sign in with your identity provider, keep organisations apart, give people roles, write policies the editor and publishing enforce, and read the audit log.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Run AgentCanvas on your computer: one Docker command, or from source with a two-minute smoke test.
  2. Getting started: build and run your first workflow.
  3. Core concepts: the handful of ideas everything else builds on.

Then dive into the area you need:

  • Models and API keys
  • Building on the canvas and the widget reference
  • Running and debugging
  • Workspace: code, secrets and events
  • Memory
  • Evaluation Studio
  • Publish and integrate
  • Organisations, roles and policies
  • Deploy and operate
  • FAQ

docs.title: Current release
docs.text: This guide describes AgentCanvas v0.5.0 (Evaluation in production). See the changelog for what changed in each release.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
In production AgentCanvas signs people in through your identity provider (any OpenID Connect provider: Keycloak, Okta, Entra ID, Auth0, Google…). The administrator configures it once (see Deploy and operate); people then click through to their usual login page. Sessions renew silently. The top bar shows who you are and your role, with Sign out and Sign in with a different account.

In local mode (make dev-fake / make dev-api without OIDC) there is no sign-in: you are the built-in admin dev@localhost.

docs.title: Organisations
docs.text: Everything (projects, workflows, runs, secrets, memory, deployments, policies, audit log) belongs to an organisation, and nobody can see another organisation's data. A person can belong to several organisations: invitations to someone who already belongs to another organisation wait for them to accept (Home shows a banner), accepting switches to the new organisation, and AgentCanvas opens the one used last.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Can viewer see workflows and runs reviewer also answer approvals and human-input requests in the Inbox builder also build, run, test and publish workflows admin also manage members, policies, release gates and read the audit log

Buttons for actions your role can't take are hidden.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
Admins open Members, enter an email, pick a role and click Invite. The invitation takes effect at the person's first sign-in with that (verified) email. Admins can change roles or remove people. An organisation can never be left without an admin who has signed in.

To bootstrap a new install, list the first admins' emails in AGENTCANVAS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAILS; they become admins of the default organisation on first sign-in.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Audit log (admins) records every change: who did it, what it touched, when and from where. Approvals record a hash of exactly what was approved; publishing past a failed release gate records the reason given. Rows are kept for 400 days by default.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
Policies are organisation rules the editor and publishing enforce. Each policy has:

  • a scope: each step, each resource, or the workflow;
  • a match (CEL): which steps or resources it applies to, e.g. resource.type == "model.chat";
  • a require (CEL): what must hold, e.g. resource.config.model in ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5"];
  • a severity: error or warning;
  • optional environments: limit the rule to publishing to, e.g., prod.

Two presets get you started:

Preset Rule Writes need approval every step's external writes are gated by a human: node.effects.all(e, e.effect != "external_write" \|\| e.gated) Approved models in prod in prod, chat models must come from an approved list

Names you can use: node (type, config, effects, ungated, models, tools), resource, workflow, env.

Admins can Switch off a policy without deleting it. Broken policies show in the editor's Problems dock (E095; W095 for environment-only rules), steps inside subgraphs included. Draft and debug runs still work, but publishing is refused until every applicable policy holds.

docs.title: Connect to other agents and tools
docs.text:
Four ways AgentCanvas works with the tools you already use:

  • Agents from other frameworks as steps. An agent built with the OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Google ADK and six more, or one running elsewhere (A2A or MCP), becomes one step of your workflow. Flows move in and out as Open Agent Spec files.
  • Your workflows as tools for other agents. Every published workflow is also an MCP server and an A2A agent, so Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT and other agent frameworks can call it.
  • One-click app connectors. A gallery of ready-made MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Notion, Postgres, a web browser, search and more) that your agents can use as tools.
  • Traces in your observability tool. Every run can be sent to Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Datadog or any OpenTelemetry backend.

docs.title: Use agents from other frameworks
docs.text:
Three blocks in the AI group run an agent that was not built on the canvas. Each is one step: it gets an input, returns an answer, and shows both in the trace. A badge on the block names the framework (or A2A, MCP).

Block Runs You set Agent from another framework an agent from your Workspace, inside this server the framework and where the agent is, e.g. tools.agents:support Remote agent (A2A) an agent running elsewhere, over the Agent2Agent protocol its Agent Card address (…/.well-known/agent-card.json) Remote agent (MCP) one tool of an MCP server, e.g. an agent published as a tool plug an App connector (MCP) into tools, then the tool name

All three have What to send the agent (insert data with {{ state.<field> }}; empty sends the latest chat message), Save the answer in (messages adds the answer to the chat) and Ask a person before it runs, which shows what will be sent on an approval card; a rejection skips the agent.

Supported frameworks and what the step calls:

Framework Package (exports install this version) Point the block at OpenAI Agents SDK openai-agents==0.23.1 an Agent CrewAI crewai==1.15.25 a Crew (its task texts can use {input} and other field names), an Agent or a Flow Google ADK google-adk==2.11.0 an agent (LlmAgent, …) Pydantic AI pydantic-ai-slim==2.54.0 an Agent Agno agno==3.1.1 an Agent or Team Strands Agents strands-agents==1.58.1 an Agent LlamaIndex Workflows llama-index-workflows==2.25.0 a Workflow (it gets input= and the other fields) Microsoft Agent Framework agent-framework-core==1.20.0 an agent (client.as_agent(...)) Claude Agent SDK claude-agent-sdk==0.2.164 a ClaudeAgentOptions Python function none async def run(input, ctx): return text, or a dict to set several fields
  • The agent's own package (and its model provider's, such as openai) must be installed on the server, and an export lists the framework package in its requirements. Add provider packages in the workspace if the agent needs them.
  • A function with no arguments that returns the agent works too: a fresh agent is built for every run, so runs never share an agent's memory.
  • The agent's tools run inside its framework, so AgentCanvas cannot see or gate them one by one. Tick what they can do under Side effects (writes, messages, code, spending) so the blast-radius view and dry runs know, and use Ask a person before it runs where that matters. The hosted edition does not offer this block, because the agent's code runs inside the server.
  • Remote agents (A2A): when the remote agent asks for more information (input-required), the run pauses and the question appears in the Inbox; the answer goes back to the same task. Addresses on private networks are refused unless you turn on Allow private network. Put keys in Headers as secrets. If AgentCanvas restarts while a remote agent waits for an answer, the step stops with a message instead of sending the first message again; start the run again.

docs.title: Open Agent Spec files
docs.text:
Open Agent Spec is a framework-neutral file format for agents and flows.

  • Export: in the editor, Versions → Download as an Agent Spec file. AI steps become LlmNodes, agents AgentNodes (remote agents as A2AAgent), questions InputMessageNodes, routers with rules like state.category == "billing" become BranchingNodes, and other steps become tools the other runtime provides. After downloading, a list says what Agent Spec cannot express, for example models it has no config for (they are written as OpenAI-compatible) or an agent's tools. Header values typed in directly are left out of the file; secret references (names, never values) stay.
  • Import: on the home page, Import an Agent Spec file reads a flow, or a single agent, as a new workflow and lists what it approximated before you open it. Steps AgentCanvas cannot run become placeholders to replace.
  • A file AgentCanvas exported carries the whole workflow, so importing it back gives exactly the same workflow, layout included.

docs.title: Call a workflow from other agents
docs.text: Publish the workflow, then open Versions → the deployment → Use from other agents (MCP, A2A). The panel shows the addresses and a ready-to-paste Claude Desktop setting. Both use the deployment's API key, the same one as the deployment API, with the same rate limits.

docs.title: As an MCP server
As an A2A agent
docs.text:
Agent card https://<your AgentCanvas>/api/v1/deployments/<id>/a2a/.well-known/agent-card.json (no key needed to read it) Endpoint https://<your AgentCanvas>/api/v1/deployments/<id>/a2a (JSON-RPC, A2A 0.3) Sign-in Authorization: Bearer <deployment key>
  • message/send runs the workflow. A data part gives the input fields; a text part goes to the workflow's text field (one named message, question, query, input, text, request, prompt or ticket, or its only text input). The answer is a task whose artifact holds the output.
  • A pause becomes the input-required state. Send the answer to the same task (taskId): "yes" or "no" for an approval, or the answer to a question.
  • contextId continues a conversation; tasks/get reads a task again.
  • Not supported: streaming (message/stream), push notifications and cancelling a task.

Runs started over MCP or A2A are ordinary runs of the deployment: they appear under Runs, count towards online evaluation and keep their conversations.

docs.title: App connectors
docs.text:
In the editor's block list, open App connectors (or search for an app). Drag one onto the canvas, or double-click it: it becomes an App connector (MCP) block already set up for that app. Plug its tools output into an agent, and use Browse tools to pick tools.

  • Keys. Connectors that need a key name the secret they read, such as GITHUB_MCP_AUTH. Add it under Workspace → Secrets. Where a server expects Authorization: Bearer <token>, store the whole value, including Bearer.
  • Local connectors start a program on the AgentCanvas server (npx or uvx). They work only in the local edition, after an admin turns on local MCP servers, and need Node.js or uv on the server.
  • Sign-in only. A few apps accept only an interactive sign-in (OAuth). They are listed so you can find them, but AgentCanvas cannot sign in to them yet.

Each entry was checked against npm, PyPI or the official MCP registry when the gallery was built; its tooltip says what it needs.

docs.title: Send traces to your observability tool
docs.text:
Under Setup → Send traces to your observability tool, an admin picks a destination:

Destination Address Keys Langfuse https://cloud.langfuse.com (EU), https://us.cloud.langfuse.com (US), or your own public and secret key, each as a project secret Arize Phoenix your Phoenix, e.g. http://phoenix:6006 API key, if your Phoenix needs one Datadog the Datadog Agent's OTLP/HTTP receiver, e.g. http://datadog-agent:4318 none here: the Agent holds your Datadog key Other any OTLP/HTTP traces URL, e.g. an OpenTelemetry Collector an optional Authorization header, as a secret

Send a test trace checks the address and keys. From then on every run of the project's workflows is sent as one trace: the run, each step, every model call (model, tokens, reply) and every tool call (arguments, result). Spans use the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and the OpenInference ones, which all three tools understand.

  • Secret values are masked, and fields a workflow marks as never in traces are redacted. Turn off Include inputs, outputs and model replies to send only timings, models and token counts.
  • Export runs in the background and never slows a run down. If the destination is down, traces are dropped and the server logs a warning.
  • A model or tool call is shown as a point in time inside its step: the step's duration is exact.

docs.title: Beginner's guide: your first AI workflow
docs.text: This page assumes you have never built anything with AI before. No coding is needed. The same guide is inside the app: open a workflow and press ❓ Help at the top (it also opens by itself the first time you open an empty workflow).

docs.title: What is an "agentic workflow"?
docs.text:
A workflow is a recipe a computer follows, one step at a time. Some steps use AI to read, write or decide. Others ask a person, call a web service, or tidy up data.

An agentic workflow is one where an AI can also decide what to do next and use tools on its own, for example look up an order, then write a reply based on what it found.

Example: a customer email arrives → AI decides whether it is urgent → urgent ones go to a person for approval → AI drafts a reply.

docs.title: The words you will see
docs.text: Word What it means Block or step A box on the canvas that does one thing, like Ask AI or Ask for approval. Drag them in from the palette on the left. ▶ Start and ■ Finish Every run begins at Start and ends at Finish. Arrow (grey) Decides what runs next. Drag from the dot on the right of a block to the dot at the top-left of the next one. AI model The AI “brain” (Claude, GPT, Gemini, a local model…). AI steps need one plugged into their model input. Add-on (dashed outline) Something that plugs into a step instead of running on its own: an AI model, a tool, a limit, a safety check. It connects with a coloured, dashed line. Data field (channel) The workflow's notepad: named boxes like question and answer that steps read and write. In text you write, insert one with {{ state.question }}. Agent An AI that works in a loop: think, use a tool, look at the result, repeat until done. Tool Something an agent can use, such as calling a web service or running a Python function. Run Trying the workflow with some input, in the Run tab.

docs.title: Build your first workflow in 5 steps
docs.text:
Before you start, pick your AI model once on the home page (Model, or the Set up your model banner). Every new AI model block uses it automatically.

  1. On the home page, type a name and press Create empty.
  2. Click empty canvas. In the panel on the right, press + Channel twice and name the fields question and answer.
  3. Click the dot on the right of ▶ Start and choose Ask AI. The block is added and already connected.
  4. In the right panel, write the instructions, e.g. Answer simply: {{ state.question }}, and set Save the reply in to answer.
  5. Click the coloured square marked model on the Ask AI block and choose AI model. Then click the Ask AI block's right-hand dot and choose Finish (END).

The Problems list at the bottom now says No problems — the workflow can run. Open the Run tab, type {"question": "What is an AI agent?"} and press ▶ Run. The block turns green and the answer appears.

Want a person to check the answer before it is used? Click the arrow into Finish, press Delete, then click the Ask AI block's right-hand dot and choose Ask for approval; connect that to Finish and run again.

Prefer to learn by doing with a checklist? On the home page, press Start the guided build: a card walks you through six steps and ticks each one off as you do it.

docs.title: Getting unstuck
docs.text:
• Hover over any dot on a block to see what it carries and what to do with it.
  • Click a dot to see everything that can connect to it. Pick one and it is added and connected for you. Clicking a coloured input (like model or tools) shows the add-ons that fit there.
  • Hover a block's title, or a block in the palette, to read what it does.
  • A red ⛔ on a block means something is missing. The Problems list at the bottom says what happened and how to fix it for every problem; click one to jump to the block.
  • If an arrow refuses to connect, a message at the bottom of the canvas says why and what to do instead.
  • If a run fails, the Run tab explains the likely cause (a missing API key, a local model that is not running, a misspelt field name…) and how to fix it.
  • Made a mistake? ↶ (or Ctrl/⌘+Z) undoes it. Everything saves automatically.

docs.title: Common problems and fixes
docs.text:
You see What it means How to fix it needs a ChatModel connected to its 'model' port The AI step has no AI model. Click its model square and choose AI model. no path from START to END A run could never finish. Connect Start to your first step and your last step to Finish. has no outgoing flow edge A dead end: nothing comes after this step. Click its right-hand dot and choose the next step, or Finish. refers to unknown state channel A step uses a data field that does not exist. Click empty canvas and add the field with + Channel, using the exact name. template error A {{ }} is not closed. Every {{ needs a matching }}. The run says the API key is wrong The AI provider refused your key. Re-enter it on the home page under Model, or in Workspace → Secrets. The run says connection refused The AI model's server could not be reached. If you use Ollama or LM Studio, make sure it is running.

Next: browse the Block reference or read Core concepts for the details.

docs.title: The editor at a glance
docs.text:
Area What it does Palette (left) Every widget, grouped by category, plus your workspace scripts, tools and custom widgets. Type in Search widgets… to filter. Canvas (middle) Your workflow. ▶ START and ■ END mark where runs begin and finish. Steps are solid cards, resources are dashed boxes. Toolbar (top) ⌘K command palette, Tidy (auto-layout), Blast radius, ⧉ Subgraph, ▭ Frame, undo ↶ / redo ↷, ▶ Test, and links to Evaluate, Workspace, Memory and Inbox. Side panel (right) Inspector (settings of the selection, or the Workflow panel when nothing is selected), Run, Tests, Versions, Code. Dock (bottom) Problems, Timeline, Explain.

Themes. The switch at the right of the top bar on every page picks Light, Medium (a softer dimmed slate), Dark, or System (follows your computer). Your choice is remembered in this browser.

docs.title: Add and connect steps
docs.text:
• Add: drag a widget from the palette onto the canvas, or use the ⌘K palette.
  • Connect: drag from a handle on one card to a handle on another. Step-to-step edges define order; resource-to-port edges give a step its model, tools or middleware. Ports are typed and colour-coded (for example model* takes a ChatModel, tools takes a list of Tools; * means required). A connection that doesn't fit is refused with the reason.
  • Configure: click a card. The Inspector shows its name (used in code and the API), label (shown on the card) and a settings form. Prompts and many fields are templates over the state: {{ state.ticket }}. Conditions (routers, policies, filters) are written in CEL, e.g. state.urgency == "high".
  • Select several: drag a selection box or shift-click. Copy and paste with ⌘C / ⌘V (Ctrl on Windows/Linux).
  • Undo / redo: ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z, or the ↶ ↷ buttons.
  • Tidy lays the graph out automatically.

Everything saves automatically. If someone else saved the same workflow in the meantime, you are told about the conflict instead of overwriting it.

docs.title: State channels
docs.text: Click an empty spot on the canvas to open the Workflow panel. There you set the name, description, recursion limit (the maximum number of steps per run), durability (how eagerly checkpoints are written: exit fastest, async default, sync for workflows with side effects), a budget, and the state channels (see Core concepts). + Channel adds one.

docs.title: Budgets
docs.text: A budget stops a run that spends too much: maximum tokens, cost (USD, from catalog prices) or seconds per run, and maximum tokens or cost per thread (all runs of a conversation together).

docs.title: Structure: subgraphs and frames
docs.text:
• ⧉ Subgraph (or ⌘G) turns the selected steps into one Subgraph step with its own state. Input channels are copied in and output channels copied back. Double-click to work inside it.
  • ▭ Frame draws a labelled box around the selected steps. It is purely visual.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text: The Problems dock validates the workflow continuously. Codes starting with E are errors (the workflow can't run until they are fixed), W are warnings, I are hints. Click a problem to jump to the step it is about. Organisation policies show up here too (E095, or W095 for rules that only apply in one environment).

docs.title: Blast radius
docs.text: Blast radius colours every step by what it can do to the outside world (write, send, execute, spend) and whether a human approves it first. Use it before publishing to spot ungated side effects. A dry run (Run tab) replaces every risky tool with a recorder so you can run the whole workflow safely.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text: The Code tab shows the LangGraph Python program generated from the canvas. Each block is tagged with the card it came from (# ── @canvas-node … ──). It is read-only: change the canvas and the code follows. To take the code away, use Export (see Publish and integrate).

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: A few ideas carry through the whole product.

docs.title: Organisation, project, workflow
docs.text:
• An organisation owns everything: people, projects, secrets, memory, policies. Organisations never see each other's data.
  • A project groups workflows that share a workspace (Python code in a git repository) and secrets. Every install starts with a Default project.
  • A workflow is one graph on the canvas. It has a draft you edit, versions you freeze, and deployments that serve a version behind an API.

docs.title: State and channels
docs.text:
A workflow passes one shared state from step to step. The state is made of named channels (fields), which you declare on the Workflow panel (click the empty canvas). Each channel has:

Setting Meaning type A JSON Schema type (string, boolean, array, an object…). reducer How a write combines with the current value: replace (default), append (lists), add_messages (chat history), sum, or merge (objects). io Whether it is part of the workflow's input and output (inout), input only, output only, or private. storage full, or delta for long histories that should be stored as changes.

Steps read channels (prompts use templates like {{ state.ticket }}) and write their results to channels. The inputs and outputs of the whole workflow form its contract, which the API uses.

docs.title: Steps, resources and edges
docs.text:
• Steps (nodes) do work in sequence: Ask AI, an AI Agent, Choose a path, a script, Ask for approval.
  • Resources are things steps use rather than steps themselves: a chat model, a tool, an MCP server, middleware, a memory backend. They sit on the canvas as dashed boxes and are wired into a step's typed ports (model, tools, middleware). Several steps can share one resource.
  • Edges connect steps from ▶ START to ■ END. Routers have one output per route. Map runs a step once per list item in parallel; Join waits for all branches.

Ports are typed and colour-coded; a connection that doesn't fit is refused with a reason.

docs.title: Runs and threads
docs.text:
• A run executes the workflow once. It can finish, fail, or pause (at an approval, a human-input form, or a breakpoint) and be resumed later, even after a restart: runs are durable.
  • A thread is a conversation: consecutive runs on the same thread keep their state, which is how chat works. Every step boundary is saved as a checkpoint, which is what the timeline, fork and replay use.

docs.title: Human in the loop
docs.text: Approvals, human-input forms and tool approvals on agents (Pause for a human before these tools run) all pause the run and show up in the Run panel and the cross-workflow Inbox. Reviewers can approve, reject, or edit the value before approving.

docs.title: Generated code
docs.text: The canvas is stored as a JSON document (the workflow IR). AgentCanvas validates it (about 70 rules, shown in the Problems dock) and compiles it to readable LangGraph Python, visible live on the Code tab and exportable as a standalone project. There is no hidden runtime: what you export is what runs.

docs.title: AI Copilot
docs.text:
The Copilot is an assistant in the editor that knows AgentCanvas. Describe what you want in plain words and it writes a short brief, proposes the blocks, and builds the workflow for you to review. Ask it what a workflow does and it explains. It never saves anything by itself: every change is a proposal you accept or reject.

Open it with ✦ Copilot in the editor's top bar (or the Copilot tab on the right).

docs.title: Build mode and Ask mode
docs.text: Mode What the Copilot may do Who can use it Build Read the workflow, write a brief, propose changes. Builders and admins Ask Read the workflow and the product docs, answer questions. Nothing changes. Everyone, viewers included

docs.title: How a build goes
docs.text:
1. Brief. For a new workflow or a big change, the Copilot first writes a brief: the goal, inputs, outputs, steps, tools, how you will know it works, and any open questions. The brief card stays at the top of the chat. Answer the questions or say "yes, build it".
  2. Plan. It says in a few lines which blocks it will use, in which order.
  3. Build. It sends edit commands, checks the result with the same validator as the Problems dock, and fixes its own mistakes until there are no errors.
  4. Review. The proposal appears on the canvas: new blocks are outlined in green, changed ones in amber, and the canvas is read-only while you look. Accept applies it as one edit (Undo takes it back in one step); Reject throws it away. If you edit the workflow first, the proposal is still offered when it applies cleanly.

The Copilot tells you what it cannot do for you, such as adding an API key as a secret or filling a memory space.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Ask "write tests for this and run them", or let the Copilot do it after building from a brief with success criteria. It turns the criteria into test cases (input plus the expected status, field values or steps), tries the workflow with them, and fixes what fails. Test runs use the workflow as it would be with the proposal and are dry runs: tools that send or write to outside systems are stubbed. When no model key is set it can script the model's replies instead of calling a model. Proposed tests are saved as the workflow's test cases when you accept.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
The Copilot can find, explain and fix problems:

  • Problems: it reads the Problems list with a plain explanation of every code. ✦ Ask the Copilot to fix these at the top of the Problems list sends them over.
  • Failed runs: it reads recent runs and what each step did (the same data as Explain mode), and explains the cause in plain words. ✦ Ask the Copilot why under a run error asks about that run.
  • Fixes it can check: after proposing a fix it reruns the failed run's input on the fixed workflow, replaying that run's recorded model replies and tool outputs when it has them, so you see whether the fix works before you accept it.

Ask "explain" to get only an explanation; ask "fix" to get a proposal. In Ask mode it never changes or runs anything.

docs.title: Project notes
docs.text: Notes on the Setup page under AI Copilot are read on every message: conventions ("drafts use ollama:llama3.3", "anything that emails customers needs an approval step"). The Copilot can propose a note too; it is added when you accept.

docs.title: Help with code
docs.text: In the Workspace, under any Python file, the Copilot writes code from a description, explains the file or the lines you selected, and fixes the problems ruff found. Its changes come as a diff you accept or reject; nothing is saved until you press Save. It uses the same model and privacy setting as the chat.

docs.title: Which model it uses
docs.text:
Set this on the Setup page under AI Copilot:

  • Use the workflow's model (default): the project's default model from first-run setup, or, without one, the first AI model in the workflow.
  • Use a separate model: any provider:model, for example a stronger model for building, or a local model (ollama:…) so nothing leaves your machine. Its key is the provider's project secret, as for any model.

The model must support tool calling. Your organisation's model policies apply to the Copilot too: a policy that allows only some models in workflows also limits the Copilot.

Model for questions (optional) answers Ask-mode questions with a different, usually cheaper, model. Private limits the Copilot to models running on your own machines (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp), so your workflows never leave them.

Token limit per chat caps what one conversation can spend (input plus output tokens). The chat shows how much is used; New chat starts over with a fresh limit.

docs.title: What it knows
docs.text:
The Copilot gets a knowledge pack built from the running product on every message: how workflows are put together, every block with its ports and settings (including your workspace's own blocks), the starter templates and the edit commands and the meaning of every problem code. Providers that support prompt caching (Anthropic) cache it, so it is cheap after the first message. Its tools look up a block's full settings, read a template, read your workflow with its problems, read past runs, search this user guide, and list the models and which secrets are set (names only).

Text inside your workflow (prompts, descriptions) is treated as data: it cannot change what the Copilot is asked to do. The Copilot refuses to put API keys or passwords into settings and uses secret references instead.

docs.title: For administrators
docs.text:
• GET/PUT /v1/projects/{id}/copilot-settings turns the Copilot on or off and sets its model and token limit.
  • GET /v1/workflows/{id}/copilot returns your conversation, its brief and any open proposal; POST …/copilot/messages streams an answer (Server-Sent Events); POST …/copilot/proposals/{id} records accept or reject; DELETE …/copilot starts a new chat. Conversations are per person and per workflow.
  • Developers can measure a model's building quality with the eval harness: uv run python -m agentcanvas.copilot.evals --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 builds ten workflows from plain requests and checks each one validates and uses the expected blocks; --suite debug plants about 30 bugs in the starter templates (a missing arrow to Finish, an unplugged model, a wrong output field, a broken condition, an unknown field in a prompt) and checks the Copilot's fix leaves no errors.

docs.title: Deploy and operate
docs.text: This page is for whoever runs AgentCanvas for a team. To try it on one computer, use the one-command Docker setup in Run AgentCanvas on your computer. The developer-level runbook is the deployment & operations guide.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text: Component Notes web nginx serving the web app and forwarding /api/ to the API. Sends a strict Content-Security-Policy and rate-limits public calls. api The FastAPI control plane and run engine. Stateless: run two or more replicas. Runs survive restarts and are handed to another replica on shutdown. Postgres 16 + pgvector Everything: workflows, runs, checkpoints, memory, audit log. workspaces volume One git repository per project, shared by the API replicas. Identity provider Any OpenID Connect provider, for sign-in.

docs.title: Option 1: Docker Compose on one host
docs.text:
docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.api -t agentcanvas-api apps/api
docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.web -t agentcanvas-web .
cp infra/.env.prod.example infra/.env.prod      # fill it in (never commit it)
docker compose -f infra/compose.prod.yml --env-file infra/.env.prod up -d --wait

This starts Postgres, a one-shot migration, two API replicas and the web server on port 8080 (WEB_PORT). Put a TLS-terminating proxy in front and keep response buffering off for /api/ (runs stream Server-Sent Events).

docs.title: Option 2: Kubernetes with Helm
docs.text:
The chart is in infra/helm/agentcanvas. Create a Kubernetes Secret with DATABASE_URL, AGENTCANVAS_SECRET_KEY and provider keys, name it in secrets.existingSecret, set the config.oidc.* values, and install:

helm install agentcanvas infra/helm/agentcanvas -f my-values.yaml

Migrations run as a Helm hook Job before the API starts.

docs.title: Essential settings
docs.text: Setting Purpose DATABASE_URL postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/agentcanvas AGENTCANVAS_SECRET_KEY 64+ random characters. Production refuses the development default. AGENTCANVAS_ENV prod (default in compose prod and Helm), staging or dev LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY 32 characters: encrypts conversation checkpoints at rest AGENTCANVAS_KMS_KEY Master key for project secrets: file:<path>, aws:<key ARN> or gcp:<key name> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY Model provider keys for the whole server; a project secret of the same name takes precedence (Models and API keys) AGENTCANVAS_LOCAL_MODELS_HOST Host that local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) are reached on when their address isn't set, e.g. host.docker.internal or a GPU machine's name AGENTCANVAS_SCRIPT_EXECUTION Where workspace code runs: subprocess (default in production), docker, langsmith, inprocess AGENTCANVAS_CORS_ORIGINS The web app's origin, as a JSON list AGENTCANVAS_RETENTION_DAYS Delete conversations idle this long (default 90; 0 keeps them) AGENTCANVAS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_DEPLOYMENT / _PER_WEBHOOK / _PER_PROJECT Public API requests per minute (120 / 120 / 600)

docs.title: Sign-in
docs.text:
1. In your identity provider, create a public client (authorization code + PKCE) with redirect URI https://<your app>/auth/callback, and enable refresh tokens (offline_access).
  2. Make the access token's audience the API's (e.g. agentcanvas-api).
  3. Set AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE=oidc, AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_ISSUER, AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_AUDIENCE, AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, and AGENTCANVAS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAILS for the first admins.

The API checks every token against the provider's keys. AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE=dev (no sign-in) is refused in staging and prod.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• Health: /healthz (process up) and /readyz (database and run store reachable).
  • Metrics: Prometheus on /metrics. A Grafana dashboard and alert rules (including evaluation drift) are in infra/observability/.
  • Traces: set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for OpenTelemetry; LANGSMITH_TRACING / LANGSMITH_API_KEY for LangSmith.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: infra/scripts/backup.sh writes a pg_dump of the compose prod database; infra/scripts/restore.sh <file> restores one (and migrates it to the running version). With managed Postgres, rely on its point-in-time recovery and run the backup nightly as a portable second copy.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text: Pull the new images and roll the API. On shutdown each replica stops taking runs, lets running ones reach a step boundary and hands them to another replica, which resumes them. Conversations move to a newly published workflow version only when it is resume-compatible.

docs.title: Rotating the secrets master key
docs.text: Set the new key in AGENTCANVAS_KMS_KEY, keep the old one in AGENTCANVAS_KMS_PREVIOUS_KEYS, then run python -m agentcanvas.security.kms rewrap in an API container.

docs.title: Evaluation Studio
docs.text: Evaluation answers "is this version better than the last one?" with numbers instead of impressions. Open it from the editor's Evaluate link. It has six tabs: Datasets, Evaluators, Experiments, Release gates, Production and Annotation queues.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
A dataset is a list of examples: an input, optionally a reference (expected) output, and metadata. Create dataset, then fill it by:

  • Add example by hand,
  • Add the saved test cases of the workflow,
  • adding past runs (from the run list or an annotation queue),
  • Import CSV or JSONL.

Every change creates a new version, so an experiment always knows exactly which examples it used. Examples can carry a split (e.g. train, test) to evaluate a subset. Datasets can be pushed to or pulled from LangSmith when you ask (project secret or server LANGSMITH_API_KEY).

docs.title: Evaluators
docs.text:
An evaluator scores one run from 0 to 1, passes or fails it at a threshold (pass at), and can add a comment.
