Kind Scores exact match the output equals the reference regex the output matches a pattern JSON Schema the output is valid against a schema LLM judge a model grades the output against your rubric tool trajectory the agent called the expected tools (in order, in any order, or a subset) workspace code your own function in scripts/ composite a weighted mix of other evaluators, or all/any must pass pairwise judge which of two answers is better (asked twice with the answers swapped to avoid position bias); reports a win rate with a confidence interval

Try runs an evaluator on a sample before you rely on it.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text:
An experiment runs one or more targets over a dataset version and scores every result. A target is the draft, a published version, or a variant with another model or prompt. ▶ Run experiment starts it in the background; it can be cancelled and survives a server restart.

The results grid shows mean scores, pass rates, latency, tokens and cost per target, and each example's output with its run timeline one click away. Compare two experiments to see which examples improved or regressed.

Simulated users: for chat workflows, an experiment can hold a whole conversation per example with a simulated user (a model given a persona, a goal and a turn limit). Evaluators see the full transcript.

docs.title: Release gates
docs.text: An admin can require an evaluation before anything is published to an environment: minimum mean scores on a dataset, and the maximum drop in pass rate against the version currently live. Publishing to that environment evaluates the exact workflow being published (or reuses an evaluation of the same thing) and is refused on a miss. Admins can publish anyway with a reason, which the audit log keeps. A gate measures with the dataset version and evaluator settings it was saved with.

docs.title: Production (online evaluation)
docs.text:
Attach evaluators to a deployment with a sampling rate (0-100 %) and a filter (run status, metadata the caller sent, e.g. tier=gold). Sampled runs are scored in the background after the response is sent, so callers never wait. Scores appear on runs and as hourly or daily averages on the Production tab; the judge's own cost is counted separately.

Drift alerts fire when an evaluator's recent mean falls below a value (alert below) or drops more than a set amount under its 7-day average (alert drop).

docs.title: Annotation queues
docs.text:
A queue collects runs for people to review. Fill it automatically by rules (a low online score such as polite < 0.7, a failed run, a thumbs-down from an API caller) or by hand. Reviewers see input, output and timeline, score each rubric criterion, comment, and can add the run to a dataset with a corrected reference in one step (Submit review). The tab shows progress and agreement between reviewers.

API callers send thumbs up or down with POST /v1/deployments/{id}/runs/{run_id}/feedback.

docs.title: Export and deploy in your own environment
docs.text:
Export turns a workflow into a project you deploy wherever you run software: your computer, a Linux server, Kubernetes, Google Cloud Run, AWS or Azure. You choose where; the download holds everything for that place, and step-by-step guides written for this workflow, with its keys, settings and outside services already named.

AgentCanvas never needs access to your environment or your cloud account: every step runs on your machine with your own tools.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
In the editor open Versions → ⬇ Export to run in your own environment…:

  1. Pick the version (or the current draft).
  2. Pick where it will run. The panel lists what you will need before you download: the tools to install, the keys and settings to provide, the outside services it calls, whether it needs a database and why, and a starting size.
  3. ⬇ Download.

Or call GET /v1/workflows/{id}/export.zip?target=<target>&version=<x.y.z>, and GET /v1/workflows/{id}/export/plan?target=<target> for the list of needs.

Target What you get Database local: your computer (Docker) Docker Compose with the service and Postgres included server: Linux server or VM Docker Compose with Postgres and Caddy (automatic HTTPS for your domain) included, or your own kubernetes A Helm chart: Deployment, Service, optional Ingress, autoscaling your managed Postgres cloudrun: Google Cloud Run A script: Cloud Build, Secret Manager, Cloud Run Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL aws: ECS Fargate A task definition and a script: ECR, Secrets Manager, ECS Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL azure: Container Apps A script: Azure Container Registry build, Container Apps with secrets Azure Database for PostgreSQL

A database is needed when the workflow pauses for people (approvals, questions), keeps memories, or continues chats across messages. Without one, the service keeps conversations in a SQLite file on one machine.

docs.title: What is in the download
docs.text: Path What it is docs/1-PREREQUISITES.md … 4-VERIFY-AND-OPERATE.md The four guides: what you need, setup, deploy, then check, scale, upgrade, roll back, back up and rotate keys Makefile make doctor, setup, test, gate, run, deploy, smoke, logs .env.example Every setting, each with where to get it src/<name>/app.py The service (below) deploy/<target>/ Deploy files for the target you chose, and only those Dockerfile Port 8000, a non-root user, a health check, pinned base images tests/ The saved test cases (with scripted model replies) and the service's own tests, all offline workflow.ir.json The exported workflow; import it into AgentCanvas to see which version is deployed src/<name>/graph.py, src/agentcanvas/ The generated LangGraph code and the node library it uses src/flows/<id>/…, src/scripts/… and other workspace folders Your workspace code that this workflow uses (below) tests/test_workspace_code.py Checks that every code path the workflow names (flows.<id>.scripts.x:run …) imports inside the export

docs.title: Your workspace code in the export
docs.text:
The export carries exactly the Workspace code the workflow uses, not the whole workspace:

  • the files its steps, tools and custom blocks name, from the workflow's own folder or the shared folders;
  • every workspace module those files import, found by following their import lines;
  • data files in the workflow's own folder (prompts, JSON, CSV …);
  • the Python packages listed in requirements.txt at the workspace root or in the workflow's folder, added to the export's pyproject.toml (one line per package, like rapidfuzz>=3; options and URLs are skipped).

Other workflows' code is left out. If the workflow names code that is not in the workspace (a deleted file, say), the export stops and names it, so a broken download never leaves AgentCanvas. make test runs tests/test_workspace_code.py with the other tests.

docs.title: Deploy, step by step
docs.text:
make doctor      # checks tools, settings, database, outside services and the port; says which guide section fixes each problem
make setup       # creates .env with a fresh API key; fill in the empty values
make test        # the graph builds and the saved test cases pass
make deploy      # runs deploy/<target>/deploy.sh: read it first, every line is a plain command
make smoke URL=https://…   # calls the deployed service once and prints the answer

make doctor ARGS=--live also makes one tiny call to each AI model with your keys. To try the service before you have model keys, set DEMO_MODE=true in .env: the models answer with canned replies.

The service checks its settings when it starts and stops with a plain message naming what is missing, instead of failing on the first request.

docs.title: The service's API
docs.text:
The service answers the same API as an AgentCanvas deployment, so a client moves to it by changing only the base URL and the key:

Call Does POST /v1/deployments/<name>/runs/wait Runs the workflow; returns the answer, or the questions it is waiting on POST /v1/deployments/<name>/runs/stream The same run as Server-Sent Events POST /v1/deployments/<name>/threads/<id>/resume Answers an approval or a question POST /v1/deployments/<name>/runs/<id>/feedback A thumbs up or down (logged, and written to FEEDBACK_FILE if set) GET /healthz, GET /docs Health and the interactive API page

Every call except /healthz and /docs needs Authorization: Bearer <key>, one of the comma-separated API_KEYS. <name> can be anything. The MCP and A2A addresses of an AgentCanvas deployment (Connect to other agents and tools) are not part of the exported service.

docs.title: Keys and secrets
docs.text: Secret values never leave AgentCanvas: the export names every secret the workflow uses, and you copy the values from Workspace → Secrets into .env. The deploy scripts put them in the platform's secret store (Secret Manager, Secrets Manager, Container Apps secrets, or a Kubernetes secret).

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text: make gate runs the saved test cases and the service's API tests, and fails unless every one passes; run it before make deploy (or in your CI). Evaluations that need an AI judge stay in AgentCanvas's Evaluation Studio.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Do I need an API key to try AgentCanvas? No. Use a local model (Ollama, LM Studio…), or run from source with make dev-fake, which answers with built-in demo models so every feature works offline and free. See Run AgentCanvas on your computer.

What is the quickest way to run it? make docker-up with Docker installed, then open http://localhost:7777 and choose your model.

Which models are supported? Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, any OpenAI-compatible API, and models on your own computer through Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or llama.cpp. All are installed with AgentCanvas. Choose one on the Model screen and enter its key there. See Models and API keys.

Can I use AgentCanvas without sending data to a cloud provider? Yes: pick a local model (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) on the Model screen. Runs, memory and traces stay on your machine unless you turn on LangSmith tracing.

Is the generated code mine? Can I run it without AgentCanvas? Yes. Export gives you a plain Python project (LangGraph graph, node library, your workspace code, pinned dependencies) with a service that answers the same API as a deployment, deploy files for where you run it, and guides; see Export and deploy.

What happens if the server restarts during a run? Runs are durable. Paused runs (approvals, human input) wait indefinitely; running runs are resumed from their last checkpoint by another API instance.

How do I keep an agent from doing something irreversible? Turn on Blast radius to see every step that can write, send, execute or spend. Put an Ask for approval step before it, or list the tool under the agent's Pause for a human before these tools run. Use Dry run to test safely, and an organisation policy such as Writes need approval to make it mandatory.

Where are API keys and passwords stored? As project secrets: encrypted at rest (under a master key you can keep in AWS or Google Cloud KMS), never readable through the API, and masked as *** in run events and traces.

Can several people work on the same workflow? Yes. Edits save automatically with conflict detection: if someone else saved first, you are told instead of overwriting their work. Roles decide who can build, review or only view.

How do I call a workflow from my application? Publish it, copy the API key, and POST to /v1/deployments/{id}/runs/wait or /runs/stream. See Call a deployment.

How do I know a new version is better? Build a dataset, add evaluators, run an experiment comparing the live version with the draft, and set a release gate so publishing is refused when scores drop. See Evaluation Studio.

How do I delete a user's data? Erase their memory namespace on the Memory page. Conversations are deleted automatically after the retention period (90 days by default).

Where do I report a bug or see what's planned? On GitHub. PROGRESS.md lists what is done and pending.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This walk-through builds and runs a small workflow in about ten minutes. It assumes AgentCanvas is running (Run AgentCanvas on your computer). With the demo models (make dev-fake) every step works without API keys; answers are canned.

docs.title: Choose your model
docs.text: On first start, Home shows Set up your model. Click Choose a model, pick a provider (hosted, or a local server such as Ollama), enter the key if it needs one, Test connection and Save. Templates then use that model. See Models and API keys. You can skip this when running with the demo models.

docs.title: Option A: the guided build
docs.text: On Home, click Start the guided build. A six-step tutorial walks you through state, steps, flow, a model, a run and a human approval, and advances by itself as the real canvas takes shape. It is the fastest way to learn the editor.

docs.title: Option B: start from a template
docs.text:
On Home, the template cards create a ready-to-run workflow:

Template What it shows Chat assistant One agent chatting over the messages channel. The best starting point for adding tools. Classify and route An LLM classifies the input, a router picks a branch, each branch writes a reply. Support triage Classify a ticket's urgency; urgent tickets wait for a manager's approval, the rest get a drafted reply. Approval workflow An LLM drafts, a person approves or edits, and only approved drafts are published. Data extraction Turn free text (an email, an invoice) into validated structured fields. RAG Q&A Answer from a knowledge base kept in long-term memory. Research brief Map-reduce research: one LLM call per topic in parallel, then a Deep Agent writes the brief.

Support triage (demo tools) is a variant of Support triage wired to a demo send_reply tool from the examples, used in the smoke test.

docs.title: Your first run
docs.text:
1. Click Classify and route. The editor opens:
    • the palette of widgets on the left,
    • the canvas in the middle,
    • the Inspector / Run / Tests / Versions / Code tabs on the right,
    • the Problems / Timeline / Explain dock at the bottom.
  2. Click a step on the canvas. The Inspector shows its settings: prompt, output channel, model.
  3. Open the Run tab. The input box is pre-filled with the workflow's inputs as JSON. Fill in a value and click ▶ Run.
  4. Steps light up as they run and show a done badge with tokens and time. The Run tab streams output, then shows the final state.
  5. Open the Explain tab in the bottom dock for a step-by-step narrative ("chose route 'normal' → …").
  6. Open the Code tab to see the LangGraph Python program AgentCanvas generated from your canvas. It updates as you edit.

docs.title: Make a change
docs.text:
1. Drag an Ask for approval block from the palette (People) onto the canvas.
  2. Drag from the output handle of one step to the input of the Approval, and from it onward. Connections are checked as you draw; if one is refused, a message says why. Tip: click a block's right-hand dot to see what can come next and add it already connected.
  3. In the Inspector, choose which data field the reviewer sees (What the person reviews) and where the decision is written (Save the decision in).
  4. Watch the Problems dock: it lists anything that would stop the workflow from running, and says No problems — the workflow can run. when it is ready.
  5. Run again. The run pauses with Approval needed; approve or reject in the Run tab, or from the Inbox.

Changes save automatically (the header shows Saved). Undo and redo with the ↶ ↷ buttons or ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• New to AI? Read the Beginner's guide.
  • Learn the vocabulary in Core concepts.
  • Add a tool to the Chat assistant: see Widgets › Tools.
  • Save the run as a test case and freeze a version: see Publish and integrate.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Workflows have two kinds of memory.

  • Short-term: the state of a thread. Everything in the channels, including chat history, is kept between runs on the same thread and checkpointed at every step.
  • Long-term: facts kept across conversations, stored per organisation in the database (with semantic search on Postgres + pgvector). This page is about long-term memory.

docs.title: Spaces and sharing
docs.text:
Every memory belongs to a space (a name you choose, e.g. knowledge or preferences) and is shared per:

Shared per Meaning user (default) Each end user has their own memories. Needs a context field with source user so the run knows who the user is. API callers pass user_id; it is stored as api:<deployment>:<user_id> so API users never mix with organisation members. workflow One set of memories for everyone using the workflow. thread Memories that last for one conversation.

Same space + same sharing = same memories, whichever widget reads or writes them.

docs.title: Using memory in a workflow
docs.text:
• Remember saves a channel's value under a key (a template, e.g. preference:{{ state.topic }}).
  • Recall searches a space with a query template and writes up to top_k matches to a channel. An empty query returns the most recent memories.
  • Forget deletes one key.
  • Memory tools give an agent search_memory and save_memory, so the agent decides when to use memory.
  • Saved files folder blocks mount a Planning Agent folder (e.g. /memories/) on long-term memory, so files the agent writes there survive the conversation. The Research brief template does this.

The RAG Q&A template answers questions from the knowledge space: fill it first with a Remember step or from the Memory page.

docs.title: The Memory page
docs.text: Memory in the top bar lists what has been remembered, per space and owner (for example memories/user/usr_dev). Pick a namespace to see its items, search within it, delete single items, or erase the whole namespace (for example everything one end user asked you to forget).

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Long-term memories are kept until deleted, unless the server sets AGENTCANVAS_MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS, in which case memories not updated for that long are removed by the daily retention job.

docs.title: Models and API keys
docs.text: AgentCanvas works with any major model provider and with models running on your own computer. You choose a default model once on the first-run screen, and any AI model block on the canvas can use a different one.

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text:
A model is written provider:model. Type it in a AI model block's Model field (suggestions are listed), or pick it on the Model screen.

Provider Example model id API key (project secret or server variable) Anthropic anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY OpenAI openai:gpt-5.5 OPENAI_API_KEY Azure OpenAI azure_openai:<deployment> AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY (plus endpoint and API version) Google Gemini google_genai:gemini-2.5-flash GOOGLE_API_KEY Mistral AI mistralai:mistral-large-latest MISTRAL_API_KEY Groq groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile GROQ_API_KEY DeepSeek deepseek:deepseek-chat DEEPSEEK_API_KEY xAI xai:grok-4 XAI_API_KEY Any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks, a gateway…) openai_compatible:<model> OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY, or a secret you pick; a Base URL is required

docs.title: Models on your computer
docs.text:
Server Example model id Default address Ollama ollama:llama3.3, ollama:qwen3, ollama:gpt-oss:20b http://localhost:11434 LM Studio lmstudio:<model loaded in LM Studio> http://localhost:1234/v1 vLLM vllm:<served model name> http://localhost:8000/v1 llama.cpp server llamacpp:<model> http://localhost:8080/v1

Local models need no key. Set Base URL only when the server is not on its default address (the vLLM default port 8000 is also the AgentCanvas API's in development, so run vLLM on another port and set the Base URL). Start the server and load or pull the model before running a workflow. Local models vary in how well they call tools and produce structured output: if an agent misbehaves, try a larger model.

When AgentCanvas runs in Docker, localhost is the container itself: local servers are reached through host.docker.internal automatically (AGENTCANVAS_LOCAL_MODELS_HOST).

Any other provider LangChain's init_chat_model supports can be used by its prefix too (for example bedrock_converse:), once its integration package is installed on the server; the editor then warns that the model is not in the catalog (W010).

docs.title: Where a model's API key comes from
docs.text:
For each AI model block, the first of these that exists is used:

  1. The API key (secret reference) field of that AI model block: pick any project secret by name.
  2. The project secret named after the provider, for example OPENAI_API_KEY. The first-run screen saves the key you enter under this name; you can also add it on the Workspace page under Secrets.
  3. The server's environment variable of the same name (set when the server was started).

So one key entered on the first-run screen serves every model of that provider in the project, and a single model can still use another key (a second account, a customer's key) through its own secret reference.

Keys are stored encrypted, never shown again, and masked as *** in run events and traces. Exported projects read them from environment variables with the same names (listed in the export's .env.example).

docs.title: The first-run screen
docs.text:
Open it from Choose a model on Home (until setup is done) or Model in the top bar.

  1. Pick a provider and a model.
  2. Enter the API key, or the server address for a local server on a non-default port.
  3. Test connection sends one short message with exactly these settings and shows the reply or the error. Nothing is saved yet.
  4. Save stores the key as a project secret and the model as the project's default model. Workflows you create from templates afterwards use it instead of the template's own models (their other settings, such as temperature, are kept). Existing workflows don't change.

Skip for now hides the prompt; templates then keep their own models.

docs.title: Checks in the editor
docs.text:
Code Meaning W010 The model is not in the catalog, so its tool calling and structured-output support are not checked. It still runs. W011 The provider's integration is not installed on this server. Install the package named in the message. E017 An OpenAI-compatible model has no Base URL.

Under the Model field, a hint names the provider, where its key comes from, and its default address.

docs.title: LLM judges and simulated users
docs.text: Evaluators that use a model (LLM judge, pairwise judge) and simulated users accept any catalog model or any provider:model of a known provider, local ones included, so you can evaluate with a model on your own machine. They use the project's keys the same way.

docs.title: Publish and integrate
docs.text: Everything about shipping lives on the editor's Tests and Versions tabs.

docs.title: Tests before you ship
docs.text:
• After a run, Save as test case (Run tab) stores the input and the expected final status, route and output.
  • The Tests tab lists the cases and runs them all with ▶ Run tests, against the draft or a version.
  • Record as test turns a recorded run, including a production run, into a regression test that replays the recorded model and tool answers, so it is deterministic and needs no network.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
Save version freezes the workflow together with its workspace commit as a semantic version (1.0.0, …). Pick two versions to see a field-level diff drawn on the canvas, and Restore an old one into the draft.

The Contract panel shows the workflow's API: input and output fields and where it may pause. Publishing reports breaking contract changes (a removed input, a changed type) against the version currently live.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: ⬇ Export to run in your own environment… downloads a project you deploy yourself (your computer, a Linux server, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, AWS or Azure), with a service that answers the same API as a deployment and guides written for the workflow. See Export and deploy.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
Publish (or Publish to prod) creates a deployment: one per environment (prod, staging, dev, …), always pinned to a version. Editing the draft never changes what callers get until you publish again.

Publishing first runs a checklist, and refuses on a failure:

Check Passes when validation the workflow has no errors policies every organisation policy holds secrets every {"$secret": …} reference exists tests the saved test cases pass contract no breaking change against the live version (or it is the first publish) release gate the evaluation meets the environment's gate, if one is set

The deployment's API key is shown once, when the deployment is created. Store it safely. Rotate key issues a new one; Unpublish removes the deployment.

docs.title: Call a deployment
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/deployments/<deployment id>/runs/wait \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <api key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}}'

The answer:

{"run_id": "run_…", "thread_id": "th_…", "status": "success",
 "output": {"messages": [ … ]}, "interrupts": [], "error": null}
Endpoint Use POST /v1/deployments/{id}/runs/wait Run and wait for the result. POST /v1/deployments/{id}/runs/stream Run and receive Server-Sent Events as it goes. POST /v1/deployments/{id}/threads/{thread_id}/resume Answer a pause: body {"value": true} (and interrupt_id when several are open). POST /v1/deployments/{id}/runs/{run_id}/feedback Send {"rating": "up" \| "down", "comment": "…"}.

Request fields: input (the workflow's input channels), thread_id (continue a conversation), context, and user_id (your end user, used for per-user memory). When status is interrupted, interrupts says what the run is waiting for.

Through the web server (production setups) the same paths are under /api/. The public API is rate-limited per key, per webhook and per project (429 with Retry-After when exceeded). Full, interactive API reference: http://localhost:8000/docs in development.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
On the Versions tab:

  • + Webhook creates a URL (POST /v1/hooks/{trigger_id}) that starts a run. Without a mapping the request body is the input; a mapping builds the input from templates over the body, e.g. {"ticket": "{{ body.issue.title }}"}. Senders sign each request: header X-AgentCanvas-Timestamp: <unix seconds> and X-AgentCanvas-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>." + body> using the trigger's secret. Requests older than five minutes are refused.
  • + Cron runs the workflow on a 5-field schedule in UTC (e.g. */5 9-17 * * 1-5) with a fixed Cron input (JSON). Each scheduled minute fires once, however many API replicas run.

A trigger runs its deployment's pinned version when it is attached to one, otherwise the draft (the panel says which). For starting workflows from your own domain events, see Events.

docs.title: Run a workflow
docs.text:
Open the Run tab (or click ▶ Test in the toolbar).

  • JSON mode: edit the input (pre-filled with the workflow's input channels) and click ▶ Run.
  • Chat mode: for workflows built around the messages channel. Type a message and Send; each message continues the same conversation (thread).
  • continue thread: tick it to run on the previous thread, keeping its state, instead of starting fresh.
  • Dry run (stub risky tools): every tool that can write, send, execute or spend is replaced by a recorder, so the run has no side effects. The output shows what would have been called.

While a run streams, each card shows its status (running, done, interrupted, failed) and, when finished, its tokens and time. The Run tab shows streamed output, the run's totals (tokens, latency, cost when the model has catalog prices), and the final state as JSON.

docs.title: Human decisions
docs.text:
When a run reaches an Ask for approval or Ask a person step, or an agent tool call that needs approval, it pauses and the Run tab shows Approval needed with the value under review.

  • Approve or Reject. Approvals can also edit the value before approving.
  • Paused runs are durable: you can close the browser or restart the server and resume later.
  • The Inbox (top bar) lists every pending decision across all workflows you can see, so reviewers don't need to open the editor. Reviewers (and above) can answer.

docs.title: Breakpoints
docs.text: Select a step and click ○ Add breakpoint in the Inspector. A run pauses before that step (Paused at a breakpoint before …); inspect the state, then ⏵ Continue.

docs.title: Timeline: time travel and fork
docs.text: The Timeline tab in the bottom dock lists every checkpoint of the run's thread. Select one to see the state at that moment, including lineage (which step or input last wrote each channel). Edit the state and click ⑂ Fork from here to re-run from that point with the change, without touching the original run. This is the quickest way to try "what if the classifier had said high?".

docs.title: Explain
docs.text: The Explain tab narrates the run in plain language: which step ran, what each router chose and why (chose route 'normal' → reply_drafter), where it paused. Useful for sharing what happened with someone who doesn't read JSON.

docs.title: Pins and mocks
docs.text:
• 📌 Pin last output: after a run, select a step and pin its last output. Debug runs then skip that step and replay the pinned output: handy for iterating on a later step without re-running an expensive one. Unpin to undo.
  • Mock replies: select a AI model block and enter Mock replies for debug runs. Debug runs use those replies instead of calling the model.

Pins and mocks only affect runs started from the editor, never published deployments.

docs.title: Cost and budgets
docs.text: Each step shows tokens and latency; the run panel shows totals. Set a budget to stop runs that exceed tokens, cost or time.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: With LANGSMITH_TRACING=true and a LANGSMITH_API_KEY on the server, each run gets an Open trace in LangSmith link. With OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set, the server also exports OpenTelemetry traces. Secret values are masked as ***; list fields in the workflow's trace_redact setting to keep their values out of traces entirely.

docs.title: Save a run as a test
docs.text: After a run, Save as test case in the Run tab records the input and the expected status, route and output. The Tests tab runs all saved cases (▶ Run tests) against the draft or any version. Record as test turns a recorded run (including a production run) into a deterministic regression test that replays the model and tool answers instead of calling them. See Publish and integrate.

docs.title: Run AgentCanvas on your computer
docs.text:
This guide takes you from a fresh machine to a working AgentCanvas in your browser, then checks that it works. There are two ways to run it:

  • Docker (quickest): one command runs the whole app; a first-run screen asks which model to use. Only Docker is needed. See Run everything in Docker.
  • From source (for development): the API and the web app run as dev servers with live reload. It needs no API keys at first: it uses built-in demo models. Steps 1 to 10 below.

docs.title: Run everything in Docker
docs.text:
You need Docker Desktop (Windows, macOS) or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin (Linux), and Git.

git clone https://github.com/marunsct/AgentCanvas.git
cd AgentCanvas
make docker-up        # or: docker compose -f infra/compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait

This one command starts everything the app needs, each in its own container: Postgres 16 with pgvector (your workflows, runs and keys, kept in a Docker volume), the API (it applies the database migrations itself on start) and the web app. Nothing else needs installing or running: no Python, Node or separate database. Redis is not used.

The first build takes a few minutes. Then open http://localhost:7777: Home shows Set up your model.

  1. Click Choose a model.
  2. Pick a provider: hosted (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API such as OpenRouter or Together) or on your machine (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp).
  3. Pick or type the model (suggestions are listed for each provider).
  4. Hosted providers: paste your API key. It is stored encrypted as a project secret and never shown again. Local servers: leave Server address empty to use the default port on your computer.
  5. Click Test connection: AgentCanvas sends one short message and shows the reply, or the error.
  6. Click Save. Templates you open from now on use this model. You can change it any time from Model in the top bar, and pick a different model on any AI model block on the canvas.

Models on your own computer are reached from inside Docker through host.docker.internal, so start Ollama (ollama serve, then ollama pull llama3.3) or LM Studio's local server before testing.

Command Does make docker-up build and start (again) make docker-logs follow the logs make docker-down stop; your workflows and keys stay in Docker volumes docker compose -f infra/compose.local.yml down -v stop and delete all data

Optional settings (another port with WEB_PORT, server-wide provider keys) go in infra/.env.local: copy infra/.env.local.example and fill it in; make docker-up picks it up. The Docker setup has no sign-in (you are the local admin): don't expose it to other people. For a shared server follow Deploy and operate.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
Verified

The from-source steps were run on a clean checkout on 2026-10-06: make setup, make dev-fake, make dev-web, the smoke test in step 6, a publish + API call, and the first-run model screen. The Docker stack is started and checked (first-run setup included) by CI on every change.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: What Where Web app http://localhost:5173 API http://localhost:8000 (health: /healthz, interactive API docs: /docs) Data apps/api/agentcanvas.db (SQLite) and apps/api/workspaces/ (one git repo per project) Sign-in none: in local mode every request is the built-in admin dev@localhost

docs.title: 1. Install the prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Version Why Check Git any recent clone the repo; project workspaces are git repositories git --version uv 0.8 or newer Python packages; it also downloads Python 3.12 if you don't have it uv --version Node.js 22 the web app node -v pnpm 10 web packages pnpm -v make any the shortcuts below (optional: every target is a plain command you can type) make -v Docker Desktop recent optional: only for Postgres (step 8) docker version

Install commands:

macOSLinuxWindows 
brew install git node@22 make
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate

# Node 22 from your package manager or https://nodejs.org, then:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate

Use WSL 2 (Ubuntu) and follow the Linux steps inside it: the Makefile and scripts assume a Unix shell. If you prefer native PowerShell, install uv with powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex", Node 22 from nodejs.org, then corepack enable; corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate, and type the commands shown under each make target instead of make.

Open a new terminal after installing so the tools are on your PATH.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/marunsct/AgentCanvas.git
cd AgentCanvas

docs.title: 3. Install dependencies
docs.text:
make setup

This runs cd apps/api && uv sync (Python packages into apps/api/.venv) and cd apps/web && pnpm install. The first run downloads a few hundred MB and can take a few minutes.

docs.title: 4. Start the API (terminal 1)
docs.text:
make dev-fake

Same as cd apps/api && uv run uvicorn agentcanvas.dev.fake_server:app --reload --port 8000.

On first start the API creates the SQLite database, runs migrations and seeds a default organisation, project and admin user. You should see:

INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000
... api.started  auth=dev database=sqlite edition=dev env=dev
INFO:     Application startup complete.

Check it from another terminal: curl http://localhost:8000/healthz answers {"status":"ok"}.

Demo models

dev-fake answers every model call with a scripted demo model, so nothing leaves your machine and nothing costs money. Tools, scripts, approvals, memory and the database are all real.

docs.title: 5. Start the web app (terminal 2)
docs.text:
make dev-web

Same as cd apps/web && pnpm dev. Open http://localhost:5173. The web dev server forwards /api/* to the API on port 8000, so no extra configuration is needed.

You land on Home: a Start the guided build button, a New workflow box, eight template cards and your workflow list. The top bar shows you · admin.

docs.title: 6. Smoke test (two minutes)
docs.text:
1. On Home, click the Support triage (demo tools) card. The editor opens with five steps on the canvas.
  2. In the right-hand panel, open the Run tab.
  3. Replace the input with {"ticket": "Where is my invoice?"} and click ▶ Run.
  4. The steps light up in turn. Reply drafter stops with an Approval needed box for the send_reply tool.
  5. Click Approve.
  6. Streamed output shows reply_drafter Done — the tool call finished (demo model). and the Output shows the tool's answer sent: demo. Every step shows a green done badge.

If you got this far, the API, the web app, the database and durable runs all work. Optional extra checks:

  • Inbox: run again, don't approve, and open Inbox in the top bar: the pending approval is there too.
  • Chat: open the Chat assistant template, switch the Run tab to Chat, and send a message.
  • Publish and call it over HTTP: see Publish and integrate.
  • Tests: make test runs the backend and web test suites (several minutes).

docs.title: 7. Use real models
docs.text:
Stop the API (Ctrl+C in terminal 1) and start it with real models:

make dev-api      # same as dev-fake, but calls the models you choose

make dev-api runs cd apps/api && uv run uvicorn agentcanvas.api.main:app --reload --port 8000. Then, in the web app, click Model in the top bar (or Choose a model on Home) and pick any provider, hosted or local, with its API key: the same first-run screen as in Docker. Every supported provider's integration is installed by make setup.

You can also give keys to the whole server instead: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY or XAI_API_KEY in the shell that starts make dev-api. See Models and API keys for every provider and how keys are chosen.

Optional: LANGSMITH_TRACING=true and LANGSMITH_API_KEY=... add an Open trace link to each run.

docs.title: 8. Optional: Postgres instead of SQLite
docs.text:
SQLite is enough for trying the product. To run against Postgres (what production uses, with pgvector for semantic memory search):

docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://agentcanvas:agentcanvas@localhost:5432/agentcanvas make dev-fake   # or dev-api

Migrations run automatically at startup. make infra also starts Redis, which the API does not need today.

docs.title: 9. Optional: the production-style container setup
docs.text: To run what production runs (two API replicas behind nginx, sign-in through an identity provider), follow Deploy and operate. For trying AgentCanvas on one computer, Run everything in Docker is simpler.

docs.title: 10. Optional: try sign-in, roles and invitations
docs.text:
Local mode makes you an admin with no sign-in. To try real sign-in with Keycloak on your machine:

  1. docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml --profile auth up -d keycloak and open http://localhost:8080 (admin / admin).
  2. Create a realm (e.g. agentcanvas) and a user with an email address, marked Email verified.
  3. Create a client agentcanvas-web: OpenID Connect, Client authentication off (public), Standard flow on, valid redirect URI http://localhost:5173/auth/callback, web origin http://localhost:5173.
  4. Make the access token carry the audience agentcanvas-api: on the client's dedicated scope add an Audience mapper with included custom audience agentcanvas-api.

  5. Start the API with:

    AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE=oidc \
AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:8080/realms/agentcanvas \
AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_AUDIENCE=agentcanvas-api \
AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=agentcanvas-web \
AGENTCANVAS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAILS='["you@example.com"]' \
make dev-fake

The web app now redirects to Keycloak; the bootstrap email becomes an admin on first sign-in and can invite others from Members.

docs.title: Stop, reset and update
docs.text:
• Stop: Ctrl+C in both terminals.
  • Reset to a clean slate: stop the API, then rm apps/api/agentcanvas.db && rm -rf apps/api/workspaces.
  • Update: git pull && make setup, then restart both servers. Migrations run at startup.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Fix make: command not found (Windows) Use WSL 2, or type the command each make target runs (shown above). uv: command not found after installing Open a new terminal, or add ~/.local/bin to PATH. pnpm: command not found corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate, or npm i -g pnpm@10. address already in use on 8000 or 5173 Another process holds the port: stop it (lsof -i :8000 on macOS/Linux) or stop an old server. The web app shows an error on every page The API is not running or not on port 8000. Check curl localhost:8000/healthz. A run fails with an authentication error from the provider The key is missing or wrong: enter it again under Model, or check the project secret named after the provider on the Workspace page. Test connection to Ollama / LM Studio fails with a connection error The local server is not running, or listens on another port: start it, or enter its address under Server address. In Docker, the address must use host.docker.internal, not localhost. A model shows integration is not installed on this server Run make setup again (it installs every provider), or docker compose … up --build. make docker-up fails with port is already allocated Something else uses 7777: set WEB_PORT=7778 in infra/.env.local. git errors when the API starts or saves a workspace file Install Git and make sure it is on PATH. Startup says AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE=dev gives every request admin rights You set AGENTCANVAS_ENV to staging/prod; use dev locally or configure OIDC. Startup says oidc needs AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_ISSUER and AGENTCANVAS_OIDC_AUDIENCE Set both, or leave AGENTCANVAS_AUTH_MODE unset for local mode. Something is odd after many experiments Reset (above) and restart.

More developer detail is in the build guide and its troubleshooting FAQ.

docs.title: Block reference
docs.text:
Blocks (also called widgets) are the building pieces in the palette on the left. Steps (solid outline) run one after another along the grey arrows. Add-ons (dashed outline, such as an AI model or a tool) do not run on their own: they plug into a step's coloured inputs.

New to all this? Start with the Beginner's guide. On the canvas you can hover any dot on a block to see what it is for, and click it to see everything that can connect there.

The names below are what you see in the palette. The internal type id (for example core.llm) is shown in brackets; it is what the saved workflow and the generated code use, and it never changes.

docs.title: AI
docs.text: Block What it does Ask AI (core.llm) Sends your instructions (the prompt) to an AI model and saves its reply in a data field. Insert data with {{ state.<field> }}. Needs an AI model plugged into model. AI Agent (core.agent) An AI that can use tools on its own, step by step, until the task is done (LangChain create_agent). It reads and writes the conversation (the messages field). Plug an AI model into model, tools into tools and add-ons into middleware. Settings: instructions (system prompt), Tools that need approval (a person approves, edits or rejects each call), and structured output: design a response schema with + Field and the final answer is validated and written to structured_response. Planning Agent (agent.deep) A stronger agent for big, multi-step jobs: it writes a plan, keeps notes in files and can hand work to helper agents (create_deep_agent). Helper Agent (add-on, agent.subagent) A specialist a Planning Agent can hand a task to with its task tool. Fill in When to use it.

docs.title: AI models
docs.text: Block What it does AI model (add-on, model.chat) The AI “brain” as provider:model from any provider, hosted or local: anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5, openai:gpt-5.5, google_genai:gemini-2.5-flash, ollama:llama3.3, lmstudio:<model>… A new AI model block starts as your project's default model from first-run setup. A hint under the field says where its key comes from. Optional temperature, max output tokens, timeout, Base URL, and API key: pick a project secret by name, or leave it empty to use the secret named after the provider. One model can power several steps. See Models and API keys.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Block What it does Web API tool (add-on, tool.http) Lets an agent call a web service (an HTTP API). The URL is a template over the tool's inputs, e.g. https://api.example.com/orders/{{ args.order_id }}. Private and local addresses are refused unless the tool allows private networks. App connector (MCP) (add-on, mcp.server) All tools of a Model Context Protocol server. Browse tools lists them and flags which ones change things, so you can pick and gate them. Python tool (add-on, tool.python) A LangChain @tool function from the workspace's tools/ folder. Memory tools (add-on, tool.memory) Gives an agent search_memory and save_memory tools for one memory space.

docs.title: People
docs.text: Block What it does Ask for approval (core.approval) Pauses until a person approves or rejects, optionally editing the value shown. The decision (true/false) goes to a data field. Ask a person (core.human_input) Pauses and asks a person a question (a form when a response schema is set); the answer goes to a data field.

docs.title: Flow control
docs.text: Block What it does Choose a path (core.router) Sends the run down different paths: the first rule whose condition is true wins (a CEL expression such as state.priority == "high"), otherwise the default path. Each path is an output dot. Repeat for each item (core.map) Runs the step connected to each once per list item, in parallel. Results must go to an append (list) field. Wait for all (core.join) Waits until every incoming branch has finished, then continues. Group of steps (core.subgraph) A small workflow with its own data, run as one step. Double-click it to look inside.

docs.title: Data and code
docs.text: Block What it does Set values (core.set) Writes templated values into data fields, e.g. summary = "Ticket: {{ state.ticket }}". Run Python code (core.script) Runs def run(state) -> dict from a file in the workspace's scripts/ folder; return the fields to update. Workspace scripts and custom blocks Files in the workspace appear in the palette under Workspace. See Workspace.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Block What it does Look up memory (core.memory_recall) Searches long-term memory and writes the matches to a data field. Save to memory (core.memory_remember) Saves a field's value in long-term memory under a key. Forget memory (core.memory_forget) Deletes one memory by key. Saved files folder (add-on, backend.store) Mounts a Planning Agent folder (e.g. /memories/) on long-term memory. Scratch files (add-on, backend.state) Planning Agent files kept with the conversation: they live and die with it.

See Memory for spaces and sharing.

docs.title: Agent add-ons
docs.text:
Add-ons (middleware) change how an agent's model and tool calls behave. Plug one or more into an agent's middleware input; the order of the lines is the order they apply.

Block What it does Protect personal data (mw.pii) Finds personal data in messages and blocks, redacts, masks or hashes it. Limit AI calls / Limit tool use (mw.model_call_limit, mw.tool_call_limit) Stop the agent after N model or tool calls per run or conversation. Retry AI calls / Retry tools (mw.model_retry, mw.tool_retry) Retry failed calls, waiting a little longer each time. Backup models (mw.model_fallback) Try the connected models in order when the main model fails. Shorten long chats (mw.summarization) Summarise old messages when the conversation grows too long. To-do list (mw.todo) Give the agent a write_todos tool to plan multi-step work. Pick tools first (mw.tool_selector) Let a cheaper model pick the relevant tools before each call. Quality check (mw.rubric) Before answering, a grader model checks the work against your checklist and sends it back with what is missing, up to a set number of rounds. Each round shows live in the Run panel.

docs.title: Workspace: code, secrets and events
docs.text:
Each project has a workspace: a git repository of Python code used by its workflows. Open it from the Workspace link in the top bar.

Folder What goes there Appears as scripts/ Script functions def run(state: dict) -> dict (sync or async) Workspace scripts in the palette; use with the Run Python code block tools/ LangChain @tool functions Python tool resources for agents nodes/ Custom widgets declared with @canvas_node(...) New widgets in the palette, in the category you choose events/ Event handlers declared with @on("type"); JSON schemas in events/schemas/ The Events page

Click a file to edit it (with lint markers), New file to add one. Every save is a git commit, and a workflow version pins the workspace commit it was made with.

docs.title: Each workflow's own code, and shared code
docs.text:
Open the Workspace from a workflow (the Workspace button in the editor, or Open … in the Workspace on a Script block) and you see two groups:

  • This workflow's code lives in flows/<workflow>/ with its own scripts/, tools/ and nodes/. A Script block's + Create the code file puts the file there, and its import path starts with flows.<workflow>.. Other workflows do not see it in their palette.
  • Shared code is everything in the folders at the root (scripts/, tools/, nodes/, events/). Every workflow in the project can use it, and event handlers always live here.

Code can import other workspace code the usual Python way, for example from scripts.textutil import shout or from .helpers import clean, and it works the same on the canvas, in the sandbox and in an export.

← Back to workflow at the top (or the browser's Back button) returns you to the canvas with the same zoom, position and selected block. The Workspace opened from the home page shows every file in the project.

The + Script step, + Tool for the AI and + Custom block buttons start a new file with working starter code for that kind of file.

docs.title: Copilot help with code
docs.text:
Below the editor of a Python file, the ✦ Copilot box helps you write it:

  • Write with Copilot: describe what the code should do (select lines in the editor to focus on them).
  • Explain: what the file, or the selected lines, does, step by step.
  • Fix N problems: fixes the problems the linter reports, changing as little as possible.

The Copilot answers with an explanation and, when it changes code, a diff. Accept changes puts the new code in the editor as an ordinary, undoable edit; nothing is saved until you press Save. It uses the Copilot's model and privacy settings (see Copilot). Viewers can use Explain only.

docs.title: A script
docs.text:
# scripts/clean.py
def run(state: dict) -> dict:
    text = str(state.get("text") or "")
    return {"text": text.strip()}   # return only the channels you want to update

docs.title: A tool
docs.text:
# tools/orders.py
from langchain_core.tools import tool

@tool
def order_status(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Look up the status of an order."""
    return "shipped"

docs.title: A custom widget
docs.text:
# nodes/crm.py
from agentcanvas.sdk import canvas_node

@canvas_node(name="acme.score_lead", label="Score lead", category="CRM", writes=["score"])
def score_lead(state: dict, cfg: dict) -> dict:
    return {"score": 0.8}

config can be a Pydantic model or a JSON Schema; its fields become the widget's settings form. Declare side_effects so the blast radius and policies know what it does.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Store API keys and passwords on the Workspace page under Secrets (Save secret). Names are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Secrets are encrypted at rest, can't be read back through the API, and are masked as *** in run events and traces.

  • In widget settings: {"$secret": "NAME"}, e.g. an HTTP tool's header. A AI model block's API key field lets you pick a secret by name; a secret named after the provider (OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY…) is used by that provider's models automatically. See Models and API keys.
  • In scripts and custom widgets: from agentcanvas.sdk import secret then secret("NAME").

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: Workspace code runs where the server is configured to run it (AGENTCANVAS_SCRIPT_EXECUTION): in the API process (local default), a child process (production default), a Docker container, or a LangSmith Sandbox (experimental). Sandbox policy edits sandbox.json: time and memory limits, an outbound network allow-list, and headers injected into outgoing requests (so code can call an API without seeing its key).

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Events start or resume workflows when something happens elsewhere ("a lead was created", "a payment failed").

# events/leads.py
from agentcanvas.sdk import on

@on("crm.lead.created", filter="event.data.amount > 50000", dedup_key="event.data.lead_id")
def qualify(event, act):
    act.start_workflow("Lead qualification", input={"lead": event.data})

Handlers only describe actions (act.start_workflow, act.resume, act.emit); the platform performs them, so handler code never holds credentials. Steps can emit events during a run with agentcanvas.sdk.emit(type, data).

The Events page shows the event map (which events start or resume which workflows), lets you Send a test event (or Dry run it to see what would happen), and keeps an event log. Other systems send events with POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/events.
